180 Total content (elapsed 3h15 with the break). Protected measurement time: 12 minutes (6.7%)

The Leaders' Session — 45 minutes, before the team session

45 minutes with managers and the chief executive. For a five-person business, a one-to-one with the owner. This is not a briefing. The leader does the same work the team will do, first. The evidence direction the offerings draft relies on is about managers being trained, not informed — so a session in which the leader is told what the team will learn produces none of the effect being claimed for it.

# Outcome Why it matters Taught Activity Evidence Claim boundary
L1 Chooses one recurring moment of their own, writes it down, and completes one full pass on it in the session If the person at the top has not done it, the team session does not transfer — it produces dissonance. This is the whole reason the session exists Compressed E2/E3/E4: the gap, the three steps, the state read 18 min (8 teach, 10 choose + full pass) L-01 (NEW, end) — the moment, free text. L-04 (NEW, 3 weeks) — F-01/F-02 mirrored: how many times did it come up, in how many did you run the steps Licenses: "leaders complete the practice themselves before their teams do." Not: that leadership behaviour changed
L2 States one sentence they will say out loud to their team, and where and when they will say it Norms shift when network-central people visibly adopt something. A leader who practises privately produces no visible signal at all. This converts an attitude into an observable act That the visible act is the mechanism, not the private practice; two worked example sentences (naming their own moment; asking someone how theirs went) 7 min — write the sentence and the meeting it happens at L-02 (NEW, end) — the sentence and the occasion. L-03 (NEW, 3 weeks) — "Did you say it? (yes / no / partly) What happened?" Licenses: "X of Y leaders reported saying it." Not: that norms changed, or that the team noticed
L3 Names one enabling condition inside their control and commits to changing it Leaders hold the conditions participants can only ask for. This is the receiver for every Foundations F3 request The control test; that an enabling condition is a change to what is available, not an instruction to the team 7 min Folded into L-03's free text; no dedicated item — a disclosed gap Licenses nothing about the organisation. A stated commitment is a stated commitment
L4 States back, unprompted, the two things they will not do The leader is the single person who could most easily turn this into surveillance or a performance measure. Left unsaid, "did you do your reps?" is the most likely failure mode of the whole product (1) Never ask to see anyone's moment — Radar content is private, always; (2) never treat non-practice as a performance issue, in a review, a one-to-one or a joke 3 min — the facilitator asks the leader to say both back, out loud, in their own words No item. Verified in the room by the facilitator only — a real gap, and the highest-consequence one in this document Licenses nothing. It is a prohibition, not an outcome to report
L5 Names the route for a problem that is structural, not a practice problem Without it, the leaders' session is a mechanism for converting a workload problem into a skill deficit — the exact misuse K-07 prohibits The named internal route for that organisation, agreed with the host before the session 3 min (inside L3's block) No item Licenses nothing

Leaders' Session clock, 45 minutes: 0:00–0:03 scope and what this is not · 0:03–0:08 why you, and why first · 0:08–0:16 the gap, the three steps, the state read · 0:16–0:26 your moment, and one full pass · 0:26–0:33 the sentence you will say, and where · 0:33–0:40 enabling conditions and the hazard route · 0:40–0:43 the two prohibitions, said back · 0:43–0:45 leaders' form, four items.

Measurement constraint on the leaders' form, which matters more than it looks. Leaders' responses must never be linked to their team's responses, at any point, for any reason. And the reporting floors already fixed in the instrument (nothing reported on a group under 20, no subgroup under 10) mean a single organisation's leaders can never be reported at all — often a group of one to three. Leaders' data is poolable across organisations and nowhere else. If that is not designed in before the first session, the first interesting finding will be un-reportable, or reported wrongly.

1 · What is in Foundations that is not in Essentials, and why

In Foundations only Extra time Why 90 minutes genuinely cannot produce it
F1 — peer application 21 min (+14 min self-elicitation, which is what makes the room safe enough for it) Needs two turns and a debrief. A one-turn version rehearses half the skill and leaves the other half practised by nobody. The room also has to be safe before people take each other through anything, and that safety is built by the self-elicitation opener Essentials cuts
F2 — matched shift move +19 min net (the 6-minute Essentials menu becomes a 10-minute live toolkit, plus a 15-minute contrast) Essentials can produce a named move. It cannot produce a felt contrast, and without one the matching is guesswork dressed as judgement
F3 — enabling condition and the named ask 23 min (8 diagnostic + 15 write and route) Needs the diagnostic lens before the write, and the hazard-routing safeguard is not optional. Compressed, it becomes a slogan about environment with no person and no route — worse than not raising it
F4 — the five skills, given a job 6 min Conditional. Included only if the five skills are taught at all in the standalone session (see the conflict below)

The 90 extra minutes, reconciled: F1 35 + F2 19 + F3 23 + F4 6 = 83, plus 7 minutes given to beats that are simply longer with the room available (the moment 12 not 10, the full pass 10 not 8, cue and close 7 not 4) = 90. Every minute of the difference between the two formats is attached to a named outcome or to a beat that already exists in both.

Everything else in Foundations is Essentials, unchanged. The two formats teach the same procedure, the same cue and the same countable unit — which is exactly what the offerings draft already promises buyers ("the teaching does not change... what changes is how far we go"). This document makes that claim true, where the existing 3-hour and 1-hour builds made it approximately true.

2 · What was cut, and why

Cut From Why
The six-component Human Operating System Both. Foundations keeps only the diagnostic question and Environment No outcome depends on the six components, and the existing guide already tells participants they are not expected to memorise them. Eleven minutes for something nobody is asked to retain. What survives is the part that does a job: the lens F3 needs
The five public skills Essentials entirely; Foundations only if F4 stands Named once as vocabulary, never used again — the outcomes checklist's own finding. Naming five things a participant will never be asked to do anything with costs 5–6 minutes and produces recognition at best
Three Radar moments → one Both The ratio measure needs one countable cue with an unambiguous denominator. Three moments make F-01 unanswerable — which moment came up? Three was always MFC's own design choice, never an evidence-validated number (D-0010), and the 1-hour build already reduced it to one
The Radar's second strand ("experience more fully") Cut from the counted spine in both; offered as an optional extra private line, explicitly not measured It is uncountable by design, and forcing it into an opportunity-conditional measure would either corrupt the denominator or invite a claim MFC cannot support. Cutting it entirely would reframe mental fitness as damage control and contradict the proactive category claim — so it is offered and named, not counted
My moments / Our moments as taught structure Both. Replaced by F3's enabling condition and named ask A candidate Our moment drafted in a room still requires an agreement conversation outside it, and nothing in the offer supports or follows up that step (D-0090 §2). The workshop produced an intention and stopped. F3 produces a named person, a sentence and a follow-up item — which is the same intention, made checkable
Pair-share on the wall themes (4 min) Both The explain-back at E2 does the same job — a low-stakes first speaking turn — and serves an outcome while doing it
The worked example between the Radar halves (3 min) Both There are no longer two Radar halves. The contrast activity is the worked example in Foundations; the board narrowing is in Essentials
Skill-acquisition normalisation analogy (2 min) Both Folded into E6's normalising beat, which does the same work with a moment from the room rather than an analogy about learning guitar
System basics / Engine Basics signpost (1 min) Both Not on the outcome spine, and its own record positions it as named and referenced, never expanded. It is a line in the take-home card, not a beat
"Two things this doesn't mean" caveat pair Both Insurance, not teaching, on a distinction the room has already produced itself
ST-2 — intent to use The instrument Intent is a weak predictor of behaviour and no outcome depends on it. With F-01/F-02/F-03 now measuring actual opportunity-conditional use, an intent item at post buys nothing and costs burden
ST-1 / ST-3 as separate items The instrument Superseded by P-05 and F-07, which are the same items with better wording, already in the current draft
Form 3 Q8 — "approximately how many Mental Reps" The instrument Already ruled out by Hunter directly ("Agreed — don't count reps!"). Not yet actioned in the live advisor draft; that edit still has to go through Eimear and Debra

The general rule applied. A beat survives if an outcome depends on it. Nine beats did not, and they cost roughly 30 minutes across the two formats — which is where E2, E7, F1 and F3 came from. Essentials is 30 minutes longer than the 1-hour build and delivers more, because it stopped paying for a tour.

3 · Outcomes with no item; items with no outcome

Outcomes with no measurement item — defects, in order of consequence

# Outcome Status Proposed
1 E7 — completing a full pass in the room The session's central activity, entirely unmeasured. Every claim about what the room produces currently rests on facilitator impression P-09, using F-02/F-03's exact wording so the in-room and three-week passes sit on one scale
2 E1's countability — whether the chosen moment is frequent enough to practise Unmeasured. A participant who chooses an annual event is invisible until F-01 returns zero at three weeks, by which point nothing can be done P-10 — expected weekly frequency, at post
3 L4 — the two prohibitions No item, and the highest-consequence gap here: it is the control against the product becoming surveillance. Currently verified by facilitator memory alone Facilitator sign-off on the delivery record is the minimum. A leader-facing item would be self-serving and is not proposed
4 F1 — peer application No item P-12 (post), F-11 (3 weeks)
5 F3 — the named ask No item F-12 (3 weeks)
6 F2 — matched, not just named P-05 cannot distinguish a named tool from a matched one P-05b — "why that one, for that moment?"
7 F4 — the five skills No item P-11, conditional on F4 surviving
8 Anything organisational or cultural Not a defect — a scoped exclusion. Every item in every form is individual first-person self-report, by design; organisational measurement is deliberately reserved to a separate pack that does not exist yet Nothing. F-12 is the closest honest approach and it is still one person reporting one act

Items with no outcome

Genuine defects — the item measures nothing the session is designed to produce:

  • B-03 (which statement best describes mental fitness) and B-05 (when is building mental fitness relevant). Concept recognition, asked at three timepoints, attached to no outcome in either format. Either an outcome exists that requires them — in which case write it and give it a beat and an activity — or they are burden. Recommendation: keep B-04 only (the mental health / mental fitness distinction, which is MFC's central positioning claim and does carry a beat), and cut B-03 and B-05 to buy back the burden P-09, P-10 and P-05b cost.
  • B-01 / F-05 (the matched ordinal: how often did you remember to use something helpful while the moment was happening) duplicates the ratio, less well. It is subject to exactly the ceiling and recall problems F-01/F-02/F-03 were built to defeat. It is not proposed for cutting — it is the only pre/post-comparable item and the then-test is built on it — but it must never be reported as a second, corroborating outcome. Two measures of one construct, one of them weaker, reported side by side, reads as two findings.

Not defects — instrumentation, and should be labelled as such in the instrument so nobody later mistakes them for outcomes: B-02 (prior reliance — market evidence), P-01 (then-test — a measurement correction, not a thing taught), P-06 (predicted retrieval — only useful paired with F-04 as a calibration check), P-07 (feasibility — tests the design's central assumption), F-06 (perceived helpfulness), F-08 and F-09 (barriers and what would help — the items that tell MFC what to build next), F-10 (the narrative item — an evidence asset carrying the real identifiability risk).

4 · Where records conflict — named, not silently resolved

  1. "Don't count reps" versus the counted ratio. 03-measurement-and-behaviour-tracking.md states rep counts and practice frequency are "deliberately not measured", and Hunter confirmed it directly: "Agreed — don't count reps!" The current forms draft's primary outcome is F-01, F-02 and F-03 — three counted numbers over a seven-day window. These cannot both be current. The reconciliation this document assumes, stated so it can be rejected: the objection was to tallying a person's practice volume as a performance measure, which the ratio does not do — it is opportunity-conditional, attempt-based rather than outcome-based, never fed back to the participant, and cannot rank anyone. But the earlier ruling was categorical and the newest instrument reintroduces counting. This is founder question 1 and no session plan should be written before it is answered, because E1, E6 and E7 are all shaped by it.
  2. Whether a standalone session teaches the five public skills. D-0091 resolves that a standalone Foundations Session collapses Stage 1 and Stage 2, so it may teach the full five skills, State Check and Shift menu. K-08's audience-translation table still reads: "Stage 1 leads with one moment, Stop Shift Do, one live rep and a Radar; the five public skills are named from Stage 2." Both are current; neither cites the other. This document cuts the five from Essentials (following K-08's row) and keeps them conditionally in Foundations (following D-0091) — a per-format split that neither record authorises. Flagged, not resolved.
  3. The formats that exist versus the formats being sold. Every built artefact is a 3-hour or 1-hour session (MFC-1H-v1, whose own guide says "there is no recoverable padding anywhere in this design"). The offerings ladder sells 90 minutes and half a day. A 90-minute session is not the 1-hour kit with 30 minutes added — the whole allocation changes, and the facilitator guides do not currently describe either product on the price list.
  4. Three Radar moments versus one. K-07 and D-0010 carry three (as an explicit design choice, not evidence); the 1-hour build names the reduction to one as a D-0014 deviation. The ratio measure requires one. This document takes one for both formats, which makes the 1-hour's named deviation the standard rather than the exception.
  5. Foundations' embedding promise versus the Leaders' Session being optional. The offerings draft promises Foundations includes "help embedding it" and prices the Leaders' Session as an add-on (free when bundled). F3 assumes a leader who has been through L1–L5 — otherwise the named ask goes to someone who has not been told what it is, and the enabling condition has no receiver. See founder question 3.

5 · Inferences — where this document is deciding, not following a record

Stated so a reader can tell the difference:

  • The 90/180 split of outcomes is an inference. No record allocates outcomes by format; the existing formats differ by content volume, not by outcome.
  • E7 (the in-room full pass) is new. The existing builds contain a live State Check, a Radar write and a cue selection, but no beat in either format has a participant run all three steps on their own moment. The audience-intelligence review found the equivalent gap for outcome 1 and it was fixed with the live State Check; the same gap for the full sequence was never caught.
  • P-09, P-10, P-11, P-12, P-05b, F-11, F-12 and L-01 to L-04 are new items written here. None has been through Eimear Quigley or Debra Fidler, none has been cognitively tested, and the forms draft's own approval path (steps 1–7) applies to all of them.
  • F3's shape — enabling condition, named person, one sentence, follow-up item — is this document's construction. It is deliberately narrower than Team Pulse, which is escalated and undecided (D-0090).
  • The claim that E6 protects the primary measure (that "even partly, even badly" only works if the room was told partly and badly count) is reasoning, not a finding from data.
  • Every burden figure is arithmetic on the forms draft's own estimates, which are themselves estimates. Nothing has been timed with real participants.

6 · What remains unresolved

  • D-0016's six safeguarding matters are open. Nothing here is deliverable to participants until they resolve; the disclosure placeholder must not go out unresolved. F-12 and F-11 in particular reach a participant alone, weeks later, and sit behind the clinical-governance gate the forms draft already names.
  • The privacy, consent and linkage protocol is the blocker, overdue since 31 July, and it gates the build and the send of everything in section 3.
  • The measurement instrument is unapproved and untested. Every item cited here is a draft, and the counted items are the ones cognitive testing should focus on.
  • K6, K7 and K8 were never approved. E2 depends on K6, and B-06 already measures it. The instrument is ahead of the approved content.
  • No claim level is board-approved. All eight board decisions remain pending, including the red-line claims. Every claim boundary in this document is a boundary against an unapproved ceiling.
  • The second Radar strand's status — offered but uncounted — is a compromise, not a resolution.
  • Nothing here has been tested with a real audience, in either format.

The three questions the founder must answer before a session plan can be written

1. Does the counted ratio stand, or does "don't count reps" still govern? F-01, F-02 and F-03 are three counted numbers over seven days. Your own ruling was that rep counts and frequency are deliberately not measured. The reconciliation offered above is that the objection was to tallying practice volume as a performance measure, and the ratio is not that — but that is this system's reading, not your ruling. Everything downstream turns on it: if counting is out, E1's countability test, E6's "even partly, even badly" framing, E7's full-pass item and the entire primary outcome are rebuilt around a different measure.

2. Is Essentials a Stage 1 session or a collapsed Stage 1+2 session? D-0091 says a standalone session may teach the full five skills; K-08's audience table says the five are named from Stage 2. This document cuts them from Essentials and keeps them conditionally in Foundations, which neither record authorises. The concrete choice: do the five public skills get six minutes and a job in a 90-minute session that is also used for schools and keynotes, or do they come out of it entirely? If they come out, F4 and P-11 go with them and nothing else changes.

3. Is the Leaders' Session a prerequisite for Foundations, or an add-on? It is currently priced as optional. F3 — the enabling condition, the named person, the sentence — assumes a leader who has already done L1 to L5, most critically L4, the two prohibitions. Without that leader, a participant's request goes to someone who does not know what they are being asked for, and the single most likely failure mode of the whole product is a manager asking to see people's moments. Either the Leaders' Session becomes a condition of booking Foundations, or F3 is cut from Foundations and the embedding promise on the offerings page comes off with it.

B2 Outcome Chain And Session Plan

B2 — The corrected outcome chain, and the session plan

What this is. B1's chain, rebuilt against the live build rather than the design-of-record files, with every C3 BLOCK resolved or explicitly justified; plus a runnable beat-by-beat plan for Essentials, the delta for Foundations, and the open founder decisions.

What changed against B1, in one place.

C3 finding Grade Resolution here
C3-07 safeguarding block below floor BLOCK 5 minutes, non-compressible, in Essentials; 8 in Foundations. Stated as a floor in both clocks and in the cut-order rule
C3-08 drill below D-0004's floor BLOCK 10 minutes, both formats, Sets A and B. Named as a floor
C3-09 no cut-order rule BLOCK §B4 — a written "if you are behind at 0:52, cut this, not that"
C3-14/C3-15 five public skills cut BLOCK Restored to Essentials as outcome E8. D-0003 fixes all six essential-content items as introduced in-session; cutting them dropped Stage 7 outcome K3. No D-0018 record is drafted because none is needed — nothing is being removed
C3-17 Our moments / Team Pulse deleted BLOCK Restored. Full aggregate-reveal-and-agree beat in Foundations (6 min), as D-0091 built it; a 2-minute anonymous theme reveal with no live agreement in Essentials, carried as a named D-0014 deviation exactly as the 1-hour build already does. Form 1 nomination item and the facilitator aggregation step both restored
C3-21 P-10 is a leading item BLOCK P-10 cut. Countability moves to a facilitator-side shape check in the room (no item) plus B-07, a banded Form 1 item asked before the session shapes anyone's answer

E7 is an improvement to that existing beat — all three steps, on the participant's own chosen moment, rather than a State Check plus one Shift run generically on "how you are right now." Stated that way everywhere in this document

C3-01/C3-02/C3-03 MAJOR E2 relabelled a knowledge outcome (K-E2); E4's licensed claim narrowed to what P-03 can carry; "would actually reach for" deleted from E5
C3-05 F2 unmeasurable MAJOR Accepted and disclosed. F2 keeps P-05b but the claim boundary no longer credits P-05b with evidencing the felt contrast

C3-16/C3-24 frequency criterion imposed by the instrument MAJOR The "twice a week" criterion is removed. The pair check tests shape (a place and a trigger), never frequency. D-0010's "not required to meet a frequency target" holds
C3-18 Leaders' Session retrofitted into Offer 1 MAJOR Removed from both Offer 1 formats. Held as a separate Offer 2 product with its own chain (§A3), per D-0090 Proposal 2. The struck Mas & Moretti reasoning is not used

Two things B1 got right and this document keeps unchanged: the outcome-chain format itself, and the arithmetic discipline. Every clock below is added up in the open.

Part A — the corrected outcome chain

The measurement constraint everything hangs off — restated correctly

B1 wrote the chain so that a cardinal ratio (F-01 ÷ F-02 ÷ F-03) could detect it, and C3-24 correctly identified the consequence: the instrument started setting product policy. That is inverted here.

The primary outcome is D-0017's approved architecture, in its approved form: an opportunity-conditional, binary, attempt-based initial-use threshold — "at least one reported attempted application," with an opportunity item so "didn't practise" is never confused with "had no opportunity." That is already approved and needs no founder ratification (C3 §6 is right about this).

  • F-01 (banded, revised): "In the last seven days, did the moment you chose come up? Not at all / once or twice / most days / not sure."
  • F-02 (binary, revised): "Did you run the three steps in any of them — even partly, even badly? Yes / no / there was no relevant moment."
  • Primary outcome: the proportion of participants who had an opportunity and attempted at least once, reported inside its own denominator and its band.

No participant tallies anything. This removes C3's self-administered failure rate ("five came up, I did one") without weakening the design: the band defeats the ceiling problem identically — someone with a quiet fortnight and someone with a busy one are read inside their own band, not against each other. Moving to cardinal counts would be a change to an approved architecture and needs its own decision record; a draft is in §D3 if Hunter wants it.

F-03 is not used by any outcome in this chain. See §D4 — it is a founder decision, recommended for cutting.

Format 1 — Essentials, 90 minutes

Talk-led with real practice in the room. Teams of 1–15. The bar: one moment, one full pass, one tool, one cue. (Adult workplace and community audiences only. School, youth and other external use is out of scope here — K-08's control-state warnings, C-16, block it pending review, and no safeguarding lead is named. B1's "also used for schools, public talks and keynotes" line is deleted, not softened.)

E1 — Names one recurring moment from their own week, specific enough to recognise when it arrives

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes one moment stated as a situation with a place and a trigger — "when my daughter asks for the iPad at dinner," not "stress" — and confirms with a neighbour (or the facilitator) that it has both.
Its job in the design It is the participant's cue, so it carries the whole transfer path (D-0008); and it is the unit F-01 asks about, so a moment that cannot be recognised when it arrives cannot be reported on. It is not required to recur at any frequency — D-0010 states the Radar is "a personal map, not a three-part compliance task" and that participants are not required to meet a frequency target. B1's twice-a-week test is removed.
Content required K-07's Radar prompt verbatim ("Think about the person you are trying to become in this season of life"); one worked narrowing of a vague moment to a specific one, modelled live; the two named stuck points — "my moment is too big" and "I can't think of one" — each with a scripted way through (both are in the plan at §B, beat 11). Both Radar strands are offered (handle better / experience more fully); only one moment is written. Not the two ownership layers as taught structure, not three moments.
Activity, with minutes 12 min. 2 min anonymous aggregate reveal of the Form 1 nomination themes (see below). 3 min facilitator narrows one vague moment live on the board. 4 min private silent write on the moment slip. 3 min shape check, in pairs, on format only, never content: "Does it name a place? Does it name a trigger?" Solo alternative stated before pairs form.
Measurement item and timepoint P-08 (post, existing) — "Write the one recurring moment you have chosen to work on." Scored for form only: does it name a situation rather than a feeling. B-07 (NEW, Form 1, pre-session) — "In a typical week, how often do you face situations like these? Not at all / once or twice / most days." Banded, asked before the session has taught anyone a criterion, which is why it is not the leading item P-10 was (C3-21).
Claim boundary (K-08) Licenses: "participants leave having chosen and written one specific moment from their own life." Does not license that they have a Radar, a practice, or a habit — a written moment is a starting condition, not behaviour change.

Our moments in Essentials — restored, at the deviation D-0091 already records. The Form 1 nomination item ("If your team, family or group had real appetite to get better at one thing together, what would it be?") is collected for both formats, and the facilitator aggregates it before the session — a real operational cost, named, not hidden. In Essentials the facilitator reveals the two or three common themes anonymously, in two minutes, and does not run a live agreement: there is no room in 90 minutes for a genuine facilitated agreement, and a nominal consensus from a room without appetite would be worse than none (D-0090, carried into D-0091). The aggregate goes to the host as a written theme list. This is exactly the treatment D-0091 §"The 1-hour format" already approves, carried as a named D-0014 deviation (text in §D2).

K-E2 — Accounts for the knowing–doing gap in their own words, without MFC's vocabulary

Relabelled from B1's "E2": producing a sentence is observable, but this is a knowledge outcome, not a skill outcome (C3-01). It sits in the K-series.

Field Content
Observable behaviour Says to one other person, in one or two sentences, why someone who knows what would help still does the other thing — using none of MFC's words.
Its job in the design It makes the definition land as an answer to a problem the room is holding, rather than an assertion; it earns Stop. It is the beat whose absence Hunter identified in the live build ("cycling through the framework").
Content required A plain causal account of ordinary experience: under load, attention narrows and the practised response arrives before the considered one; the old route is faster because it has been used more. Delivered as description a participant recognises from their own life, never as science — no brain diagrams, no amygdala, no fight-or-flight (K-08's ladder puts mechanism claims at Level 3, pending).
Activity, with minutes 7 min. 4 min facilitator account, built on one of the four moments named in the beat before it. 3 min explain-back to one other person, or written alone — the alternative is stated before pairs form. Facilitator listens to two or three and corrects nothing except a science claim.
Measurement item and timepoint B-06 (existing, all three timepoints) — the scenario item. P-01b (NEW, post, free text, one line) — "In one sentence: why does someone who knows what would help still do the other thing?" B-06 alone is recognition inside MFC's own framing and cannot detect whether the participant needed MFC's vocabulary (C3-04); P-01b can. ~30 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can account for the gap between knowing and doing in their own words." Does not license any claim about mechanism or brain change, and explicitly does not license that understanding the gap closes it.

Authority flag, carried forward unresolved. This corresponds to K6 in 10-product-finalisation-v1/02-design-rationale-and-outcomes-checklist.md, marked "Proposed — requires Hunter's approval under D-0018", never approved. B-06 already measures it. The instrument is ahead of the approved content. See §D4, question 5.

E3 — Says what each of the three steps means, unprompted, without the colours

Field Content
Observable behaviour Given "Stop, Shift, Do" and nothing else, states what each one is: catch the moment; create enough space where useful and available; make the next move with intention. Answering "red, amber, green" is a fail — that is the mnemonic retrieved, not the mechanism.
Its job in the design Retrieval under load is the design intent. A step recognised on a slide but not producible in a car park is not available in a real moment.
Content required K-07's locked wording, verbatim. The traffic light named exactly once, as contrast (D-0054), then the three corrections taught as their own items: red is catching the moment, not freezing in it; amber is making space, which is not always calming down; green is the next move with intention, not the right answer. Stop taught as the pivot. Explanatory feedback, never correctness-only (D-0004).
Activity, with minutes 7 min teach + 10 min drill (D-0004's mandatory retrieval element — 10 minutes is a floor, not a target; the live 60-minute build gives it 10 and calls it the single largest allocation in the format). Choral call-and-response, whole room answers as one voice, nobody cold-called. Two sets alternating, finishing on Set B: Set A the colour mapping, Set B the three corrections drilled as standing items ("Is amber calming down?" → "No — making space."). Online variant: "say it where you are" for Set A, chat waterfall released on a countdown for Set B; nobody unmuted by name.
Measurement item and timepoint P-02 (post, existing) — the ordered-sequence scenario. P-02b (NEW, post, free text, one line) — "What does Shift mean? Don't use the colours." This is the item that can register E3's actual failure mode; P-02 cannot (C3-04). ~30 s. F-04 (3 weeks, existing) — did you remember the three steps during a real moment.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants could state the three steps and what each means, and X% reported recalling them during a real moment at three weeks." Does not license that they used them well, or that recall predicts use.

E4 — Reads their own state as too much / too little / workable, for a specific moment

Field Content
Observable behaviour Two parts, and only one is verifiable. Verifiable: says why "workable" is not "calm" — that it is about what choice is available, not how pleasant it feels. Delivered but unverifiable by design: runs one silent State Check on themselves in the room, never shared, never collected, never scored (K-08 rule 7).
Its job in the design It is the only sanctioned self-assessment language MFC has, and the precondition for Shift meaning anything. It is also K-08 rule 9's protection delivered in the room rather than in a footnote.
Content required The three words with the anchor phrase "for this moment" used every time; the lock-in that State Check is not a fourth step; and the access idea underneath — state changes what is available to you, not only how you feel.
Activity, with minutes 5 min. 3.5 min teach. Ten counted seconds of silence for the live check — "Don't answer out loud. Right now, in this room — too much, too little, or workable for this moment?" — then: "That was a Stop." Eyes open or closed, their choice.
Measurement item and timepoint P-03 (post, existing) — what does a "workable" state mean.
Claim boundary — narrowed from B1 (C3-02) Licenses: "participants can state what workable means and distinguish it from calm, and were given one silent opportunity to apply it to themselves." Does not license that participants can use the state language on a real moment of their own — nothing verifies the silent half, and this document does not pretend otherwise. No claim about emotion regulation, physiological change, or that the check improves state.

E5 — Names one shift move, in their own words, for the moment they chose

B1's "that they would actually reach for" is deleted — it was an intention, forty lines after B1 cut ST-2 for being one (C3-03). The observable residue is the written move.

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes a concrete move in their own words — "stand up and walk to the kitchen before I answer" — not a category name ("Move it") and not "breathing".
Its job in the design A category name written back is recognition; a concrete self-worded move is the only thing an in-room activity can actually produce.
Content required The Shift menu as a menu to pick from, not a taxonomy to learn — Move it / Zoom in or out / Ask a different question / Bring someone in, K-07's public menu names used aloud, not the bare category words. One worked example each. The claims boundary stated aloud: breath is one option, not the required strategy (D-0083); Move it is never taught as a breathing exercise.
Activity, with minutes 5 min. 2 min menu named with one example each. 2 min private write: one move, for the moment chosen at E1. 1 min, optional, spoken to a neighbour: "which of these do you already reach for?" — existing behaviour, not a commitment.
Measurement item and timepoint P-05 (post, existing) — "Name one thing you could do in a moment to give yourself a bit more space." F-07 (3 weeks, existing) — did you use anything to give yourself space; what was it. Naming something MFC never taught is a success at F-07, not a failure.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants left with a self-worded, retrievable move, and X% reported using something at three weeks." Does not license that any tool works, that one category beats another, or that MFC's tools were the ones used.

E6 — States what counts as a rep, including one that went badly

Field Content
Observable behaviour Says that a rep counts when the moment was caught with intention, whatever the outcome — and gives one example, their own, of a rep that did not go well and still counted.
Its job in the design Outcome-independence is the most load-bearing idea for whether anyone practises after the session, and it is what makes F-02 answerable honestly: "even partly, even badly" only works if the room has already been told partly and badly count.
Content required K-07's locked definition, verbatim in written materials: "A mental rep is catching a moment and choosing your next move, on purpose, toward what matters. You may catch the moment before it happens, while it is happening, or afterwards. The outcome does not determine whether it counts." What does not count: a moment by itself, a habit done entirely on autopilot, reading about it. Plus the normalising beat — hands up if you've ever caught yourself scrolling and put the phone down.
Activity, with minutes 4 min. 2 min definition and normalising beat. 2 min: "Think of a time this week you caught something and it still went badly. That was a rep." One or two volunteered aloud, never solicited by name.
Measurement item and timepoint P-04 (post, existing) — which example best represents a rep. P-04b (NEW, post) — "Think of a rep you ran that didn't go the way you wanted. Did it still count? Yes / no." One tick, optional one line. This is the half C3-04 found measured by nothing. ~30 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can distinguish a rep from information or an accident, and can identify a rep that did not go well as still counting." Does not license any claim about practice volume. MFC does not count reps as a performance measure.

E7 — Runs all three steps on their own chosen moment, in the room

Stated honestly, because B1 got this wrong. The live build already ends on an actual rep: the 1-hour format's "Do one, right now" beat at 0:38–0:41, added 2026-08-05, carrying its own rationale (Baldwin & Ford transfer of training; Bandura mastery experience) and mapped in the build's own traceability table to Form 2 Q7. This is not a discovered hole. What that beat runs is a State Check plus one simple Shift, generically, on "how you actually are right now." E7 is an improvement to it in two specific respects: all three steps, and on the participant's own chosen moment, which is written eight minutes earlier rather than after. The 3-hour build's Application phase genuinely has no equivalent beat — that half of B1's finding stands.

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes four lines on their own moment: the moment / what the Stop looks like here / my state read / my next move — then says the next move out loud to themselves or a neighbour.
Its job in the design It is the in-room analogue of F-02, and it makes the follow-up wording honest: "even partly, even badly" refers to something they have already done once.
Content required Nothing new. It applies E1, E3, E4, E5 and E6 in sequence — which is why it fits inside 90 minutes. Minimum-viable version stated aloud (C3-10): "If you only get two lines down, write the moment and the next move. That's the pass."
Activity, with minutes 8 min. 2 min facilitator models one full pass aloud on the board moment. 5 min private, silent, written. 1 min: say the next move out loud — to a neighbour, or under your breath to yourself; both named as equal. No public hands-up. B1's "hands up if you got all the way through / partway" is deleted: it sorts the room into completers and partial-completers on a construct K-07 defines as outcome-independent, and it contaminates P-09 asked ninety seconds later (C3 §5, §6).
Measurement item and timepoint P-09 (NEW, post) — "Today, did you run all three steps on a moment of your own? Yes / no." Binary and attempt-based, matching F-02's revised form so the in-room pass and the three-week attempt sit on one scale. ~20 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "X% of participants reported running all three steps on a moment of their own before leaving the room." Does not license competence, habit or transfer. One rehearsed pass in a supported room is not one pass in a real moment, and the two must never be reported in the same number.

E8 — Says which of the five public skills their own moment mainly asks for

Restored to Essentials. D-0003 fixes all six essential-content items as first introduced within the session, and the five public skills are one of them; cutting them also dropped approved Stage 7 outcome K3. D-0091 and K-07's amended staged-arc section resolve the Stage 1 / Stage 2 question directly: for a standalone session — which is the only contact this audience gets — Stage 1 and Stage 2 collapse, and the session legitimately teaches the full five skills, full State Check and the full Shift menu. K-08's audience-translation table still reads "the five public skills are named from Stage 2" and has not been updated to match; that conflict is named in §D5, not silently chosen — but K-07 governs Framework meaning and D-0091 is the later, specific decision, so the skills stay in.

Field Content
Observable behaviour Given the five labels in their locked wording, says which one their own written moment mainly asks of them, and why, in one line.
Its job in the design It gives the five skills a job instead of leaving them as vocabulary named once, which was the outcomes checklist's own finding against K3. It also makes E5's menu choice less arbitrary — the skill named is a bridge from the moment to the move.
Content required K-07's locked wording, read once, one short line each: Notice — notice what is happening inside you, around you, and between you and others · Shift — create enough space to become workable, through your body or through your thinking · Choose — identify what matters and follow through · Focus — put your attention where it matters and return it when it drifts · Connect — connect better with yourself and others. The seven deep skills stay out (Stage 3 holds, per K-07).
Activity, with minutes 5 min teach, plus 60 seconds folded into E1's write — "Which one is your moment mainly asking for?" — written on the same slip. Private; nothing read out.
Measurement item and timepoint P-11 (NEW, post) — "Which of the five does your moment mainly ask for, and why?" (select one + one line). ~30 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can map a real moment of their own to one of the five public skills." Does not license that they can distinguish all five, define them, or use them.

Essentials — the clock, added up

Clock Min Beat Serves
0:00–0:05 5 Welcome, non-clinical scope, D-0015's six controls, D-0016 disclosure + placeholder Floor — non-compressible
0:05–0:09 4 Protected form time — token cards issued, Form 1 catch-up Measurement
0:09–0:13 4 Four ordinary moments named; the definition and the distinction B-04
0:13–0:20 7 Why the gap exists + explain-back K-E2
0:20–0:25 5 The five public skills, locked wording E8
0:25–0:32 7 Stop–Shift–Do, Stop as the pivot, the three colour corrections (D-0054) E3
0:32–0:37 5 State Check + live silent check E4
0:37–0:47 10 Retrieval drill, Sets A and B, finishing on B (D-0004) E3 — floor
0:47–0:52 5 Shift menu — four named, one written in their own words E5
0:52–0:56 4 What counts as a rep, including one that went badly E6
0:56–1:08 12 The moment — theme reveal, narrow, write, shape check, which skill E1, E8
1:08–1:16 8 The full pass, on their own moment E7
1:16–1:19 3 Cue attached to something already in the week; lapse-and-return; named barriers Transfer (D-0008)
1:19–1:21 2 Close — threshold framing —
1:21–1:30 9 Protected form time — Form 2, in the room Measurement

5+4+4+7+5+7+5+10+5+4+12+8+3+2+9 = 90. Protected measurement time: 4 + 9 = 13 minutes (14.4%).

Phase mapping (D-0003), published rather than assumed. Orientation 0:00–0:20 (welcome, forms, definition, the gap) · Skills 0:20–0:52 (five skills, SSD, State Check, drill, Shift menu) · Revisiting/Connecting 0:52–0:56 (what counts as a rep — the recall-based retrieval element sits in the drill at 0:37) · Application 0:56–1:21. Essentials has no distinct Mechanism block. The Human Operating System's six components are not taught; the one line that does Mechanism's job — state changes what is available to you, not only how you feel — is delivered inside E4. This is a declared D-0014 deviation with its reason (§D2), not an undeclared reordering.

Two honest notes on this clock.

  1. 0:09–0:13 is the tightest beat in the format. Four minutes carries four named moments plus the definition and the distinction — MFC's central positioning claim. It is deliverable as a pure talk beat with no discussion, and it is the first thing the cut-order rule protects from further compression rather than a place to find time.
  2. The clock starts with everyone seated. There is no arrival or settling allowance. Book the room for 1h45, not 1h30, and open the doors fifteen minutes early with the form on the table. If Form 1 cannot be sent seven days ahead — likely for a very small business with no email list — the session runs at 95 minutes with a 9-minute Form 1 block, and the facilitator must know which version they are running before they arrive (§B6).

Format 2 — Foundations, half day (180 min content + 15 min break)

Foundations carries every Essentials outcome unchanged. What follows is only what the extra time buys. The rule: an outcome belongs here only if it cannot be produced in 90 minutes — because it needs a partner, a second person's material, a felt contrast, or a conversation the room has to prepare. "More content" is not a reason.

F1 — Runs the three steps on another person's moment, out loud, in both roles

Field Content
Observable behaviour In a pair, takes both roles: as supporter, asks the three questions ("What's going on for you right now?" / offers rather than directs a shift / "What's one next step that could help?"); as the person in the moment, is taken through their own. Then names one thing that was harder about doing it with someone than alone.
Its job in the design Nearly every moment worth practising has another person in it, and running the sequence with someone is a different skill from running it alone. It is also the only outcome producing behaviour another person could observe.
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it Two turns plus a debrief. A one-turn version rehearses half the skill and leaves the other half practised by nobody. 21 minutes minimum.
Content required K-07's "supporting others" table — the three moves, alone and with someone. The binding limits delivered as content, not as a caveat: offer, never force (K-08 rule 6); peer support, not treatment (rule 2); knowing when to stop and bring in more support is part of the skill (rule 10). Opting out of pairs stated as normal before pairs are formed, with a solo written alternative offered by default.
Activity, with minutes 21 min. 3 min model and limits. 7 min turn one. 7 min turn two. 4 min debrief: "What was harder about doing it with someone?"
Measurement item and timepoint P-12 (NEW, post) — "Today, did you take someone else through the three steps? Both roles / one role / no — I worked alone." ~20 s. F-11 (NEW, 3 weeks) — "Since the session, did you use this with another person — either taking someone through it, or saying out loud what you were doing? Yes / no / no relevant moment." Optional one line.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants practised the sequence as peer support, and X% reported using it with another person at three weeks." Does not license anything about team culture, relationships, psychological safety, or that MFC delivers support to third parties.

F2 — Picks a shift move that fits the specific moment, having run the contrast

Field Content
Observable behaviour Beyond E5's "a move I can name": states which move fits this moment and why another does not; and, in the debrief, names one thing they noticed between the version run without the skill and the version run with it.
Its job in the design Matching is where the toolkit stops being a poster. A participant with one move for all moments will abandon it the first time it does not fit and read that as the method failing rather than the match.
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it Two tools actually tried in the room (10 min) plus the same moment run without and then with the skill, with a debrief on what was noticed (15 min). Essentials can produce a named move; it cannot produce a felt contrast. 25 minutes.
Content required The four categories with the downshift/upshift rule — the same tool can do either (K-07, D-0083). Two tools practised live, chosen by the room. The contrast run both times ending identically — still tired, phone in hand, the thing still not done — so the tension is in what changed, not in whether it worked out (this is the live build's own staging, and it is correct). Facilitator asks what participants noticed, never what was correct.
Activity, with minutes 25 min. 10 min toolkit, two tools tried live. 15 min contrast — pre-filmed clip or two facilitators live — then pair debrief: "what was in the second version that wasn't in the first?" The second live State Check is folded into the debrief, unannounced, demonstrating the answer changes.
Measurement item and timepoint P-05 (existing) plus P-05b (NEW, post) — "Why that one, for that moment?" (free text, one line). ~45 s. F-07 at follow-up, unchanged.
Claim boundary — corrected (C3-05) Licenses: "participants selected a tool for a specific moment and can say why." P-05b measures reasoning about fit; it does not evidence the felt contrast, and the contrast run is therefore a delivered activity with no item of its own. That is disclosed, not papered over: the most expensive fifteen minutes in Foundations currently cannot be distinguished, in the data, from a room that skipped it. Does not license that the tool works, that matching improves outcomes, or anything physiological.

F3 — Names the enabling condition their moment depends on, and who they have to ask

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes: the enabling condition their chosen moment depends on; whether it is inside their control or someone else's; if someone else's, the named person, the sentence they will say, and when. Separately, states where a problem goes if it is a workload, safety or leadership problem rather than a practice problem.
Its job in the design This is the environment layer, and it is simultaneously the safeguard: the beat that opens the collective layer is the beat that closes the door on reframing a psychosocial hazard as a skill deficit. K-07's Radar constraints make that non-optional — "a shared or team Radar must never be used to reframe harmful workload, unsafe leadership or psychosocial hazards as individual skill deficits. A route must exist for structural issues."
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it It needs the diagnostic lens first (8 min), then the write and the routing (15 min). Compressed, it becomes a slogan about environment with no named person and no route — worse than not raising it.
Content required The Human Operating System's diagnostic question — "What is shaping access in this moment?" — and the Environment component only, not all six. The enabling-conditions layer of the Radar. That an Our moment requires genuine agreement and is not a demand one person makes and labels shared (K-07). The hazard route, named concretely for that organisation, agreed with the host before the session.
Activity, with minutes 23 min (8 diagnostic + 15 write and route). Nothing read aloud, nothing collected.
Measurement item and timepoint F-12 (NEW, 3 weeks) — "You wrote down one thing you would ask someone for. Did you ask? Yes / no / not yet / it stopped being relevant." Optional one line. The only item in the instrument that reaches past the individual without making an organisational claim: one person, one act, self-reported.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants identified an enabling condition and X% reported making the request at three weeks." Does not license anything about culture, norms, team change, absenteeism, productivity or psychosocial risk. MFC has no organisational measurement instrument and may not claim one engagement changes any of the above.

F5 — The room agrees one shared "when X, we will Y" commitment, or declines it out loud

This is D-0091's decided-and-built beat, restored. B1 deleted it on reasoning that was superseded five days before B1 was written.

Field Content
Observable behaviour Either: the room states one shared commitment in the form "when [this happens], we will [this]", which each participant writes on their own worksheet next to their own moment — or the room declines, out loud, and moves on. Both are successful outcomes of this beat.
Its job in the design Groups routinely already want a change and each person privately assumes they are the only one; anonymously surfacing what the room nominated corrects that before any discussion. A shared if-then plan outperforms a shared aspiration. Declining is protected because a nominally-agreed moment from a room without appetite would be worse than none.
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it It needs a genuine facilitated agreement conversation. Essentials gets the reveal and the host handover only (named D-0014 deviation, §D2).
Content required The anonymously aggregated Form 1 nomination themes, prepared by the facilitator beforehand. What My moments and Our moments are. That an Our moment requires explicit agreement. The plain permission to decline.
Activity, with minutes 6 min. 2 min anonymous theme reveal. 1 min genuine read of the room — hands or a plain ask. Then either 3 min drafting one "when X, we will Y" and naming who owns it, or a plain "that's completely fine, plenty of rooms don't" and straight on.
Measurement item and timepoint No participant item, deliberately. The commitment, its wording and its named owner are recorded on the facilitator's delivery record. For case-study cohorts only, it is reviewed at D-0056's extended check-in wave. D-0091's day-10–14 templated reminder to the named owner is drafted but not wired into the send infrastructure — do not describe it as running.
Claim boundary Licenses: "the room agreed one shared commitment" or "the room declined one" — a facilitator record of what happened in a room. Does not license anything about norms, culture, or that the commitment was kept.

F4 — is deleted as a separate outcome

B1's F4 ("the five skills, given a job") existed only because the skills had been cut from Essentials. They are restored, so the outcome is E8 in both formats and Foundations gains nothing new here — it simply has room to illustrate each skill with a second example. P-11 stays, in both formats.

0:08–0:12 4 Protected form time — token cards, Form 1 catch-up Measurement
0:12–0:22 10 Self-elicitation — butcher's paper per table, sheets to the wall, facilitator circulating Generation-effect opener
0:22–0:26 4 Four ordinary moments named; the gap named Sets up K-E2
0:26–0:33 7 Why the gap exists + explain-back K-E2
0:33–0:38 5 The reveal — definition and distinction read against the room's own words B-04
0:38–0:45 7 Stop–Shift–Do, Stop as the pivot, colour corrections E3
