First block: 8+4+10+4+7+5+7+5+10+5+8 = 73 (0:00–1:13). Second block: 10+15+5+6+12+8+21+15+3+2+10 = 107 (1:13–3:00). 73 + 107 = 180 content minutes. Elapsed with the 15-minute break: 3h15, before arrival — book the room for 3h30. Protected measurement time: 4 + 10 = 14 minutes (7.8%).

Phase mapping (D-0003). Orientation 0:00–0:38 · Skills 0:38–1:05 · Mechanism 1:05–1:13 · Revisiting/Connecting 1:13–1:49 (toolkit, contrast, what counts as a rep, Our moments) · Application 1:49–2:50. Skills precedes Mechanism, which is the fixed order; B1 inverted it (C3 §8 item 8).

The 90-minute difference, reconciled beat by beat

What the extra time buys Min
Self-elicitation opener (generation effect — charged here, not to F1, correcting C3-11) +10
Deeper safeguarding block (8 vs 5) +3
Definition and gap given two beats instead of one compressed one (9 vs 4) +5
HOS diagnostic lens and Environment +8
Shift toolkit with two tools tried live (10 vs 5) +5
Experiential contrast and debrief +15
What counts as a rep, with room to take two examples (5 vs 4) +1
Our moments — live agreement rather than a 2-minute reveal +6
Peer application, both roles +21
Enabling condition, named ask, hazard route +15
Form 2 protected time (10 vs 9 — two more items) +1

3+10+5+8+5+15+1+6+21+15+1 = 90. 90 + 90 = 180. Every minute of the difference is attached to a named outcome or to a beat that exists in both. Nothing is reassigned to an outcome it does not serve.

A3 — The Leaders' Session is a separate offer, not part of either format

D-0090 Proposal 2 is explicit: leader modelling "is an Offer 2 requirement and must not be retrofitted into Offer 1. A standalone workshop has no leader relationship to work with, and pretending otherwise would be the exact individual-responsibility framing K-07's own binding constraints prohibit." B1's L1–L5 was exactly that retrofit. It is removed from both Offer 1 formats here.

Held as its own product, with its own chain, not built in this document. Four things must be true before it is designed:

  1. Its evidential basis has to be rebuilt. B1's rationale — "norms shift when network-central people visibly adopt something" — is the sentence D-0090 struck. Mas & Moretti shows behavioural spillover under observation, and the line of sight runs opposite to what leader modelling requires. D-0090 retains it only for visibility effects.
  2. It needs a fifth instrument that does not exist. L-03/L-04 are three-week items, and the architecture is "three forms, every participant, every pathway" plus a case-study wave.
  3. It cannot be anonymous at n=1–3. With one to three leaders, a self-generated linkage code provides no anonymity: MFC would know exactly who wrote the sentence. The reporting floors (nothing under 20, no subgroup under 10) also make single-organisation leader data unreportable. Leaders' data is poolable across organisations and nowhere else.
  4. The one prohibition worth carrying forward regardless — and it does not need the session to exist — is the standing instruction that a manager must never ask to see anyone's moment, and never treat non-practice as a performance issue. K-07's Radar constraint already requires personal moments to stay private in organisational delivery. That belongs in the host agreement and the booking checklist, signed before the session, not in a leaders' session that may never be bought. It is written into §B6.

Consequence for Foundations, and it is a real one. F3 produces a named person and a sentence. If that person has had no contact with MFC, the request lands on someone who does not know what they are being asked for. This document's position: F3 stands without a Leaders' Session, because the hazard-routing half is what makes it safe and that does not depend on a leader — but the embedding promise on the offerings page does depend on it. See §D4, question 3.

A5 — Burden arithmetic, shown

Baseline from the forms draft: Form 2 today = 12 items ≈ 8 min (B-03…B-06, P-01…P-08), ≈40 s per item. Form 3 = 10 items ≈ 6 min.

Form 2, Essentials. Cut B-03 and B-05 (concept recognition attached to no outcome in either format) −80 s. Cut P-06 (predicted retrieval; instrumentation only, useful solely as a calibration check against F-04, and F-04 survives) −40 s. Cut P-10 (C3-21, leading) — never added. Add P-01b 30 s, P-02b 30 s, P-04b 30 s, P-09 20 s, P-11 30 s = +140 s. 480 − 120 + 140 = 500 s ≈ 8.3 min → 9 minutes budgeted. 14 items.

Form 2, Foundations. Essentials' set plus P-05b (45 s) and P-12 (20 s) = 565 s ≈ 9.4 min → 10 minutes budgeted. 16 items. B1 budgeted 8 for both and was two minutes short at Foundations; that is why Foundations here totals 180 and not 182.

Form 3. Cut F-03 (§D4, question 1) −1 item. Essentials: 9 items ≈ 5.5 min. Foundations adds F-11 and F-12, both with an optional one-line free text rather than a required one: 11 items ≈ 7 min. That is still a ~15% increase on the instrument whose response rate carries every durability claim MFC will make — disclosed, and the reason both free texts are optional.

Form 1. Adds B-07 (banded, ~20 s) and the nomination item (D-0091 item 08, ~30 s). ≈5 min → ≈6 min. Sent seven days ahead; the in-room block is a catch-up, not a completion slot.

All of this is arithmetic on the forms draft's own estimates. Nothing has been timed with real participants, and none of the new items has been through Eimear Quigley or Debra Fidler or been cognitively tested.

Part B — the Essentials session plan, beat by beat

Written so a facilitator who has never seen this can run it. [SAY] lines are the intent and the wording, not a script to read verbatim — except where marked verbatim, which are the locked or safeguarding lines and must be delivered as written.

Before the room: the delivery record and booking checklist at §B6 must be complete. This session is not deliverable to participants until D-0016's six safeguarding matters resolve. The disclosure placeholder must not go out unresolved.

Room: 12–20 seated so everyone can turn to a neighbour. Visible clock or silent timer, facilitator-only. Standing rules, said once at 0:00 and honoured all session: you can step out of anything without explaining why; nobody is required to say anything personal; every pair activity has a written solo alternative, stated before pairs form, not offered on request.

0:00–0:05 · Welcome, scope, consent, disclosure — 5 minutes, non-compressible

Serves: the enabling conditions for everything else. This block is the same length it would be in a three-day programme. Brevity is never a legitimate reason to shorten safeguarding text.

Facilitator does: stands, does not sit; delivers D-0015's six universal minimum controls in full, the non-clinical scope statement, and the D-0016 disclosure statement with its visible placeholder. Points to the disclosure card in front of each person.

[SAY], and this one is verbatim in substance: "Before anything else. This is education and skill practice. It is not therapy, not treatment, not counselling, and not a crisis service. If something comes up for you today that needs more than a workshop, that's not a failure of anything — it's what this card in front of you is for. You can step out of any part of today without telling me why. You will never be asked to say anything personal out loud. Nothing you write today gets collected or read by me or by anyone who booked this session."

Participants do: nothing but listen. No task in this block.

Materials: disclosure / participant card, one per person, on the seat before they arrive.

0:05–0:09 · Protected form time — 4 minutes

Serves: measurement. Protected: this block is never shortened to buy content time.

Facilitator does: hands out shuffled token cards — pre-printed, never tied to a name. Explains once that the code goes on every form and the card is theirs to keep. Then a catch-up window for anyone who did not complete Form 1 in the week before.

[SAY]: "The card in your hand has a code on it. Write that code on anything you fill in today and on the form that reaches you in three weeks. It isn't your name and we can't work backwards from it to you — that's the point. Keep the card. If you didn't get to the form we sent last week, do it now; if you did, this is four minutes to get a coffee where you're sitting."

Participants do: write the code on the Form 2 sheet in front of them; complete Form 1 if outstanding.

Materials: shuffled token cards (one per person, +5 spare); Form 1 printed (+5 spare); Form 2 printed, face-down, one per person; pens, identical.

0:09–0:13 · Four ordinary moments, the definition, the distinction — 4 minutes

Serves: B-04, and it loads the material K-E2 uses next.

Facilitator does: names four ordinary moments out loud, no discussion — the tone is recognition, not diagnosis. Then the definition and the distinction, in that order, in two sentences each.

[SAY]: "Four moments. The email you read three times before you answer it. The conversation at home that goes sideways in about nine seconds. The thing you meant to do at 4pm and it's now 7. The walk to the car after a meeting, replaying it. Anyone recognise any of those? Don't answer, just notice." "Mental health is how you're doing. Mental fitness is what you're able to do — think, feel, act and connect in life's everyday moments. They're related and they're not the same thing, and almost nothing you've ever been offered was aimed at the second one."

Participants do: listen. Hold this beat at four minutes — questions here are the single commonest source of over-run in the format; take them at 1:19.

Materials: none.

0:13–0:20 · Why the gap exists, and say it back — 7 minutes

Serves: K-E2.

Facilitator does (4 min): gives a plain causal account, built on one of the four moments just named. No brain diagrams, no amygdala, no fight-or-flight — this is a K-08 boundary, not a style preference.

[SAY]: "Take the conversation at home. You know, at the time, that the useful move is to stop talking and listen. You've known that for years. And you interrupt anyway, and you notice about a second later. So what happened? Nothing's wrong with you. Under load, your attention narrows, and the response you've done ten thousand times arrives before the one you've thought about twice. The old route is faster because it's been used more. That's it. That's the whole problem. Knowing the answer was never the missing piece." "And here's the part nobody says out loud: nobody sat you down and taught you what to do with that. Not at school. Not really at home. You assembled your own strategies out of whatever happened to you and whatever you picked up. That's why your life makes the sense it does. It isn't a you problem. It's a gap in what everyone was given."

Then (3 min): "Turn to one person. Say that back in your own words — and you're not allowed to use any of the words I just used. If you'd rather not turn to anyone, write it instead; that's a completely normal choice and it's the same exercise."

Facilitator listens to two or three pairs, corrects nothing except a science claim. If someone says "it's your amygdala," correct it once, gently, out loud: "that's the version we're all told — it's not what's happening here, and we don't need it."

Participants do: explain the gap to one person, in their own words, or write it.

Materials: none. Solo variant (n=1 or a room that will not speak): the participant writes the sentence and reads it back to the facilitator.

0:20–0:25 · The five public skills — 5 minutes

Serves: E8, and it is one of D-0003's six essential-content items.

Facilitator does: reads the five in their locked wording, one short line of illustration each. No elaboration, no deep skills, no evidence layer.

[SAY], the five verbatim: "Notice — notice what is happening inside you, around you, and between you and others. Shift — create enough space to become workable, through your body or through your thinking. Choose — identify what matters and follow through. Focus — put your attention where it matters and return it when it drifts. Connect — connect better with yourself and others." "That's the map. You're not learning five things today. You're going to pick one moment, and one of these is what that moment is mainly asking of you. We'll come back to it."

Participants do: listen; the skills card is in front of them.

Materials: skills reference card, one per person.

0:25–0:32 · Stop, Shift, Do — 7 minutes

Serves: E3.

Facilitator does: teaches the three steps in K-07's locked wording. Names the traffic light exactly once, as a contrast, then drops it (D-0054). Teaches the three corrections at the point of teaching, not as an afterthought. Teaches Stop as the pivot.

[SAY], the three steps verbatim: "Stop — catch the moment. Shift — create enough space where useful and available. Do — make the next move with intention." "People sometimes map these to red, amber, green. Say it once, then let it go, because the colours mislead in three specific ways. Red is not freezing — Stop is catching the moment, and it's the pivot: everything after it only exists because you noticed. Amber is not calming down — Shift is making space, and sometimes making space means getting your energy up, not down. Green is not the right answer — Do is your next move, made on purpose. There is no correct move here, and I'm not going to grade one."

Participants do: listen; the SSD card is in front of them.

Materials: SSD card (colour + word + glyph — colour is never the only carrier).

0:32–0:37 · State Check — 5 minutes

Serves: E4.

Facilitator does (3.5 min): teaches the three words with the anchor phrase used every time. States the lock-in: not a fourth step. Names what workable is not.

[SAY]: "One question: is my state too much, too little, or workable — for this moment. That last bit, 'for this moment', is not decoration; it's the whole thing. Too much is more intensity, urgency or load than the moment can use. Too little is less energy, clarity or alertness than the moment needs. Workable means you've got enough access to choice. It does not mean calm. You can be furious and workable. You can be perfectly calm and completely unable to act. This isn't a fourth step and it's never scored."

Then (~1.5 min), the live check: "Don't answer out loud, don't write anything, nobody will ever ask you. Right now, in this room — too much, too little, or workable, for this moment? Ten seconds. Eyes open or closed, your choice." Count ten seconds of silence. Then: "That was a Stop."

Participants do: one silent self-check. Nothing shared, nothing collected, nothing scored (K-08 rule 7).

Materials: State Check card.

0:37–0:47 · The retrieval drill — 10 minutes, floor

Serves: E3. This is D-0004's mandatory retrieval element. 10 minutes is the floor. If the session is running behind, this is not where the time comes from.

Facilitator does: call-and-response at pace, whole room answering in unison. Nobody is cold-called by name. Two sets, alternating, finishing on Set B. Feedback is explanatory, never correctness-only (D-0004): when the room gets one wrong, say why, not just "no."

  • Set A — the mapping. "Stop is?" → "Catch the moment." "Shift is?" → "Create enough space." "Do is?" → "The next move, with intention." Vary the order; speed up.
  • Set B — the three corrections, drilled as standing items. "Is Stop freezing?" → "No — catching the moment." "Is amber calming down?" → "No — making space." "Is Do the right answer?" → "No — the next move, with intention."

Online variant: the choral version does not work over video. Set A becomes "say it where you are" (mics off, facilitator answers after a counted three). Set B becomes a chat waterfall — typed but held until a countdown releases every answer at once. Nobody is ever unmuted by name.

Participants do: answer out loud, together, repeatedly.

Materials: none physical. The facilitator must have rehearsed the call-and-response pattern.

0:47–0:52 · The Shift menu — 5 minutes

Serves: E5.

Facilitator does (2 min): names the four menu items with one concrete example each — the menu names aloud, never the bare category words (K-07, D-0084). States the claims boundary out loud.

[SAY]: "Four kinds of shift. Move it — feet on the floor, one slower breath, stand up, step outside. Zoom in or out — name three things you can see, or ask what this will matter in a week, or narrow to the one next thing. Ask a different question — what would I tell a friend here? Is this a fact, or a feeling talking? Bring someone in — text one person, ask for two minutes, say out loud what's actually going on." "One thing, plainly: breathing is one option on that list. It is not the required strategy and it is not what this is. Same tools go both ways — the same move can bring you down or bring you up."

Then (2 min), private write: "One move. In your words, not mine. Not 'Move it' — what you'd actually do." Then (1 min), optional to a neighbour: "Which of these do you already reach for?" — existing behaviour, not a commitment. Opt-out stated.

Participants do: write one concrete move on the moment slip.

Materials: shift-menu card or the reverse of the skills card; moment slip already on the table.

0:52–0:56 · What counts as a rep — 4 minutes

Serves: E6.

Facilitator does (2 min): the locked definition, then the normalising beat.

[SAY], the definition verbatim: "A mental rep is catching a moment and choosing your next move with intention. You may catch the moment before it happens, while it is happening, or afterwards. The outcome does not determine whether it counts." "Hands up if you've ever caught yourself scrolling and put the phone down. That was a rep. You've done thousands. Nobody ever named it — and nobody ever taught you the shift."

Then (2 min): "Think of a time this week you caught something and it still went badly. Went badly. That was a rep too. It counts. If a rep only counted when it worked, everybody would stop by Thursday." One or two volunteered aloud if they arise; never solicited by name.

What does not count, said once: a moment by itself; a habit done entirely on autopilot; reading about it without applying anything.

Participants do: listen; optionally offer an example.

Materials: none.

0:56–1:08 · The moment — 12 minutes

Serves: E1, E8. Includes the Our-moments theme reveal.

0:56–0:58 — the theme reveal (2 min). Facilitator reads the two or three most common themes from the Form 1 nomination question, aggregated beforehand, anonymously and never attached to anyone. [SAY]: "Before you choose your own: when we asked what your team would want to get better at together, the things that came up most were these. I'm not going to work them here — we don't have the room for that conversation in ninety minutes, and a half-agreed one would be worse than none. I'll give the themes to whoever booked this, with nobody's name on them. Hold them in mind while you pick yours."

0:58–1:01 — narrowing, modelled live (3 min). Facilitator takes one deliberately vague moment and narrows it on the board. [SAY]: "'Stress at work' — I can't do anything with that. Where does it actually happen? 'When I open my laptop on Monday morning.' Now it has a place and a trigger, and you'll know it when it arrives. That's the whole test."

1:01–1:05 — private write (4 min). [SAY], the prompt verbatim: "Think about the person you are trying to become in this season of life." "One moment. Either one you want to handle better, or one you want to experience more fully — both are real, pick whichever is honest. Write it with a place and a trigger. Then, underneath, which of the five skills it's mainly asking for. Nobody reads this. It goes home with you."

The two stuck points, scripted — the facilitator walks the room and uses these by name: - "My moment is too big." → "Then don't take the whole thing. Take the first ten seconds of it. What's the smallest version that's still real?" - "I can't think of one." → "Don't hunt for the most important one. What happened yesterday that you'd rather have handled differently? That'll do — you're not marrying it."

1:05–1:08 — the shape check, in pairs (3 min). On format only, never content. [SAY]: "Turn to one person. You are not going to read your moment out. You're going to ask them two questions and hear yes or no. Does it name a place? Does it name a trigger? That's it. If you'd rather do this on your own, check your own against those two questions — that's a normal choice, and it works." Do not ask how often it comes up. Frequency is not a criterion (D-0010).

Participants do: write one moment, one skill; check the shape.

Materials: moment slip, one per person; board or flipchart; marker.

1:08–1:16 · The full pass, on their own moment — 8 minutes

Serves: E7. This is the beat the whole session builds to.

1:08–1:10 — modelled (2 min). Facilitator runs a complete pass aloud on the board moment, all four lines, thinking out loud. [SAY]: "My moment: opening the laptop Monday morning. What the Stop looks like here: my hand's on the lid and I notice my jaw. My state read: too much, for this moment. My next move: I stand up and fill the kettle before I open anything. That's the whole thing. Four lines. Eleven seconds in real life."

1:10–1:15 — private, silent, written (5 min). Four lines on the full-pass sheet: the moment / what the Stop looks like here / my state read / my next move. [SAY], the minimum-viable version, said before they start: "If you only get two lines down, write the moment and the next move. That is a complete pass. Don't sit there stuck on line three."

1:15–1:16 — say it (1 min). [SAY]: "Say your next move out loud. To the person next to you, or under your breath to yourself — those are the same thing here, and I'm not checking which." No hands-up. Nobody is asked who finished.

Participants do: write the four lines; say the next move aloud.

Materials: full-pass sheet, A5, one per person.

1:16–1:19 · The cue, and what happens when you stop — 3 minutes

Serves: transfer (D-0008), and it is the beat that keeps people from reading their own lapse as failure.

Facilitator does: cue selection, then the barriers named — plainly, out loud, not as a caveat.

[SAY]: "One cue. Something already in your week that will remind you — the kettle going on, unlocking your phone, sitting down at your desk. Write it on the card. You're not adding anything to your day; you're attaching this to something already in it." "And then the honest part. Most people's first go at this fades. Not some — most. That's expected, it isn't failure, and here's exactly how it'll go: you'll forget. You'll be unsure what to do in the moment. The moment will feel too big to pause in. You'll go a whole day without an obvious chance. All of that is normal, and all of it is the reason to pick one small moment rather than wait for a perfect one. One rep, whenever you next notice you stopped. That's the whole re-entry."

Also named once, in a line: sleep, movement and food shape what's available to you — that's the Engine, it's real, and it's on the card. Named, not expanded (K-07).

Participants do: write one cue on the cue card.

Materials: cue card, wallet-sized; take-home card carrying the locked rep definition and the Engine line.

1:19–1:21 · Close — 2 minutes

Facilitator does: threshold framing, not outcome framing. Takes any held questions here.

[SAY]: "You're leaving with the start of a skill, not a finished one. This isn't a course you complete, it's a practice you keep. Today was your first rep, not your last. You have one moment, one move, one reminder — that's the whole plan, and it's already written down in front of you."

1:21–1:30 · Protected form time, Form 2 — 9 minutes

Serves: measurement. Protected. In the room, before anyone leaves. This is a named block in the session plan and the facilitator's job is to hold it.

Facilitator does: "Nine minutes, and then you're free. Code from your card at the top. Nothing here is scored and nothing goes to whoever booked this with your name on it." Then stays quiet and does not answer content questions that would change an answer.

Participants do: complete Form 2 (14 items: B-04, B-06, P-01, P-01b, P-02, P-02b, P-03, P-04, P-04b, P-05, P-07, P-08, P-09, P-11).

Materials: Form 2 printed; spare pens.

B4 · The cut-order rule — what to cut when you are behind

Check the clock at 0:52. If the "what counts as a rep" beat has not started by 0:52, you are behind, and you cut in this order — never by improvising:

Order Cut Down to What you lose
1 Five public skills illustration 5 → 3 min: read the five, drop the examples E8 weakens to naming; P-11 still answerable
2 Four ordinary moments 4 → 3 min: name two, not four K-E2's account has less material to build on
3 Shift menu neighbour exchange 5 → 4 min: drop the "which do you already reach for" min Nothing measured
4 What counts as a rep 4 → 3 min: definition and normalising beat only, drop the volunteered example P-04b gets harder to answer honestly
5 Close 2 → 1 min Nothing measured

Never cut, in any circumstance: the 5-minute safeguarding block · the 10-minute drill · the 12-minute moment beat · the 8-minute full pass · the 9-minute Form 2 block. If you are more than five minutes behind at 0:52, you are running the 95-minute variant — tell the room, and finish at 1:35. Silently shortening E1, E7 or the forms invalidates the outcome claim and the primary measure at the same time, which is precisely the failure this rule exists to prevent.

B5 · The n=1 and the silent-room variants

Essentials is sold to teams of 1–15, and three beats use pairs. Every one has a stated alternative, given by default and not on request:

Beat Pair version Solo / silent-room version
K-E2 explain-back Say it to one person Write the sentence, read it to the facilitator
E1 shape check Two questions, yes/no Check your own against the two questions, printed on the slip
E7 say-it Next move to a neighbour Next move under your breath — named as equal, not a fallback

B6 · The booking checklist — four things the facilitator must know before arriving

None of this can be worked out in the room.

  1. Was Form 1 sent seven days ahead? If no → the 95-minute variant, with a 9-minute Form 1 block.
  2. Have the Form 1 nominations been aggregated into two or three themes? This is a real operational cost (D-0091 names it as one) and it must be done between the form closing and the session starting. If the response count is under five, do not reveal themes — say so plainly in the room and move to the individual write.
  3. The host agreement is signed, including the two standing prohibitions: no manager ever asks to see anyone's moment, and non-practice is never treated as a performance issue in a review, a one-to-one, or a joke. K-07 requires personal moments to stay private in organisational delivery; this is where that becomes enforceable.
  4. D-0016's six matters and the disclosure placeholder. Until they resolve, this is not deliverable to participants, and the placeholder must not go out unresolved.

Part C — what changes for the half day

Not a second plan. Everything in Part B runs as written unless named here.

Beats that extend

Beat Essentials Foundations What the extra time is actually for
Welcome and safeguarding 5 8 The same six controls delivered with room to answer a question, plus the hazard route named for that organisation up front rather than only at F3
Four moments / definition 4 (combined) 4 + 5 The definition is read against the room's own words on the wall, so it is a recognition rather than an assertion. This is why the opener exists
Shift menu → live toolkit 5 10 Two tools chosen by the room and actually tried in their seats, not described
What counts as a rep 4 5 Room to take two volunteered examples instead of one
Full pass 8 8 Unchanged — same activity, same minutes
Form 2 9 10 Two extra items (P-05b, P-12)

Beats that are added

Added beat Min Where Serves
Self-elicitation opener — butcher's paper per table, two prompts ("mental health" / "mental fitness"), sheets to the wall, room reads them in silence 10 0:12–0:22 The generation effect: the room produces the shape of the answer before hearing it. Charged here as an opener, not as a precondition for pair work — nothing supports that claim (C3-11). Facilitator circulates the whole time, reading over shoulders and prompting; that circulation is where the teaching starts, and it is why this runs on shared paper rather than private cards. That trade-off is a live safeguarding judgement, not settled by this document — it belongs with whoever reviews D-0016
HOS — the diagnostic question and Environment only 8 1:05–1:13 F3's lens. "What is shaping access in this moment?" Not all six components; nobody is asked to memorise anything
Experiential contrast + debrief 15 1:23–1:38 F2. Same moment twice — once without the skill, once with. Both versions end identically: still tired, phone in hand, thing still not done. The prompt is "what did you notice?", never "what was correct?" The second live State Check is folded into the debrief, unannounced. Run as a short pre-filmed clip, or two facilitators live if there is no screen. No participant volunteers
Our moments — reveal, ask, agree or decline 6 1:43–1:49 F5, as D-0091 built it. Reveal the themes; then a genuine low-stakes ask — does this room actually want to agree on one shared thing? If yes: one sentence, "when [this happens], we will [this]", written on everyone's worksheet next to their own moment, and someone named as owning it. If no, or unclear: say it out loud — "that's completely fine, plenty of rooms don't, write your own instead" — and move on. Nothing is pushed
Peer application, both roles 21 2:09–2:30 F1. 3 min model and limits; 7 min turn one; 7 min turn two; 4 min debrief on "what was harder about doing it with someone?" Opting out of pairs stated as normal before pairs are formed, with a solo written alternative offered by default
Enabling condition, the named ask, the hazard route 15 2:30–2:45 F3. Private write: the condition, the control test, the named person, the sentence, when. Then the hazard-routing beat to the whole room — where a problem goes if it is workload, safety or leadership rather than practice. Nothing read aloud, nothing collected

The break

One 15-minute break at 1:13 on the content clock — between the Mechanism block (HOS) and the toolkit. That is a real act-break in the session's story: the end of "what this is and how it works," before "now you use it." It is outside the 180 content minutes. Elapsed session = 3h15, plus arrival. Book the room for 3h30 and say so on the offerings page — a host booking three hours will run out of room before the peer beat.

What does not change

The locked wordings, the drill (10 minutes, same floor, same sets), the moment beat (12 minutes, same script, same stuck points), the full pass (8 minutes, same four lines, same minimum-viable version, still no hands-up), the cue beat, the close, the standing opt-out rules, and the booking checklist. Foundations' cut-order rule is the same list, checked at 2:09 instead of 0:52, with the contrast beat (15 min) inserted at position 1 — it is the most expensive beat with the weakest measurement, so it is the honest first thing to lose when a room over-runs.

Part D — cuts, sources, unresolved, and the founder's questions

D1 · What was cut, and why

Cut From Why
The six-component Human Operating System Essentials entirely; Foundations keeps only the diagnostic question and Environment Nothing in Essentials depends on the six components, and the existing guide already tells participants they are not expected to memorise them. Declared as a D-0014 deviation (§D2), because it removes the Mechanism block D-0003 fixes — not presented as a neutral trim
Three Radar moments → one Both The one-moment version is what the live 1-hour build already runs, recorded there as a named D-0014 deviation. Carried here as the same named deviation, not as a silent standard (§D2)
The Radar's second strand as a separate written line Both — both strands are offered, one moment is written Cutting "experience more fully" entirely would reframe mental fitness as damage control and contradict the proactive category claim. It is offered in the prompt and chosen by whoever wants it
P-10 — expected weekly frequency The instrument A leading item manufactured by the design: the session would have taught the target answer minutes earlier. L-032's exact failure, created fresh. Replaced by B-07 at Form 1, before the session shapes anything
The "twice a week" countability test E1 D-0010 — participants are not required to meet a frequency target, and a participant whose most important moment is a monthly review should not be told in a scripted exercise that it is the wrong shape
The public hands-up at E7 Essentials and Foundations It sorts a room into completers and partial-completers on a construct K-07 defines as outcome-independent, and it contaminates P-09 ninety seconds later
F-03 — "in how many did you get all the way through" Recommended for cutting; Hunter's call §D4, question 1
B-03, B-05, P-06 The instrument B-03/B-05 are concept recognition attached to no outcome in either format; P-06 is instrumentation whose only use is calibration against F-04, which survives. Their burden funds the five new production items — counted once, in §A5, not spent twice
ST-1 / ST-2 / ST-3 The instrument ST-2 is an intent item and no outcome depends on intent; ST-1/ST-3 are superseded by P-05 and F-07
Form 3 Q8 — "approximately how many Mental Reps" The instrument Already ruled out by Hunter directly. Not yet actioned in the live advisor draft; that edit goes through Eimear and Debra
The Leaders' Session Both Offer 1 formats D-0090 Proposal 2 — must not be retrofitted into Offer 1. Held as a separate offer (§A3)
"Also used for schools, public talks and keynotes" The format description K-08 control-state warnings, C-16: youth/schools blocked until the youth process is reviewed; external use "no until reviewed"; no named safeguarding lead. A line like that reads as authorisation once it is in a committee document
Pair-share on wall themes; the worked example between Radar halves; the guitar analogy; the "two things this doesn't mean" caveat pair Both The explain-back does the first job while serving an outcome; there are no longer two Radar halves; E6's normalising beat does the analogy's work with a real moment; the caveat pair is insurance, not teaching

What was NOT cut, against B1: the five public skills (restored, E8) · Our moments / Team Pulse (restored, F5 in Foundations, theme reveal in Essentials) · the safeguarding block's full length · the drill's full length.

D2 · The two D-0014 deviations this build declares

Neither is new behaviour; both were previously undeclared or declared for only one format.

Deviation 1 — one Radar moment, not three (D-0010). D-0010's approved structure is "three meaningful moments → one possible next move for each." Both formats here write one. Reason: in a 90-minute session, three moments produce three unfinished ones — a near-empty sheet with three blank slots reads as failure, one slot filled reads as complete; and the follow-up asks about a single named moment, so three make the answer ambiguous. D-0010 itself records three as an MFC design choice, never an evidence-validated number, and the live 1-hour build already carries this deviation. Scope: both Offer 1 formats. Not a change to D-0010; if Hunter prefers, a decision record supersedes it instead.

Deviation 2 — Essentials has no distinct Mechanism block (D-0003). D-0003 fixes the five phases Orientation → Skills → Mechanism → Revisiting/Connecting → Application, and the Human Operating System is what carries Mechanism. Essentials teaches no HOS. Reason: 90 minutes cannot carry the HOS and produce E1, E7 and the drill at their floors; the one line Mechanism must deliver — state changes what is available to you, not only how you feel — is delivered inside E4, so the phase's function survives without its block. Scope: Essentials only; Foundations runs Mechanism as a named 8-minute block in the fixed order. Declared rather than assumed, because D-0018 requires a decision record for an essential-function change and this is at minimum adjacent to one — if Hunter reads the five phases as essential functions rather than structure, a decision record is owed here and the deviation does not substitute for it.

Essentials' Our-moments treatment is not a new deviation — it is D-0091's own approved treatment of the short format, carried across.

D3 · The decision record that would be needed for cardinal counting — drafted, not adopted

Not required by this chain, which uses D-0017's approved binary-plus-band form. Drafted so the choice is real rather than rhetorical. Reserve the ID with the governed tool at the point of adoption; do not assume one.

D-[reserve at adoption] — Cardinal opportunity and attempt counts at follow-up Decision. Form 3's F-01 and F-02 ask for counts (0–20+) rather than D-0017's approved binary-plus-opportunity form, so the primary outcome can be reported as a ratio (F-02 ÷ F-01) rather than as a proportion of participants. Why. A ratio distinguishes "acted on two of two opportunities" from "acted on two of ten," which a binary cannot; it is the strongest single defence against the ceiling problem that made the nearest published instrument unable to detect its own intervention. What it costs, stated. The participant computes their own failure rate in the act of answering ("five came up, I did one"), at the exact moment D-0008's follow-up is meant to work as a lapse-and-return door rather than a check-up. No feedback protection removes this — it is self-administered. A recall tally over a fortnight is also the weakest kind of self-report. What it does not do. It does not reintroduce a rep count as a performance measure; it remains opportunity-conditional and attempt-based, never fed back, never ranked. Supersedes D-0017 item 2's binary threshold for Form 3's F-01/F-02 only. Requires cognitive testing of both items before the first cohort — this is exactly the item class the forms draft already names as testing priority.

D4 · The questions only Hunter can answer

Each arrives with a recommendation and a confidence, per the standing autonomy standard. None of them blocks the session plan — Part B runs as written under every answer.

1. F-03 — cut it? Recommendation: cut. Confidence: high. K-07's locked Mental Rep definition says "the outcome does not determine whether it counts." F-03 — "in how many did you get all the way through" — is a completion standard applied to a unit defined as outcome-independent. It is the one place the instrument contradicts a locked record. F-02 is attempt-based and fully compatible, and nothing in this chain uses F-03: the primary outcome, E6, E7 and P-09 all work without it. What is lost if it goes: the gap between starting and finishing, which the forms draft calls the place the design learns most. That is real, and it can be recovered later as a facilitator-side or case-study question rather than a graded item on every participant. This is a framework question, which is why it is yours and not this system's.

2. Cardinal counts, or bands? Recommendation: bands. Confidence: high. Opportunity-conditioning itself is not a founder question — D-0017 approved it, and the "don't count reps" instruction was given with that architecture already in force. The narrow real question is binary/band versus cardinal tally. Bands preserve the entire ratio logic, defeat the ceiling problem identically, cannot be described as counting reps by anyone including a sceptical committee member, and need no new decision record. If you want the tally, §D3 is the record.

3. Is the Leaders' Session an Offer 2 product, and does the Foundations embedding promise survive without it? Recommendation: keep it in Offer 2; soften the embedding promise. Confidence: moderate. D-0090 decides the first half — leader modelling must not be retrofitted into a standalone workshop. The consequence is commercial and it is yours: Foundations' F3 produces a named person and a sentence, and without a leader who knows what is coming, that request lands cold. Either the offerings page stops promising "help embedding it" for standalone Foundations, or the Leaders' Session becomes a condition of booking it. F3 itself stands either way — its hazard-routing half is what makes it safe, and that does not depend on a leader.

4. Is Essentials ever delivered to schools, youth, or public/keynote audiences? Recommendation: no, until C-16 and the youth process are reviewed and a safeguarding lead is named. Confidence: high. Currently blocked in K-08's control-state warnings. B1's format description named schools in its second line; that has been removed rather than qualified.

5. K6 — is the knowing–doing-gap outcome approved? It is marked "Proposed — requires Hunter's approval under D-0018" and was never approved, yet B-06 already measures it and K-E2 is now a seven-minute beat in both formats. Recommendation: approve it. It is the outcome that makes the whole product make sense, and the instrument has been assuming it for some time.

D5 · Records that conflict — named, not silently reconciled

  1. K-08's audience-translation table versus K-07's amended staged arc and D-0091. K-08's Workshops row still reads "the five public skills are named from Stage 2." K-07's staged-arc section, amended 2026-08-09 under D-0091, states that for a standalone session Stage 1 and Stage 2 collapse and the workshop legitimately teaches the full five. Resolved here toward K-07/D-0091 — K-07 governs Framework meaning and D-0091 is the later, specific decision — but K-08's row is now stale and should be amended to match. That is a one-line fix to a foundations record and it is not made here.
  2. D-0003's fixed five phases versus a 90-minute session. Declared as Deviation 2 (§D2) rather than resolved by assertion.
  3. D-0010's three moments versus one. Declared as Deviation 1 (§D2).
  4. The formats that exist versus the formats being sold. Every built artefact is a 3-hour or 1-hour session; the offerings ladder sells 90 minutes and a half day. This document is the bridge, and it is a design document, not a facilitator guide — the existing 1,644-line guide still follows the old arc and does not describe either product on the price list.
  5. D-0091's day-10–14 reminder to the shared-commitment owner is drafted and explicitly not wired into the Form 3 send infrastructure. Do not describe it as running.

D6 · What remains unresolved

  • D-0016's six safeguarding matters are open. Nothing here is deliverable to participants until they resolve, and the disclosure placeholder must not go out unresolved. This build increases disclosure exposure in two specific places over the current builds, and that has not been reassessed: E6 asks participants to recall a time something went badly, and F3 raises workload and psychosocial hazards explicitly. Both belong in Items 1–2's clinical-governance review.
  • The privacy, consent, de-identification and linkage protocol is the blocker, overdue since 31 July. It gates the build and the send of every item named here.
  • The measurement instrument is unapproved and untested. B-07, P-01b, P-02b, P-04b, P-05b, P-09, P-11, P-12, F-11 and F-12 are new here. None has been through Eimear Quigley or Debra Fidler, none has been cognitively tested, and the forms draft's own seven-step approval path applies to all of them.
  • No claim level is board-approved. Every claim boundary in this document is a boundary against an unapproved ceiling.
  • Participant materials do not exist for this recut — moment slip, full-pass sheet, token card, take-home card, shift-menu card. All are referenced in Part B; none is designed.
  • The facilitator script does not exist. Part B's [SAY] lines are the intent and the wording, written to be runnable, but they are not the full guide, and the two hardest pieces of facilitation — K-E2's causal account and E7's modelled pass — carry a script here for the first time and have never been delivered.
  • F2's contrast beat has no item (C3-05), disclosed rather than solved.
  • Nothing here has been tested with a real audience, in either format. No pilot has run.

D7 · Every record relied on

K-07 (locked — Stop–Shift–Do, State Check, Mental Rep's locked definition and its outcome-independence, the five public skills' locked wording, the Shift menu, the Radar and its binding constraints, the staged arc as amended by D-0091, supporting others as peer support) · K-08 (claim boundaries; safety rules 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12; the claim ladder; control-state warnings and C-16) · D-0003 (five phases; six essential-content items introduced in-session) · D-0004 (mandatory retrieval element; explanatory feedback, never correctness-only) · D-0005 (context-neutral framing) · D-0008 (cue and transfer path; lapse-and-return) · D-0010 (Radar target structure; no frequency target) · D-0014 (essential/flexible taxonomy and the deviation mechanism) · D-0015 (six universal minimum controls; alternative to any public disclosure) · D-0016 (safeguarding gate — open) · D-0017 (measurement architecture; opportunity-conditional binary threshold) · D-0018 (essential-function changes require a decision record and Hunter's approval) · D-0054 (traffic light named once, as contrast) · D-0056 (two-format build; case-study extended wave) · D-0083 (Shift toolkit; breath is one option, not required) · D-0090 (leader modelling scoped to Offer 2; the struck Mas & Moretti citation; no forced consensus) · D-0091 (staged-arc exception; Team Pulse compressed into the two live touchpoints; workshop-package.html is what MFC runs today).

Where this document infers rather than follows a record: the 90/180 allocation of outcomes between formats; the specific minute values of every beat that is not a stated floor; E8's mapping job for the five skills; F3's shape (enabling condition → control test → named person → sentence → F-12); B-07's banded wording; and the claim that E6 protects the primary measure by making "even partly, even badly" answerable. All are reasoning, not findings.

Original source: 60-projects/committee-pack-v1/B2-outcome-chain-and-session-plan.md

B3 Session Plan Final Draft

B3 — The outcome chain and the session plan

What this is. B2's chain and plan with every C4 finding closed or explicitly rejected on evidence, every time floor and every duration reconciled beat by beat against the live build (workshop-package.html), a cut-order rule that works at the moment a facilitator can still use it, a consent script that is true of everything the session actually collects, and the D-0018 decision records that three altered essential functions actually require.

Three things B2 got wrong that this document does not repeat.

  1. B2 cited design-of-record numbers while claiming to have checked the live build. Every duration in this document now carries its live-build source, in §0. Where a proposed duration is more than the live build gives, it is marked PROPOSED +n. Where it is less, it is marked PROPOSED −n with a reason. Nothing is presented as "what MFC already does" unless the live build actually does it.
  2. B2 used D-0014 as design-time authority. It is not. D-0014 is a facilitator-side deviation mechanism for departures that arise in delivery. The only use of D-0014 in this document is one recorded delivery-time drill deviation at the bottom of the cut-order rule (§B4) — which is exactly what it is for. Design-time changes to essential functions go through D-0018, in §D2.
  3. B2's opening consent line was false. It is rewritten in §B, checked item by item against Form 1, Form 2, Form 3, the four linkage-code items and the facilitator delivery record.

Two things carried forward from B2 unchanged, because C4 verified them: the outcome-chain format, and the arithmetic discipline. Every clock in this document is added up in the open.

Part 0 — Every time floor and duration, reconciled against the live build

How to read this. "Live 1-hour" and "Live 3-hour" are the two formats in workshop-package.html. The two products in this document — Essentials, 90 minutes and Foundations, 180 content minutes — do not exist in the live build; this is the bridge between what is built and what is on the price list, and every minute of difference is declared.

What "floor" means here, stated precisely. D-0004 mandates "one recall-based retrieval element… operating in the Revisiting/Connecting phase" and sets no duration at all. D-0015 mandates six universal minimum controls and sets no duration. No decision record in this system fixes a minute value for anything. Every "floor" below is therefore MFC's own product floor for this format, defended by argument, not a number quoted from a governing record. B2 blurred that line and C4 inherited the blur; it is unblurred here.

The drill correction, in full — this is the finding B2 failed on

B2 stated twice that "the live 60-minute build gives it 10 and calls it the single largest allocation in the format." The live 60-minute build gives it 6. Verbatim, from the file:

0:26 – 0:32 · Drill it — full pace, both sets · tag: 8 → 6 min "Tightened from the first cut, but still the largest single practice block of the hour."

The "10 minutes" came from 12-one-hour-delivery-kit.md — a design-of-record file — via C3-08. That is the exact class of source C3 said B1 failed by relying on, carried into a document whose whole claim to authority was that it had checked the live build.

C4's own figure is also wrong, in the other direction, and from the same class of source. C4 §1.3 states "the live 3-hour gives the drill 15 minutes" and reasons from it that Foundations takes "a third off the protected element." The live 3-hour gives it 12 — beat 1:32–1:44, confirmed independently by the outcome card that describes "the twelve-minute choral drill at 1:32." The reduction was real but it was 12 → 10, not 15 → 10.

Resolution. Foundations runs the drill at 12 minutes, matching the live 3-hour exactly, so no reduction to a D-0014-protected element occurs and no record is owed for it. Essentials runs it at 10, declared as PROPOSED +4 over the live short format — an increase to a protected element, which needs no authorisation. The two minutes Foundations needs come from the moment beat, whose theme reveal has moved to F5 (C4 §2.4 item 2 — the same two minutes B2 left unattached).

Three source conflicts found while reconciling, named rather than silently chosen

  1. WHO-5. The live build's measurement tab carries WHO-5 as a "required wellbeing measure" in Form 1 and Form 3. The 2026-08-10 forms draft removes it: "Not included in this draft… it also measures how someone is doing — mental health — which is the thing our own definition says mental fitness is not." This plan follows the 2026-08-10 draft (it is the later, and it is the document under review), and the consent script does not promise a wellbeing measure. If WHO-5 returns, Form 1's timing note and the consent script's burden line both change.
  2. Email. The live build's Form 1 opens with an "Evaluation email address" field. The 2026-08-10 draft states "email is removed from the instrument entirely… no identifier ever exists." This plan follows the 2026-08-10 draft. The consent script at §B says there is no email anywhere on the forms. If the live v0.10 email field survives advisor review, that sentence becomes false and must be changed before delivery. Flagged, not assumed away.
  3. The linkage code contradicts its own design rule. The forms draft's validation reasoning is explicit — "never ask someone to count letters. Ask the fact and extract it in software" — and its first code item is "the first two letters of your mother's first name." That is a letter-extraction item sitting directly under the rule that bans them. It is not this document's to fix; it goes to Eimear and Debra with the rest. Every three-week figure depends on it.

Part A — the outcome chain

The measurement constraint, restated

The primary outcome is D-0017's approved architecture in its approved form: an opportunity-conditional, binary, attempt-based initial-use threshold — "at least one reported attempted application," with an opportunity item so "didn't practise" is never confused with "had no opportunity."

  • F-01 (banded, revised): "In the last seven days, did the moment you chose come up? Not at all / once or twice / most days / not sure."
  • F-02 (binary, revised): "Did you run the three steps in any of them — even partly, even badly? Yes / no."
  • Skip and denominator rules, fixed now (closing C4 §6's first defect): F-01 governs. A respondent answering "not at all" or "not sure" is routed past F-02 and sits outside the denominator, reported in its own named cell. F-02's "there was no relevant moment" option is removed — it duplicated F-01 and created a cell with no governing rule.
  • Primary outcome: the proportion of participants who had an opportunity and attempted at least once, reported inside its own denominator and its band, with the "not at all", "not sure" and unmatched counts printed beside it.

This is a change to the 2026-08-10 forms draft, stated as one. That draft asks F-01/F-02/F-03 as cardinal counts and makes the primary outcome the ratio F-02 ÷ F-01. The revision above moves toward D-0017's approved form and away from the draft's; it is more compliant, not less, but it is a proposal for Eimear and Debra, not a correction of an error. The record that would authorise the cardinal alternative instead is drafted at §D3.

F-03 is used by no outcome in this chain. See §D4 question 1 — a founder decision, recommended for cutting, and flagged, not decided here.

Format 1 — Essentials, 90 minutes

Talk-led with real practice in the room. The bar: one moment, one full pass, one tool, one cue.

Room size, reconciled (C4 §2.3, §7 item 9): Essentials is sold to teams of 1–20 and the plan is written for 8–20 seated so everyone can turn to a neighbour. Below 8, and at n=1, the solo variants in §B5 are the default rather than the alternative. Foundations is 12–20.

Delivery mode, declared (C4 §7 item 8): both formats as specified here are in-person only. The drill keeps the live build's online variant because that variant is already built; a full online Essentials is a separate design task, and it would have to carry the live 1-hour's own online provisions — captions on by default, no registration gate before the privacy notice, 12–25 participants — none of which is designed for the pair beats, the board narrowing, the moment slip or the full-pass sheet.

(Adult workplace and community audiences only. Schools, youth, public talks and keynotes are out of scope — K-08's control-state warnings and C-16 block them pending review, and no safeguarding lead is named.)

E1 — Names one recurring moment from their own week, specific enough to recognise when it arrives

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes one moment stated as a situation with a place and a trigger — "when my daughter asks for the iPad at dinner," not "stress" — and confirms with a neighbour, or against the two printed questions, that it has both.
Its job It is the participant's cue, so it carries the transfer path (D-0008); and it is the unit F-01 asks about. It is not required to recur at any frequency (D-0010: the Radar is "a personal map, not a three-part compliance task").
Content required The word Radar named as a thing a person has (closing C4 §1.5's residual — it is one of D-0003's six essential-content items and B2 introduced it in function but never in name). K-07's Radar prompt verbatim. One worked narrowing of a vague moment, modelled live. The two named stuck points, each scripted. Both Radar strands offered; one moment written.
Activity, with minutes 10 min. 3 min facilitator narrows one vague moment live on the board. 5 min private silent write — the moment, and which of the five skills it asks for (E8's 60 seconds is funded here, closing C4 §2.3; B2 left it unfunded inside a 4-minute write). 2 min shape check in pairs, on format only: "Does it name a place? Does it name a trigger?" Solo alternative stated before pairs form.
Items P-08 (post, existing) — "Write the one recurring moment you have chosen to work on." Scored for form only. B-07 (NEW, Form 1, pre-session), rewritten — see below.
Claim boundary (K-08) Licenses: "participants leave having chosen and written one specific moment from their own life." Does not license that they have a practice or a habit.

B-07, rewritten so it can be answered cold (closing C4 §1.7). B2's version — "how often do you face situations like these" — had no antecedent on a form sent seven days before the session. Revised:

B-07. "In a typical week, how often do you run into a situation you'd like to have handled better — a conversation that goes sideways, something you keep putting off, a moment where stress or frustration gets ahead of you? Not at all / once or twice / most days / not sure."

And it is stated as an abandonment, not a relocation. B2's crosswalk claimed countability "moves to a facilitator-side shape check plus B-07." It does not. The shape check is restricted to place-and-trigger and forbidden from asking frequency; B-07 asks about a generic class, not the participant's own chosen moment. Nothing in this design checks how often the chosen moment recurs. That is the right answer under D-0010, which prohibits a frequency target — but it is a thing given up, and B-07 is baseline context for F-01, not a replacement for it.

Our moments in Essentials — the in-room reveal is dropped. B2 added a 2-minute anonymous theme reveal and attributed it to D-0091. D-0091 §"The 1-hour format" gives the short format collection and host handover only, and the live build's own change list, item 08, reads: "What changes: Nothing in the one-hour room." B2 attributed a new beat to an approval that says the opposite. Closed by dropping the beat. The Form 1 nomination item is still collected in both formats, the facilitator still aggregates it, and the anonymised theme list still goes to the host — exactly as D-0091 provides. Adding it back to the room would cost 2 minutes from a clock with no slack, make pre-session aggregation a hard dependency of the short format, and require its own decision record; the draft is at §D2, note 3, unadopted.

K-E2 — Accounts for the knowing–doing gap in their own words, without MFC's vocabulary

Field Content
Observable behaviour Says to one other person, in one or two sentences, why someone who knows what would help still does the other thing — using none of MFC's words.
Its job It makes the definition land as an answer to a problem the room is holding. It earns Stop.
Content required A plain account of ordinary experience. Delivered as description a participant recognises, never as science — no brain diagrams, no amygdala, no fight-or-flight, and no route/pathway language (see the claim correction below).
Activity, with minutes 7 min. 4 min facilitator account, built on one of the four moments named just before. 3 min explain-back to one other person, or written alone.
Items B-06 (existing, all timepoints) — the scenario item. P-01b (NEW, post, free text, one line) — "In one sentence: why does someone who knows what would help still do the other thing?" ~30 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can account for the gap between knowing and doing in their own words." Does not license any claim about mechanism or brain change, and does not license that understanding the gap closes it.

Claim correction (C4 §5.1), applied to the script. B2's [SAY] line was "the old route is faster because it's been used more" — a neural-pathway claim in plain clothes, in a beat whose own boundary forbids mechanism claims, and K-08 bars "rewiring the brain" outright with mechanism sitting at Level 3, pending. Replaced throughout with the experience-level version: "whatever you've done most is what turns up first." B2's "That's it. That's the whole problem" is also cut — a flat sufficiency claim about the cause of the knowing–doing gap, and the sentence a committee member would quote back.

Authority flag, carried forward unresolved. This is K6 in 10-product-finalisation-v1/02-design-rationale-and-outcomes-checklist.md, marked "Proposed — requires Hunter's approval under D-0018", never approved, while B-06 already measures it. §D4 question 5.

E3 — Says what each of the three steps means, unprompted, without the colours

Field Content
Observable behaviour Given "Stop, Shift, Do" and nothing else, states what each one is: catch the moment; create enough space where useful and available; make the next move with intention.
Its job Retrieval under load. A step recognised on a slide but not producible in a car park is not available in a real moment.
Content required K-07's locked wording, verbatim. The traffic light named exactly once, as contrast (D-0054), then the three corrections taught as their own items. Stop taught as the pivot. Explanatory feedback, never correctness-only (D-0004).
Activity, with minutes 7 min teach + 10 min drill (Essentials) / 12 min drill (Foundations). See §0 for the live-build reconciliation of both figures. Choral call-and-response, whole room as one voice, nobody cold-called. Two sets alternating, finishing on Set B.
Items P-02 (post, existing). P-02b (NEW, post, free text) — "What does Shift mean? Don't use the colours." ~30 s. F-04 (3 weeks, existing).
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants could state the three steps and what each means, and X% reported recalling them during a real moment at three weeks." Does not license that they used them well, or that recall predicts use.

Scoring guidance, not room language (closing C4 §5.5). "Answering 'red, amber, green' is a fail" is a marking rule for P-02b only. It must never be said in the room, where the standing line is "there is no correct move here, and I'm not going to grade one." Marked as such wherever it appears.

E4 — Reads their own state as too much / too little / workable, for a specific moment

Field Content
Observable behaviour Verifiable: says why "workable" is not "calm" — it is about what choice is available, not how pleasant it feels. Delivered but unverifiable by design: one silent State Check in the room, never shared, never collected, never scored (K-08 rule 7).
Its job The only sanctioned self-assessment language MFC has, and the precondition for Shift meaning anything.
Content required The three words with the anchor phrase "for this moment" every time; the lock-in that State Check is not a fourth step; and the access idea — state changes what is available to you, not only how you feel.
Activity, with minutes 5 min. 3.5 min teach, ~1.5 min live silent check.
Items P-03 (post, existing).
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can state what workable means and distinguish it from calm, and were given one silent opportunity to apply it to themselves." Does not license that they can use the state language on a real moment of their own — nothing verifies the silent half. No claim about emotion regulation or physiological change.

E5 — Names one shift move, in their own words, for the moment they chose

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes a concrete move in their own words — "stand up and walk to the kitchen before I answer" — not a menu name and not "breathing".
Content required The Shift menu as a menu to pick from, not a taxonomy to learn — Move it / Zoom in or out / Ask a different question / Bring someone in. K-07: "Facilitators should use the menu names aloud, not the bare category words" — the bare category words are body, attention, perspective, connection, which is what must not be said. The claims boundary said aloud: breath is one option, not the required strategy (D-0083).
Activity, with minutes 5 min. 2 min menu named with one example each. 2 min private write. 1 min optional to a neighbour.
Items P-05 (post, existing). F-07 (3 weeks, existing) — naming something MFC never taught is a success at F-07, not a failure.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants left with a self-worded, retrievable move, and X% reported using something at three weeks." Does not license that any tool works or that MFC's tools were the ones used.

C4 §2.6's third finding is rejected on the record. C4 reported that the script "contradicts its own instruction" by leading each item with the bare category word. It does not: "Move it", "Zoom in or out", "Ask a different question" and "Bring someone in" are the menu names, and K-07 line 661 is explicit that they are what should be said aloud — "since 'attention' is also deep-tier vocabulary." B2's script was correct and is kept as written.

E6 — States what counts as a rep, including one that went badly

Field Content
Observable behaviour Says that a rep counts when the moment was caught with intention, whatever the outcome.
Its job Outcome-independence is what makes F-02 answerable honestly: "even partly, even badly" only works if the room has been told partly and badly count.
Content required K-07's locked definition, verbatim. What does not count: a moment by itself; a habit on autopilot; reading about it. The normalising beat.
Activity, with minutes 4 min. 2 min definition and normalising beat. 2 min: "think of a time this week you caught something and it still went badly." At most one volunteered aloud, never solicited by name, and capped — see §B7.
Items P-04 (post, existing). P-04b (NEW, post) — "Think of a rep you ran that didn't go the way you wanted. Did it still count? Yes / no." ~30 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can distinguish a rep from information or an accident, and can identify a rep that did not go well as still counting." Does not license any claim about practice volume.

E7 — Attempts all three steps on their own chosen moment, in the room

Renamed from B2's "Runs all three steps," and this is not cosmetic — see the P-09 correction below. The live build already ends on an actual rep: the 1-hour format's "Do one, right now" beat at 0:38–0:41, added 2026-08-05, carrying Baldwin & Ford and Bandura, mapped in the build's own traceability table to Form 2 Q7. This is not a discovered hole. E7 improves that existing beat in two respects: all three steps, and on the participant's own chosen moment, written eight minutes earlier. The 3-hour build's Application phase genuinely has no equivalent beat.

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes on their own moment: the moment / what the Stop looks like here / my state read / my next move — then says the next move out loud to themselves or a neighbour. Two of the four lines is a complete attempt, stated aloud before they start.
Its job The in-room analogue of F-02, which makes "even partly, even badly" refer to something they have already done once.
Activity, with minutes 8 min. 2 min modelled. 5 min private, silent, written. 1 min: say the next move out loud. No public hands-up — it sorts the room into completers and partial-completers on a construct K-07 defines as outcome-independent, and it contaminates P-09.
Items P-09 (NEW, post), reworded — see below.
Claim boundary Licenses: "X% of participants reported attempting all three steps on a moment of their own before leaving the room." Does not license competence, habit or transfer. One rehearsed pass in a supported room is not one pass in a real moment, and the two must never be reported in the same number.

P-09 no longer grades completion (closing C4 §6's second defect, which is defect 3 of this correction pass). B2's script authorised a two-line pass at 1:10 and then asked, at 1:21, "did you run all three steps? Yes / no" — so a participant who did exactly what the facilitator sanctioned had to tick no. Worse, B2 recommended cutting F-03 precisely because "a completion standard applied to a unit defined as outcome-independent" contradicts K-07's locked definition — and then rebuilt F-03 in the room, on the same construct. Revised:

P-09. "Today, did you have a go at running the three steps on a moment of your own — even partly? Yes / no."

The [SAY] line at 1:06 is matched to it word for word (§B). F-03 remains flagged as a founder decision (§D4 question 1) and is not decided here.

E8 — Says which of the five public skills their own moment mainly asks for

D-0003 fixes all six essential-content items as first introduced within the session, and the five public skills are one of them. K-07's amended staged-arc section and D-0091 resolve the Stage 1 / Stage 2 question: for a standalone session — the only contact this audience gets — Stage 1 and Stage 2 collapse and the session legitimately teaches the full five skills, full State Check and the full Shift menu. K-08's audience-translation table still reads "the five public skills are named from Stage 2" and is now stale; named in §D5, not silently chosen.

Field Content
Observable behaviour Given the five labels in locked wording, says which one their own written moment mainly asks of them, and why, in one line.
Content required K-07's locked wording, one short line each: Notice · Shift · Choose · Focus · Connect. The seven deep skills stay out (Stage 3 holds).
Activity, with minutes 4 min teach, plus 60 seconds funded inside E1's 5-minute write.
Items P-11 (NEW, post) — "Which of the five does your moment mainly ask for, and why?" ~30 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can map a real moment of their own to one of the five public skills." Does not license that they can distinguish all five, define them, or use them.

Phase mapping (D-0003). Orientation 0:00–0:21 (welcome, forms, the four moments and the definition, the gap and the explain-back) · Skills 0:21–0:37 (five skills, Stop–Shift–Do, State Check) · Mechanism — absent, and a D-0018 record is drafted for it at §D2 · Revisiting/ Connecting 0:37–0:56 (the drill, the Shift menu, what counts as a rep) · Application 0:56–1:30.

D-0004's recall-based retrieval element sits at the head of Revisiting/Connecting, where the decision puts it. B2 mapped Skills as 0:20–0:52, which swallowed the drill and put the retrieval element inside the wrong phase — that was a mapping error, not a beat that moved. Under the corrected mapping nothing in Essentials has to move. This is stated openly so a reviewer can disagree with it: if Hunter reads the phase order as requiring the retrieval element to follow a Mechanism block that Essentials does not have, then the record at §D2 note 3 is owed and is drafted.

Format 2 — Foundations, half day (180 content min + 15 min break)

Foundations carries every Essentials outcome unchanged. What follows is only what the extra time buys. The rule: an outcome belongs here only if it cannot be produced in 90 minutes — because it needs a partner, a second person's material, a felt contrast, or a conversation the room has to prepare. "More content" is not a reason.

F1 — Runs the three steps on another person's moment, out loud, in both roles

Field Content
Observable behaviour In a pair, takes both roles; then names one thing that was harder about doing it with someone than alone.
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it Two turns plus a debrief. A one-turn version rehearses half the skill. 21 minutes minimum.
Content required K-07's "supporting others" table. The binding limits as content, not caveat: offer, never force (K-08 r6); peer support, not treatment (r2); knowing when to stop and bring in more support is part of the skill (r10). Opting out stated as normal before pairs form, with a solo written alternative offered by default.
Activity, with minutes 21 min. 3 model and limits · 7 turn one · 7 turn two · 4 debrief.
Items P-12 (NEW, post) — "Today, did you take someone else through the three steps? Both roles / one role / no — I worked alone." F-11 (NEW, 3 weeks), optional one line.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants practised the sequence as peer support, and X% reported using it with another person at three weeks." Does not license anything about team culture, relationships, psychological safety, or that MFC delivers support to third parties.

F2 — Picks a shift move that fits the specific moment, having run the contrast

Field Content
Observable behaviour States which move fits this moment and why another does not; and names one thing they noticed between the version run without the skill and the version run with it.
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it Two tools actually tried (10 min) plus the contrast and debrief (15 min). 25 minutes.
Content required The four categories with the downshift/upshift rule. Two tools tried live. The contrast both times ending identically — still tired, phone in hand, the thing still not done. Facilitator asks what participants noticed, never what was correct.
Items P-05 plus P-05b (NEW, post) — "Why that one, for that moment?" ~45 s. F-07 unchanged.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants selected a tool for a specific moment and can say why." P-05b measures reasoning about fit; it does not evidence the felt contrast, and the contrast run is a delivered activity with no item of its own. Disclosed: the most expensive fifteen minutes in Foundations cannot be distinguished in the data from a room that skipped it.

F3 — Names the enabling condition their moment depends on, and who they have to ask

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes: the enabling condition; whether it is inside their control or someone else's; if someone else's, the named person, the sentence they will say, and when. Separately, states where a problem goes if it is a workload, safety or leadership problem rather than a practice problem.
Its job The beat that opens the collective layer is the beat that closes the door on reframing a psychosocial hazard as a skill deficit. K-07: "a shared or team Radar must never be used to reframe harmful workload, unsafe leadership or psychosocial hazards as individual skill deficits. A route must exist for structural issues."
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it Diagnostic lens (8) then write and route (15). Compressed, it becomes a slogan about environment with no named person and no route — worse than not raising it.
Content required The Human Operating System's diagnostic question and the Environment component only. The enabling-conditions layer. That an Our moment requires genuine agreement. The hazard route, named concretely for that organisation, agreed with the host before the session.
Items F-12 (NEW, 3 weeks) — "You wrote down one thing you would ask someone for. Did you ask? Yes / no / not yet / it stopped being relevant."
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants identified an enabling condition and X% reported making the request at three weeks." Does not license anything about culture, norms, absenteeism or productivity. MFC has no organisational measurement instrument.

F5 — The room agrees one shared "when X, we will Y" commitment, or declines it out loud

D-0091's decided-and-built beat. This is the only place the theme reveal happens in either format (closing C4 §2.4 item 1 — B2's Part C left it running twice).

Field Content
Observable behaviour Either the room states one shared commitment as "when [this happens], we will [this]", written on each worksheet next to the participant's own moment — or the room declines, out loud, and moves on. Both are successful outcomes.
Activity, with minutes 6 min. 2 min anonymous theme reveal · 1 min genuine read of the room · then either 3 min drafting the sentence and naming who owns it, or "that's completely fine, plenty of rooms don't" and straight on.
Items No participant item, deliberately. The commitment, its wording and its named owner go on the facilitator delivery record. For case-study cohorts, reviewed at D-0056's extended wave. D-0091's day-10–14 templated reminder is drafted and not wired into the send infrastructure — do not describe it as running.
Claim boundary Licenses: "the room agreed one shared commitment" or "the room declined one" — a facilitator record of what happened in a room. Does not license anything about norms, culture, or that the commitment was kept.

F4 is deleted as a separate outcome. The five skills are E8 in both formats.

The wall-clock column closes C4 §2.5. B2 published content-clock times only and then issued operational instructions against them, so a facilitator with a wall clock was fifteen minutes wrong from the break onward. Every operational instruction in this document — including every cut-order checkpoint — is stated on both clocks.

Phase mapping (D-0003). Orientation 0:00–0:39 · Skills 0:39–0:55 · Mechanism 0:55–1:03 · Revisiting/Connecting 1:03–1:50 (drill, toolkit, contrast, what counts as a rep, Our moments) · Application 1:50–3:00. Skills precedes Mechanism, which is the fixed order; and D-0004's retrieval element now opens Revisiting/Connecting, where the decision puts it. This is a genuine restoration, not a re-labelling: the drill has moved to after the break (it was at 0:50–1:00, inside Skills, in B2). Retrieval after a spacing gap is also the stronger version of the mechanism, so the move costs nothing pedagogically.
