Here those 2 minutes are visibly the drill's.

A3 — The Leaders' Session is a separate offer, not part of either format

D-0090 Proposal 2: leader modelling "is an Offer 2 requirement and must not be retrofitted into Offer 1." Removed from both Offer 1 formats. Held as its own product, not built here. Four things must be true first: its evidential basis has to be rebuilt (the struck Mas & Moretti reasoning is not used); it needs a fifth instrument that does not exist; it cannot be anonymous at n=1–3, and the reporting floors — no report under 20, no subgroup under 10 — make single-organisation leader data unreportable; and the one prohibition worth carrying regardless belongs in the host agreement, signed before the session: a manager must never ask to see anyone's moment, and non-practice is never treated as a performance issue. §B6.

Consequence for Foundations, stated. F3 produces a named person and a sentence. Without a leader who knows what is coming, that request lands cold. F3 stands anyway — its hazard-routing half is what makes it safe and that does not depend on a leader — but the embedding promise on the offerings page does. §D4 question 3.

A5 — Burden arithmetic, shown, now including the linkage code

Baseline from the forms draft: Form 2 today = 12 items ≈ 8 min (B-03…B-06, P-01…P-08), ≈40 s per item. Form 3 = 10 items ≈ 6 min.

Form 2, Essentials. Cut B-03 and B-05 −80 s. Cut P-06 −40 s. Add P-01b 30 s, P-02b 30 s, P-04b 30 s, P-09 20 s, P-11 30 s = +140 s. 480 − 120 + 140 = 500 s ≈ 8.3 min → 9 minutes budgeted. 14 items.

Form 2, Foundations. Plus P-05b (45 s) and P-12 (20 s) = 565 s ≈ 9.4 min → 10 minutes. 16 items.

Form 3. Cut F-03 (§D4 q1) −1 item. Essentials 9 items ≈ 5.5 min. Foundations adds F-11 and F-12 with optional one-line free text: 11 items ≈ 7 min. A ~15% increase on the instrument whose response rate carries every durability claim MFC will make — disclosed, and the reason both free texts are optional.

Form 1. Adds B-07 (~20 s) and the nomination item (~30 s), plus the four linkage-code items (~40 s), which B2 omitted entirely (C4 §2.2). ≈5 min → ≈6.5 min.

In-room linkage block. The four code items are also read aloud and collected in the 0:05–0:10 block for anyone completing Form 1 in the room, and the token-card code is written on Form 2. This is why that block is 5 minutes, not 4.

All of this is arithmetic on the forms draft's own estimates. Nothing has been timed with real participants, and none of the new items has been through Eimear Quigley or Debra Fidler or been cognitively tested.

Part B — the Essentials session plan, beat by beat

Written so a facilitator who has never seen this can run it. [SAY] lines are the intent and the wording, not a script to read verbatim — except where marked verbatim, which are the locked or safeguarding lines.

Before the room: §B6's booking checklist must be complete. This session is not deliverable to participants until D-0016's six safeguarding matters resolve. The disclosure placeholder must not go out unresolved.

Room: 8–20 seated so everyone can turn to a neighbour; §B5 carries the n=1–7 variants. Visible clock or silent timer, facilitator-only. Standing rules, said once at 0:00 and honoured all session: you can step out of anything without explaining why; nobody is required to say anything personal; every pair activity has a written solo alternative, stated before pairs form, not offered on request.

0:00–0:05 · Welcome, scope, consent, disclosure — 5 minutes, non-compressible

Serves: the enabling conditions for everything else. This block is the same length it would be in a three-day programme. Brevity is never a legitimate reason to shorten safeguarding text.

Print it on a card. C4 §2.6 is right that ~110 words of dense compliance language delivered cold will be read off something; that is acceptable for safeguarding text and it should be designed as a facilitator card, not left as prose. The participant-facing summary of the collection paragraph is printed on the disclosure card as well, so it can be re-read.

Facilitator does: stands, does not sit; delivers D-0015's six universal minimum controls in full, the non-clinical scope statement, and the D-0016 disclosure statement with its visible placeholder. Points to the disclosure card in front of each person.

[SAY] — VERBATIM. Every clause below has been checked against Form 1, Form 2, Form 3, the four linkage-code items and the facilitator delivery record.

"Before anything else — what today is, and then exactly what happens to anything you write.

This is education and skill practice. It is not therapy, not treatment, not counselling, and not a crisis service. If something comes up for you today that needs more than a workshop, that isn't a failure of anything — it's what the card in front of you is for.

You can step out of any part of today without telling me why, and you don't have to say why.

You will never be required to say anything personal out loud. A few parts today invite you to share something if you want to. Every one of them has a written or silent alternative, I'll tell you what it is before we start, and if you pass, nobody will ask you why.

Now — what gets collected. I'm going to be exact, because 'nothing' wouldn't be true.

Most of what you write today goes home with you and I never see it. The moment you choose, your Radar, your state check, your shift, your reminder card, the four lines you'll write near the end — those are yours. Nobody reads them. Not me, not whoever booked this.

Two forms are collected — the one from last week, and one at the end. They ask what you learned and what you plan to try, and one of them does ask you to write down, in your own words, the moment you've chosen. Those come back to us, and yes, we read them.

They carry a code, not your name. There is no name and no email address anywhere on them, and we can't work backwards from the code to you.

Whoever booked this session never sees an individual answer — not yours, not anyone's, ever. They get numbers for the whole group. And because there are fewer than twenty of us, they get no participant data from today at all.

If you'd rather not fill in a form, don't. It changes nothing about your place here."

Foundations adds one sentence, before the last: "If the room decides later on to agree one shared thing to work on, that one sentence is written down and shared — it belongs to the room, not to any one of you, and no name goes with it."

Facilitator note — when the group is 20 or larger, drop "and because there are fewer than twenty of us…" and say instead: "they get numbers for the whole group, with nothing broken down small enough to point at a person." The reporting floors are fixed in the forms draft: no report on a group under 20, no subgroup under 10.

Facilitator note — if the live v0.10 Form 1 email field survives advisor review, the line "no name and no email address anywhere on them" becomes false and must be changed before delivery (§0, conflict 2).

Participants do: nothing but listen. No task in this block.

Materials: disclosure / participant card, one per person, on the seat before they arrive, with the collection paragraph printed on the reverse.

0:05–0:10 · Protected form time and linkage — 5 minutes

Serves: measurement. Protected: this block is never shortened to buy content time.

Facilitator does: hands out shuffled token cards — pre-printed, never tied to a name. Explains the card code once. Then reads the four linkage-code items aloud and gives the room time to answer them. Then a catch-up window for anyone who did not complete Form 1.

[SAY]: "The card in your hand has a code on it. Write that code on anything you fill in today and on the form that reaches you in three weeks. It isn't your name, and we can't work backwards from it to you — that's the point. Keep the card.

Cards get lost, so there are four small questions that let us join your three forms together if yours does. The first two letters of your mother's first name. The day of the month you were born. The month you were born. How many older brothers and sisters you have. That's it — they're not your name, they aren't enough to find you, and they exist for one job: so your answer in three weeks lands next to your answer today instead of being thrown away.

If you didn't get to the form we sent last week, do it now. If you did, this is a few minutes to get a coffee where you're sitting."

Participants do: write the token code on Form 2; answer the four linkage items; complete Form 1 if outstanding.

Materials: shuffled token cards (one per person, +5 spare); Form 1 printed (+5 spare); Form 2 printed, face-down; identical pens.

0:10–0:14 · Four ordinary moments, the definition, the distinction — 4 minutes

Serves: B-04, and it loads the material K-E2 uses next.

[SAY]: "Four moments. The email you read three times before you answer it. The conversation at home that goes sideways in about nine seconds. The thing you meant to do at 4pm and it's now 7. The walk to the car after a meeting, replaying it. Anyone recognise any of those? Don't answer, just notice." "Mental health is how you're doing. Mental fitness is what you're able to do — think, feel, act and connect in life's everyday moments. They're related and they're not the same thing, and almost nothing you've ever been offered was aimed at the second one."

Hold this beat at four minutes. It is the tightest beat in the format. Questions policy, changed from B2 (C4 §2.3): short factual questions are answered where they land, in one sentence; anything longer goes to the close, which is now three minutes, not two. Do not tell the room twice to hold everything.

0:14–0:21 · Why the gap exists, and say it back — 7 minutes

Serves: K-E2.

Facilitator does (4 min): a plain account of ordinary experience, built on one of the four moments just named. No brain diagrams, no amygdala, no fight-or-flight, and no route or pathway language — this is a K-08 boundary, not a style preference.

[SAY] — shortened from B2, and it is not to be read aloud from the page: "Take the conversation at home. You know, at the time, that the useful move is to stop talking and listen. You've known that for years. And you interrupt anyway, and you notice about a second later. Nothing's wrong with you. Under load, your attention narrows — and whatever you've done most is what turns up first. Knowing the answer was never the missing piece." "And nobody sat you down and taught you what to do with that. Not at school. Not really at home. You assembled your own strategies out of whatever happened to you and whatever you picked up. That's why your life makes the sense it does. It isn't a you problem. It's a gap in what everyone was given."

Then (3 min): "Turn to one person. Say that back in your own words — and you're not allowed to use any of the words I just used. If you'd rather not turn to anyone, write it instead; that's a completely normal choice and it's the same exercise."

Facilitator listens to two or three pairs and corrects nothing except a science claim. If someone says "it's your amygdala": "that's the version we're all told — it's not what we're doing here, and we don't need it."

0:21–0:25 · The five public skills — 4 minutes

Serves: E8, one of D-0003's six essential-content items.

[SAY], the five verbatim: "Notice — notice what is happening inside you, around you, and between you and others. Shift — create enough space to become workable, through your body or through your thinking. Choose — identify what matters and follow through. Focus — put your attention where it matters and return it when it drifts. Connect — connect better with yourself and others." "That's the map. You're not learning five things today. You're going to pick one moment, and one of these is what that moment is mainly asking of you. We'll come back to it."

Materials: skills reference card, one per person.

0:25–0:32 · Stop, Shift, Do — 7 minutes

Serves: E3. Traffic light named exactly once, as contrast, then dropped (D-0054).

[SAY], the three steps verbatim: "Stop — catch the moment. Shift — create enough space where useful and available. Do — make the next move with intention." "People sometimes map these to red, amber, green. I'll say it once and then let it go, because the colours mislead in three specific ways. Red is not freezing — Stop is catching the moment, and it's the pivot: everything after it only exists because you noticed. Amber is not calming down — Shift is making space, and sometimes making space means getting your energy up, not down. Green is not the right answer — Do is your next move, made on purpose. There is no correct move here, and I'm not going to grade one."

Materials: SSD card (colour + word + glyph — colour is never the only carrier).

0:32–0:37 · State Check — 5 minutes

Serves: E4.

[SAY] (3.5 min): "One question: is my state too much, too little, or workable — for this moment. That last bit, 'for this moment', is not decoration; it's the whole thing. Too much is more intensity, urgency or load than the moment can use. Too little is less energy, clarity or alertness than the moment needs. Workable means you've got enough access to choice. It does not mean calm. You can be furious and workable. You can be perfectly calm and completely unable to act. This isn't a fourth step and it's never scored."

Then (~1.5 min), the live check: "Don't answer out loud, don't write anything, nobody will ever ask you. Right now, in this room — too much, too little, or workable, for this moment? Ten seconds. Eyes open or closed, your choice." Count ten seconds of silence. Then: "That was a Stop."

Nothing shared, nothing collected, nothing scored (K-08 rule 7).

0:37–0:47 · The retrieval drill — 10 minutes

Serves: E3. This is D-0004's mandatory retrieval element, and under the corrected phase mapping it opens Revisiting/Connecting, where D-0004 puts it.

10 minutes is MFC's product floor for this format, not a number from a decision record — see §0. The live 1-hour build gives it 6; this is a proposed +4. It is the last thing cut and the cut is a recorded deviation, not an ordinary one (§B4).

Facilitator does: call-and-response at pace, whole room in unison. Nobody cold-called. Two sets alternating, finishing on Set B. Feedback is explanatory, never correctness-only (D-0004): when the room gets one wrong, say why, not just "no."

  • Set A — the mapping. "Stop is?" → "Catch the moment." "Shift is?" → "Create enough space." "Do is?" → "The next move, with intention." Vary the order; speed up.
  • Set B — the three corrections, as standing items. "Is Stop freezing?" → "No — catching the moment." "Is amber calming down?" → "No — making space." "Is Do the right answer?" → "No — the next move, with intention."

Online variant (the only one specified in this plan): Set A becomes "say it where you are" (mics off, facilitator answers after a counted three). Set B becomes a chat waterfall released on a countdown. Nobody is ever unmuted by name.

0:47–0:52 · The Shift menu — 5 minutes

Serves: E5. Menu names aloud; never the bare category words — the bare category words are body, attention, perspective, connection (K-07).

[SAY] (2 min): "Four kinds of shift. Move it — feet on the floor, one slower breath, stand up, step outside. Zoom in or out — name three things you can see, or ask what this will matter in a week, or narrow to the one next thing. Ask a different question — what would I tell a friend here? Is this a fact, or a feeling talking? Bring someone in — text one person, ask for two minutes, say out loud what's actually going on." "One thing, plainly: breathing is one option on that list. It is not the required strategy and it is not what this is. Same tools go both ways — the same move can bring you down or bring you up."

Then (2 min), private write: "One move. In your words, not mine. Not 'Move it' — what you'd actually do." Then (1 min), optional to a neighbour: "Which of these do you already reach for?" — existing behaviour, not a commitment. Opt-out stated.

0:52–0:56 · What counts as a rep — 4 minutes

Serves: E6.

[SAY], the definition verbatim: "A mental rep is catching a moment and choosing your next move with intention. You may catch the moment before it happens, while it is happening, or afterwards. The outcome does not determine whether it counts." "Hands up if you've ever caught yourself scrolling and put the phone down. That was a rep. You've done thousands. Nobody ever named it — and nobody ever taught you the shift."

Then (2 min): "Think of a time this week you caught something and it still went badly. Went badly. That was a rep too. It counts. If a rep only counted when it worked, everybody would stop by Thursday."

Capped, and this is a change from B2 (C4 §2.3): take at most one volunteered example, never solicited by name, and close it with a stated move — "that's exactly it, thank you — let's keep going." This is the beat where a dominator can take four minutes out of a format that has five to give (§B4), and it is a raised-exposure beat under §B8.

What does not count, said once: a moment by itself; a habit done entirely on autopilot; reading about it without applying anything.

0:56–1:06 · The moment — 10 minutes

Serves: E1, E8. No theme reveal in Essentials — see §A, E1.

0:56–0:59 — narrowing, modelled live (3 min). The word Radar is named here, as a thing a person has: "What you're about to make is a Radar — a short list of the moments you're actually watching for. Today it's one." [SAY]: "'Stress at work' — I can't do anything with that. Where does it actually happen? 'When I open my laptop on Monday morning.' Now it has a place and a trigger, and you'll know it when it arrives. That's the whole test."

0:59–1:04 — private write (5 min). [SAY], the prompt verbatim: "Think about the person you are trying to become in this season of life." "One moment. Either one you want to handle better, or one you want to experience more fully — both are real, pick whichever is honest. Write it with a place and a trigger. Then, underneath, which of the five skills it's mainly asking for. Nobody reads this. It goes home with you."

The two stuck points, scripted — the facilitator walks the room and uses these by name: - "My moment is too big." → "Then don't take the whole thing. Take the first ten seconds of it. What's the smallest version that's still real?" - "I can't think of one." → "Don't hunt for the most important one. What happened yesterday that you'd rather have handled differently? That'll do — you're not marrying it."

1:04–1:06 — the shape check, in pairs (2 min). On format only, never content. [SAY]: "Turn to one person. You are not going to read your moment out. You're going to ask them two questions and hear yes or no. Does it name a place? Does it name a trigger? If you'd rather do this on your own, they're printed on your slip — check your own against them. That's a normal choice and it works." Do not ask how often it comes up. Frequency is not a criterion (D-0010).

Materials: moment slip, one per person, with the two shape questions printed on it; board or flipchart; marker.

1:06–1:14 · The full pass, on their own moment — 8 minutes

Serves: E7. This is the beat the whole session builds to.

1:06–1:08 — modelled (2 min). [SAY]: "My moment: opening the laptop Monday morning. What the Stop looks like here: my hand's on the lid and I notice my jaw. My state read: too much, for this moment. My next move: I stand up and fill the kettle before I open anything. That's the whole thing. Four lines. Eleven seconds in real life."

1:08–1:13 — private, silent, written (5 min). Four lines: the moment / what the Stop looks like here / my state read / my next move. [SAY], said before they start — and matched word for word to P-09: "If you only get two lines down — the moment, and the next move — you've had a go, and that's exactly what I'm asking for. Don't sit there stuck on line three."

1:13–1:14 — say it (1 min). [SAY]: "Say your next move out loud. To the person next to you, or under your breath to yourself — those are the same thing here, and I'm not checking which. If there's nobody next to you, under your breath is the default, not the fallback." No hands-up. Nobody is asked who finished.

Materials: full-pass sheet, A5, one per person. Not collected.

1:14–1:18 · The cue, and what happens when you stop — 4 minutes

Serves: transfer (D-0008).

[SAY]: "One cue. Something already in your week that will remind you — the kettle going on, unlocking your phone, sitting down at your desk. Write it on the card. You're not adding anything to your day; you're attaching this to something already in it." "And then the honest part. Most people's first go at this fades. Not some — most. That's expected, it isn't failure, and here's exactly how it'll go: you'll forget. You'll be unsure what to do in the moment. The moment will feel too big to pause in. You'll go a whole day without an obvious chance. All of that is normal, and all of it is the reason to pick one small moment rather than wait for a perfect one. One rep, whenever you next notice you stopped. That's the whole re-entry."

Also named once, in a line: sleep, movement and food shape what's available to you — that's the Engine, it's real, and it's on the card. Named, not expanded (K-07).

Materials: cue card, wallet-sized; take-home card carrying the locked rep definition and the Engine line.

1:18–1:21 · Close — 3 minutes

Facilitator does: threshold framing, then takes the held questions here — this is what the extra minute is for.

[SAY]: "You're leaving with the start of a skill, not a finished one. This isn't a course you complete, it's a practice you keep. Today was your first rep, not your last. You have one moment, one move, one reminder — that's the whole plan, and it's already written down in front of you."

1:21–1:30 · Protected form time, Form 2 — 9 minutes

Protected. In the room, before anyone leaves.

[SAY]: "Nine minutes, and then you're free. Code from your card at the top. Nothing here is scored, and nothing goes to whoever booked this with your name on it — same as I said at the start." Then stays quiet and does not answer content questions that would change an answer.

Participants do: complete Form 2 (14 items: B-04, B-06, P-01, P-01b, P-02, P-02b, P-03, P-04, P-04b, P-05, P-07, P-08, P-09, P-11).

B4 · The cut-order rule — checkpoints placed before the cuts they control

Why B2's version could not work. It checked once, at 0:52, and three of its five cuts had already run by then — the rule recovered two minutes at its own checkpoint, and its fallback pointed at the "95-minute variant," which is the Form-1-was-not-sent variant and adds nine minutes at the front. That fallback is deleted. It was not a slack reservoir; it relabelled an over-run the room never agreed to.

How this version works. Every cut has a checkpoint immediately before the beat it cuts, and each checkpoint states the minutes still recoverable from that point forward. The recovery decays as the session runs, which is the true shape of the problem.

Essentials — six checkpoints (content clock = wall clock; there is no break).

Check at Are you behind? Then, from here, you can still recover Ordinary + recorded Total
0:10 four moments (1) · five skills (1) · menu exchange (1) · rep beat (1) · close (1) 5 drill 10→8 (2) 7
0:21 five skills (1) · menu exchange (1) · rep beat (1) · close (1) 4 drill 10→8 (2) 6
0:37 menu exchange (1) · rep beat (1) · close (1) 3 drill 10→8 (2) 5
0:47 menu exchange (1) · rep beat (1) · close (1) 3 — 3
0:52 rep beat (1) · close (1) 2 — 2
1:18 close (1) 1 — 1

What each cut costs: four moments 4→3 (name two, not four; K-E2 has less material) · five skills 4→3 (read the five, drop the illustration; E8 weakens to naming, P-11 still answerable) · Shift-menu neighbour exchange 5→4 (nothing measured) · what counts as a rep 4→3 (definition and normalising beat only, no volunteered example; P-04b gets harder to answer honestly) · close 3→2 (held questions go unanswered — say so).

The drill cut is not an ordinary cut. 10→8 is a material deviation under D-0014 §6 and must be written on the facilitator delivery record with the reason. It is placed last on purpose. It is also the one legitimate use of D-0014 in this document: a departure that arose in delivery, not a design-time change to an approved requirement. Even at 8 minutes the drill still exceeds the live 1-hour build's 6.

Never cut, in any circumstance: the 5-minute welcome/consent block · the drill's 8-minute residue · the 10-minute moment beat · the 8-minute full pass · the 9-minute Form 2 block · the 5-minute form and linkage block.

The honest ceiling, stated. The maximum this rule can recover is 7 minutes, and only if you catch it at 0:10. If you are further behind than the table allows at any checkpoint, the rule cannot save you and you must not improvise: tell the room the session will finish at [time], hold every protected block, and record it. Silently shortening E1, E7 or the forms invalidates the outcome claim and the primary measure at the same time, which is precisely the failure this rule exists to prevent.

It is the most expensive beat with the weakest measurement, which is why it is the honest thing to lose.

B5 · The n=1, small-room and silent-room variants

Essentials is sold to teams of 1–20, and three beats use pairs. Every one has a stated alternative, given by default and not on request.

B6 · The booking checklist — five things the facilitator must know before arriving

  1. Was Form 1 sent seven days ahead? If no → the 95-minute variant, which adds a 9-minute Form 1 block at the front. This is not a slack reservoir and must never be invoked to absorb an over-run (see §B4).
  2. Have the Form 1 nominations been aggregated into two or three themes, and by when? Deadline: the working day before the session (closing C4 §7 item 11 — B2 gave a minimum-n rule and no deadline). If the response count is under five, do not reveal themes — say so plainly and move on. In Essentials nothing is revealed in the room at all; the themes go to the host in writing.
  3. The host agreement is signed, including the two standing prohibitions: no manager ever asks to see anyone's moment, and non-practice is never treated as a performance issue in a review, a one-to-one, or a joke.
  4. Foundations only: the hazard route is named concretely for that organisation, agreed with the host, before the session. F3 cannot be run without it.
  5. D-0016's six matters and the disclosure placeholder. Until they resolve, this is not deliverable to participants, and the placeholder must not go out unresolved.

B7 · The room that does not behave

Closing C4 §2.3 and §7 item 6. None of this was in B2.

  • The dominator. Named beats where it costs most: 0:52 (what counts as a rep) and, in Foundations, the 1:25 contrast debrief. Standing move: take one contribution, name what was useful in it in one clause, and close with "that's exactly it, thank you — let's keep going." Second attempt in the same beat: "I want to hear that one properly and we've got three minutes — grab me at the end?" Never invite the room to respond to a dominator's contribution.
  • The refuser. "You can step out" is not enough on its own. Standing move: "You don't have to do this one. Sit with it, or write instead — both are fine, and I won't come back to you." Then do not come back to them. Do not ask why, do not check in publicly later.
  • The question that will not wait. Short and factual → answer in one sentence where it lands. Long, personal, or off the arc → "That's a good one and it needs more than thirty seconds. Hold it for the close and I'll take it properly." Then actually take it at 1:18. The close is three minutes for exactly this reason.
  • The room that will not speak. Run §B5's solo column throughout; do not fill the silence by extending the teach beats, which is how the drill and the moment beat get eaten.

B8 · If somebody discloses something distressing — drafted, not approved

Closing C4 §7 item 5. This wording is drafted here so it exists to be reviewed; it is not approved, and it does not satisfy or advance D-0016. It goes to D-0016 Items 1–2, with the clinical-governance input those items require.

Raised-exposure beats, named: 0:52 (E6 — recalling a time something went badly), and in Foundations 2:08 / 2:23 (F1 — a peer takes someone through their own moment) and 2:29 / 2:44 (F3 — workload, safety and leadership raised explicitly). B2 disclosed that these two raise exposure above the current builds and correctly referred them to D-0016; what it did not do was write a line for what the facilitator says when it happens.

Standing sequence: stop the beat you are in · thank them plainly, do not explore, do not interpret, do not ask a follow-up question · name the boundary once, out loud — "that's more than a workshop can hold, and that isn't a failure of anything" · point to the disclosure card · offer to speak at the break or after · do not return to them in front of the room · record it on the delivery record the same day.

Do not continue teaching over it, and do not use it as material.

D2 · The D-0018 decision records — drafted, not adopted

These replace B2's D-0014 deviations. D-0014 §1 names, at the design-requirement level, "Decision 1's five-phase session architecture and the intended function of each phase", "Decision 2's explanatory feedback and recall-based retrieval" and "Decision 5's approved Radar structure (three personally meaningful moments…)", and states they "may not be removed, contradicted, or materially weakened." D-0018 states that "a change to an 'essential function' requires a new decision record" and that "essential-element changes require Hunter's approval." D-0014's deviation mechanism is a light facilitator-side record for departures that arise in delivery — it is not a design-time licence, and used as one it makes the approved design non-compliant by construction while every facilitator records the identical "deviation" every time.

Reserve each ID with the governed tool at the point of adoption; do not assume one. ruby 90-meta/controlled-automation-v1/portfolio-autonomy-v1/id_reservation_ctl.rb next "D-"

Record 1 — D-[reserve at adoption] — Essentials runs without a distinct Mechanism block

Decision. The 90-minute Essentials format delivers D-0003's five-phase architecture with no distinct Mechanism block. The Human Operating System's six components are not taught. The one thing Mechanism must deliver — state changes what is available to you, not only how you feel — is delivered inside E4 (State Check, 0:32–0:37). Foundations is unaffected and runs Mechanism as a named 8-minute block in the fixed order at 0:55–1:03.

What it changes. D-0003 fixes "the five functional phases: Orientation, Skills, Mechanism, Revisiting/Connecting, Application" and D-0014 §1 protects "the intended function of each phase." This removes the block and retains the function. D-0014 §6 names "materially change session sequence or phase function" as material deviation, which is why this is a D-0018 record and not a facilitator-side one.

Why. 90 minutes cannot carry the HOS and also produce E1, E7 and the drill at their product floors. D-0003 itself does not fix phase durations, exercises or the specific activity in any phase, and it records its own Moderate confidence and its own status as "an approved provisional product requirement, not a research finding." The HOS is also the one element the existing facilitator guide already tells participants they are not expected to memorise.

What is given up, stated. Participants in Essentials leave without any account of what shapes access in a moment beyond the one line in E4. Nothing in the Essentials instrument measures Mechanism, so this cannot be detected in the data — it is a design judgement, not an evidenced one.

Scope. Essentials only. Does not change D-0003 for Foundations, the three-hour build, or any future format. Does not claim the four-phase version is equivalent, or better.

Requires: Hunter's approval under D-0018. Recommendation: approve. Confidence: moderate.

Record 2 — D-[reserve at adoption] — One Radar moment, not three, in both Offer 1 formats

Decision. Both Essentials and Foundations have participants write one Radar moment with one next move, rather than D-0010's approved "three meaningful moments → one possible next move for each." Both Radar strands (handle better / experience more fully) are still offered in the prompt; one moment is written.

What it changes. D-0014 §1 names "Decision 5's approved Radar structure (three personally meaningful moments…)" as an essential function, and §6 names "alter the approved Radar structure" as material deviation.

Why — and the reason B2 gave is deliberately not used. K-07, the locked foundations record governing Framework meaning, describes Stage 1 as "a Radar set with 1–3 moments" and repeats "a Radar with 1–3 moments" in its learning-arc table. One moment therefore sits inside the Framework's own range; what this record changes is D-0010's workshop target, not the Framework. Beyond that: in a 90-minute session three moments produce three unfinished ones, and a near-empty sheet with three blank slots reads as failure where one filled slot reads as complete. D-0010 itself records three as "a testable MFC product structure", explicitly not evidence-validated, and states "the initial pilot will test whether three feels manageable."

The measurement argument is excluded on purpose. D-0010 states: "The participant design must not be reduced to one Radar moment solely because one target would be easier to measure." B2's stated reason included exactly that ("the follow-up asks about a single named moment, so three make the answer ambiguous"). That reasoning is withdrawn and forms no part of this record. If the instrument is the only reason, this record should be refused.

What is given up, stated. D-0010's own rationale for three — "one moment may be too narrow to represent the different areas of life in which participants want to strengthen mental fitness" — is real and is not answered here. Breadth is traded for completion.

Scope. Both Offer 1 formats. Does not change D-0010 for any longer or multi-touchpoint pathway. Does not claim one moment transfers better than three; nothing evidences either count. The live 1-hour build already writes one moment; precedent in a build is not authority and is not offered as one — it is noted only so the change is not mistaken for a new one.

Requires: Hunter's approval under D-0018. Recommendation: approve. Confidence: moderate.

Record 3 — D-[reserve at adoption] — CONDITIONAL, and probably not owed — the retrieval element's phase

Why this is conditional. C4 §4 found that D-0004's recall-based retrieval element — which that decision places "in the Revisiting/Connecting phase" — had been moved into Skills in both of B2's formats, undeclared. In this document it is in Revisiting/Connecting in both formats:

  • Foundations: the drill has genuinely moved, from 0:50–1:00 (inside Skills) to 1:03–1:15, straight after the break, opening Revisiting/Connecting. A real change, and the stronger version of the mechanism, since it now follows a spacing gap.
  • Essentials: nothing moved. B2 mapped Skills as 0:20–0:52, which swallowed the drill. Under the corrected mapping (§A) Skills ends at 0:37 and the drill opens Revisiting/Connecting 0:37–0:56. That was a mapping error in B2, not a beat in the wrong place.

On that reading no record is owed. It is stated openly so a reviewer can disagree.

The one reading under which it is owed: if Hunter reads D-0003's phase order as requiring Revisiting/Connecting to follow a Mechanism block, then Essentials — which has no Mechanism block (Record 1) — cannot have a compliant Revisiting/Connecting phase at all, and this record is the consequence of Record 1 rather than a separate change.

Decision, if adopted. In the Essentials format only, D-0004's recall-based retrieval element operates in a Revisiting/Connecting phase that follows Skills directly, with no intervening Mechanism block. Everything else in D-0004 — explanatory feedback, never correctness-only; recall rather than re-presentation — is unchanged and delivered in full.

Requires: Hunter's approval under D-0018, only if he takes the second reading. Recommendation: not needed; adopt only if Record 1's phase reading requires it. Confidence: moderate.

Note 3, unadopted — the record that would be needed to reveal Team Pulse themes in Essentials

Not drafted as a record because the beat is cut, not proposed. If Hunter wants the 2-minute anonymous theme reveal in the short format, it needs its own D-0018 record extending D-0091, whose §"The 1-hour format" gives the short format collection and host handover only, and against the live build's own item 08: "What changes: Nothing in the one-hour room." Cost, stated: 2 minutes from a clock whose cut-order rule can recover a maximum of 7; and pre-session aggregation becomes a hard dependency of the short format, where it is currently optional.

D3 · The record that would be needed for cardinal counting — drafted, not adopted

Not required by this chain, which uses D-0017's approved binary-plus-band form. Drafted so the choice is real rather than rhetorical.

D-[reserve at adoption] — Cardinal opportunity and attempt counts at follow-up Decision. Form 3's F-01 and F-02 ask for counts (0–20+) rather than D-0017's approved binary-plus-opportunity form, so the primary outcome is reported as a ratio (F-02 ÷ F-01). This is what the 2026-08-10 forms draft currently proposes, so adopting it is keeping the draft rather than changing it. Why. A ratio distinguishes "acted on two of two opportunities" from "acted on two of ten," which a binary cannot; it is the strongest single defence against the ceiling problem that made the nearest published instrument unable to detect its own intervention. What it costs, stated. The participant computes their own failure rate in the act of answering ("five came up, I did one"), at the exact moment D-0008's follow-up is meant to work as a lapse-and-return door rather than a check-up. No feedback protection removes this. A recall tally over a fortnight is also the weakest kind of self-report. What it does not do. It does not reintroduce a rep count as a performance measure; it remains opportunity-conditional and attempt-based, never fed back, never ranked. Supersedes D-0017 item 2's binary threshold for Form 3's F-01/F-02 only. Requires cognitive testing of both items before the first cohort.

D4 · The questions only Hunter can answer

Each arrives with a recommendation and a confidence. None of them blocks the session plan — Part B runs as written under every answer.

1. F-03 — cut it? Recommendation: cut. Confidence: high. K-07's locked Mental Rep definition says "the outcome does not determine whether it counts." F-03 — "in how many did you get all the way through" — is a completion standard applied to a unit defined as outcome-independent. It is the one place the instrument contradicts a locked record. B2 recommended cutting it and then rebuilt it as P-09; that is fixed (§A, E7), and the underlying question is still yours. What is lost: the gap between starting and finishing, which the forms draft calls the place the design learns most. It can be recovered later as a facilitator-side or case-study question rather than a graded item on every participant. This is a framework question, which is why it is yours.

2. Cardinal counts, or bands? Recommendation: bands. Confidence: high. Opportunity-conditioning is not a founder question — D-0017 approved it. The narrow real question is binary/band versus cardinal tally. Bands preserve the ratio logic, defeat the ceiling problem identically, cannot be described as counting reps by anyone including a sceptical committee member, and need no new record. Note that bands are a change to the current forms draft, not a correction of it — §D3 is the record if you want the tally kept.

3. Is the Leaders' Session an Offer 2 product, and does the Foundations embedding promise survive without it? Recommendation: keep it in Offer 2; soften the embedding promise. Confidence: moderate. D-0090 decides the first half. The consequence is commercial and it is yours: F3 produces a named person and a sentence, and without a leader who knows what is coming, that request lands cold. Either the offerings page stops promising "help embedding it" for standalone Foundations, or the Leaders' Session becomes a condition of booking it. F3 itself stands either way.

4. Is Essentials ever delivered to schools, youth, or public/keynote audiences? Recommendation: no, until C-16 and the youth process are reviewed and a safeguarding lead is named. Confidence: high.

5. K6 — is the knowing–doing-gap outcome approved? Marked "Proposed — requires Hunter's approval under D-0018" and never approved, yet B-06 already measures it and K-E2 is a seven-minute beat in both formats. Recommendation: approve. Confidence: high.

6. NEW — the three D-0018 records in §D2. Records 1 and 2 need your approval before either format is a design of record. Record 3 needs it only under one reading of D-0003. Recommendation: approve 1 and 2; Record 3 not needed. Confidence: moderate.

Original source: 60-projects/committee-pack-v1/B3-session-plan-final-draft.md

B4 Session Plan Approved Draft

B4 — The outcome chain and the session plan

What this is. B3, with three founder decisions applied, the measurement construct rebuilt from the knowing–doing gap rather than from the instrument that existed, and the findings of this document's own independent review closed, rejected on evidence with the check shown, or disclosed as unsolved.

B3's substance was sound and most of it survives. Its arithmetic holds under independent re-addition; its cut-order rule works at every checkpoint; and the two C4 findings it rejected were correctly rejected. What changed is not arithmetic. It is what the session is trying to produce evidence of.

The change that matters most, stated before anything else

Every version of this document until now — B1, B2 and B3 — built counting machinery. How many moments arose; in how many did you act; in how many did you finish. That measures frequency of practice, and MFC does not exist to increase how often people rehearse.

MFC exists for the knowing–doing gap: people know what would help and cannot reach it while the moment is happening. So the measure is access under load — when it mattered, could you get to it?

The correction is smaller than it sounds, and more embarrassing. The right item already existed in the instrument, mislabelled as background. The forms draft's B-01 — "When there was something you knew could help, how often did you remember to use it while the moment was happening?" — is the Drive Blueprint's PRE-02, already specified as matched baseline-to-follow-up, already called "the single most important matched item" by the draft that files it under "Starting point." A worse primary outcome was built around it across three passes.

The full construct, its research basis, the four independent reasons the ratio had to go, the places where it departs from the standing research recommendation, and the result that would disconfirm it are in [[60-projects/committee-pack-v1/B5a-measurement-construct|B5a]]. B5a governs every measurement statement below.

What else changed from B3.

  1. F-03 is cut, and no item may reintroduce a completion standard under any name. P-09 was already reworded to attempt in B3 and is re-checked against this rule at §A, E7. K-07's locked definition — "the outcome does not determine whether it counts" — is now honoured by the instrument as well as by the teaching.
  2. WHO-5 is out of the first cohort. Not carried on any form. Available to add later if Eimear Quigley and Debra Fidler want it, with the governance D-0017 requires. Source conflict 1 is decided, not open. The record this owes against D-0017 §5 is drafted at §D2, Record 1.
  3. The Radar stays at three moments, as the live build has it. B3's D-0018 Record 2 (three → one) is withdrawn — it is no longer needed, and D-0010's approved structure is restored rather than deviated from. The Essentials clock is rebuilt around it.
  4. The Radar is no longer collected at all. Because the measure never checks whether a participant did the specific thing they wrote down, P-08 no longer needs its content. It becomes a count-and-shape item — how many moments did you write, and does at least one name a place and a trigger — and the moments themselves go home. The 0:00 consent script says so plainly, because it is finally true.
  5. Form 3 had no send channel, and nothing in B3 noticed. Removing email removed the only route by which the three-week form reaches anyone. R3 §8 item 7 already held the answer — a physically separate, clearly-labelled opt-in slip, never joined to the responses. §0, conflict 2.
  6. The linkage code's rule-breaking item is fixed, using R3 §1.7's own prescription. §0, conflict 3.
  7. Foundations gains a second break, matching the live 3-hour build, which has two. B3 gave 180 content minutes one break and left 117 unbroken content minutes. Every Foundations wall-clock time and every checkpoint is restated. §Part C.
  8. The six Foundations beats that existed only as one-line table rows now have scripts. B3 said "everything in Part B runs as written unless named here" about beats that are not in Part B at all — 75 of Foundations' 180 minutes had no [SAY] and no facilitator instruction.
  9. Room size, virtual delivery and the findings note are reconciled against the offer ladder and D-0098, or named as founder decisions rather than silently chosen. §D4.
  10. D-0015's controls are listed, not referenced. A facilitator cannot deliver "the six universal minimum controls in full" from a document that never says what they are. §B 0:00.

The second structural change: Foundations stops being a redesign

B3 designed a new 180-minute session and called it Foundations. It should not have. D-0094, decided 2026-08-09 and cited nowhere in B3, already decided what Foundations is:

"The intervention is unchanged — still approximately three hours of content. What changes is the container around it: elapsed time, breaks, and how it is sold." "Working shape: roughly 9:00–13:00 elapsed, with approximately three hours of actual content and a substantial break inside it." "Breaks are a genuine participant benefit, not just packaging."

B3's Foundations was not a repackage. Checked against the live 3-hour build, it deleted two entire teaching blocks without mentioning either one:

Live 3-hour block Length The build's own note In B3
0:45–0:57 "Thoughts, feelings, and what's actually trainable" 12 min, New "Was one line inside another beat. Now its own block, because everything later depends on it" Absent
2:30–2:40 "Train in the easy moments" 10 min, New "Missing from the previous cut entirely, and it's what makes reps make sense as training rather than as coping" Absent

It also cut "You have been doing reps your whole life" from 9 minutes to 4, and the Human Operating System block from 9 to 8, neither declared; and it replaced the live build's two 15-minute breaks with one, leaving 117 unbroken content minutes against the live build's longest run of 60.

Resolution, and it is the strongest answer available rather than a concession.

Foundations is the live 3-hour build, unchanged, repackaged as a half day per D-0094, plus the two protected measurement blocks. This document stops designing it.

What that buys, all of it real:

  • The two deleted blocks come back, because they were never removed from the thing that actually exists.
  • The 75 minutes of Foundations that had no script in B3 stop being a problem — the live build scripts them, and has been through its own review.
  • The second break returns, and with it §B8's distress remedy ("offer to speak at the break"), which in B3 pointed at a break that did not exist at either of the two beats §B8 itself names as raised-exposure.
  • D-0094 is complied with instead of contradicted.
  • The design risk drops to near zero, because nothing about Foundations is new.

The shape. Live 3-hour content (180 min) + two 15-minute breaks, with the pre-session form on the table at arrival as the live build already does, and 10 minutes added at the close for Form 2 → 190 content minutes, 3h40 elapsed. Book the room for four hours, which is D-0094's own 9:00–13:00 working shape.

Everything in this document about Foundations-as-a-new-design is therefore withdrawn, including its clock, its cut-order table and its added-beat list. What survives is the measurement layer and the outcomes, which attach to the live build unchanged. F1, F2, F3 and F5 are re-derived against the live build's own beats at §Part C.

This needs Hunter's yes or no, and it is §D4 question 7. If he wants the new 180-minute design instead, it needs its own decision record against D-0094 and roughly 75 minutes of script that does not exist.

Three things B2 got wrong that this document does not repeat.

  1. B2 cited design-of-record numbers while claiming to have checked the live build. Every duration in this document now carries its live-build source, in §0. Where a proposed duration is more than the live build gives, it is marked PROPOSED +n. Where it is less, it is marked PROPOSED −n with a reason. Nothing is presented as "what MFC already does" unless the live build actually does it.
  2. B2 used D-0014 as design-time authority. It is not. D-0014 is a facilitator-side deviation mechanism for departures that arise in delivery. The only use of D-0014 in this document is one recorded delivery-time drill deviation at the bottom of the cut-order rule (§B4) — which is exactly what it is for. Design-time changes to essential functions go through D-0018, in §D2.
  3. B2's opening consent line was false. It is rewritten in §B, checked item by item against Form 1, Form 2, Form 3, the four linkage-code items and the facilitator delivery record.

Two things carried forward from B2 unchanged, because C4 verified them: the outcome-chain format, and the arithmetic discipline. Every clock in this document is added up in the open.

Part 0 — Every time floor and duration, reconciled against the live build

How to read this. "Live 1-hour" and "Live 3-hour" are the two formats in workshop-package.html. The two products in this document — Essentials, 90 minutes and Foundations, 180 content minutes — do not exist in the live build; this is the bridge between what is built and what is on the price list, and every minute of difference is declared.

What "floor" means here, stated precisely. D-0004 mandates "one recall-based retrieval element… operating in the Revisiting/Connecting phase" and sets no duration at all. D-0015 mandates six universal minimum controls and sets no duration. No decision record in this system fixes a minute value for anything. Every "floor" below is therefore MFC's own product floor for this format, defended by argument, not a number quoted from a governing record. The drill correction, in full — this is the finding B2 failed on

B2 stated twice that "the live 60-minute build gives it 10 and calls it the single largest allocation in the format." The live 60-minute build gives it 6. Verbatim, from the file:

0:26 – 0:32 · Drill it — full pace, both sets · tag: 8 → 6 min "Tightened from the first cut, but still the largest single practice block of the hour."

The "10 minutes" came from 12-one-hour-delivery-kit.md — a design-of-record file — via C3-08. That is the exact class of source C3 said B1 failed by relying on, carried into a document whose whole claim to authority was that it had checked the live build.

C4's own figure is also wrong, in the other direction, and from the same class of source. C4 §1.3 states "the live 3-hour gives the drill 15 minutes" and reasons from it that Foundations takes "a third off the protected element." The live 3-hour gives it 12 — beat 1:32–1:44, confirmed independently by the outcome card that describes "the twelve-minute choral drill at 1:32." The reduction was real but it was 12 → 10, not 15 → 10.

Resolution. Foundations runs the drill at 12 minutes, matching the live 3-hour exactly, so no reduction to a D-0014-protected element occurs and no record is owed for it. Essentials runs it at 10, declared as PROPOSED +4 over the live short format — an increase to a protected element, which needs no authorisation. The two minutes Foundations needs come from the moment beat, whose theme reveal has moved to F5 (C4 §2.4 item 2 — the same two minutes B2 left unattached).

The three source conflicts — all three now resolved, not flagged

B3 named these and passed all three on. All three are closed here.

1 · WHO-5 — DECIDED, out. Three genuinely contradictory statuses existed: D-0017 §5 "retain WHO-5 as an instrument" and D-0055 §6, both approved decision records; the live build's measurement tab carrying it as a "required wellbeing measure"; and the 2026-08-10 forms draft removing it. B3 resolved this toward the unapproved draft, which was the wrong instrument for the job — an unapproved draft does not override an approved record (CLAUDE.md §4).

Hunter decided it directly, 2026-08-11: WHO-5 is out of the first cohort. Three reasons, all sound: the contradictory statuses; that it would reach a participant alone, weeks later, with no approved distress pathway while D-0016 items 1–2 are open; and that it measures how a person is doing — mental health — which K-05 says mental fitness is not.

This is a change to D-0017 §5 and the record is owed, not assumed. Drafted at §D2, Record 1. WHO-5 is recorded as available to add later on Eimear Quigley's and Debra Fidler's advice, with the governance D-0017 requires. The consent script promises no wellbeing measure, and now none is collected.

2 · Email — and the hole underneath it that B3 did not see. The live build's Form 1 opens with an "Evaluation email address" field; the forms draft removes email entirely — "no identifier ever exists." B3 followed the draft and flagged only that one consent sentence might become false.

The real problem is that removing email removes the only route by which Form 3 reaches a participant. The forms draft states Form 3 is "sent day 21, reminders day 24 and 27, closes day 28" and specifies no channel to send it through. Every durability figure this chain produces rests on a form that, as specified, cannot be delivered.

Resolved, using R3's own answer rather than a new invention. R3 §2 and §8 item 7:

"Collect follow-up email on a physically separate, clearly-labelled opt-in slip, and never join it to the responses… The follow-up invitation problem and the linkage problem are different problems and must not be solved with the same field."

The design. A separate opt-in slip, handed out and collected apart from every form, reading: "This is only so we can send you the three-week link. It is kept apart from your answers and is never matched to them." Held in a separate file, used only to send, deleted at day 28 when Form 3 closes. A participant may take the link without giving an address — the host also circulates a generic link to everyone, so opting out of the slip does not opt you out of the follow-up.

Disclosed: the host circulating a generic link means the host knows a follow-up went to the group. It does not tell them who responded or what anyone said. That is a real, small exposure and it is the price of having any follow-up at all. It goes to D-0016 item 4 with the protocol.

3 · The linkage code contradicted its own design rule — fixed. The forms draft's own validation reasoning is "never ask someone to count letters. Ask the fact and extract it in software," and its first code item is "the first two letters of your mother's first name" — a letter-extraction item sitting directly under the rule that bans them. B3 correctly refused to fix it and passed it on.

It is fixed here, and R3 §1.7 already specified how. The item asks for the whole fact and MFC does the extraction:

"What is your mother's first name? If you'd rather use another parent or the person who raised you, use theirs — just use the same person every time."

Plus a storage rule the forms draft does not have and needs: the name is entered, the first two letters are derived in software, and the raw name is never written to the dataset. This holds R3's 100%-stability class — the failure it documents is in the extraction operation, not in the fact — while keeping the entropy R3 costed, and it removes the objection that MFC holds a security-question answer.

One caution carried forward, not closed. ACT-061's own standing instruction is "do not adopt codes derived from personal facts without a proper privacy and technical assessment," and that assessment has not been run. The code is specified here so it can be assessed, not because the caution is satisfied. §D6.

Part A — the outcome chain

The measurement constraint, restated

The primary outcome is D-0017's approved architecture in its approved form: an opportunity-conditional, binary, attempt-based initial-use threshold — "at least one reported attempted application," with an opportunity item so "didn't practise" is never confused with "had no opportunity."

  • F-01 (banded, revised): "In the last seven days, did the moment you chose come up? Not at all / once or twice / most days / not sure."
  • F-02 (binary, revised): "Did you run the three steps in any of them — even partly, even badly? Yes / no."
  • Skip and denominator rules, fixed now (closing C4 §6's first defect): F-01 governs. A respondent answering "not at all" or "not sure" is routed past F-02 and sits outside the denominator, reported in its own named cell. F-02's "there was no relevant moment" option is removed — it duplicated F-01 and created a cell with no governing rule.
  • Primary outcome: the proportion of participants who had an opportunity and attempted at least once, reported inside its own denominator and its band, with the "not at all", "not sure" and unmatched counts printed beside it.

This is a change to the 2026-08-10 forms draft, stated as one. That draft asks F-01/F-02/F-03 as cardinal counts and makes the primary outcome the ratio F-02 ÷ F-01. The revision above moves toward D-0017's approved form and away from the draft's; it is more compliant, not less, but it is a proposal for Eimear and Debra, not a correction of an error. The record that would authorise the cardinal alternative instead is drafted at §D3.

F-03 is used by no outcome in this chain. See §D4 question 1 — a founder decision, recommended for cutting, and flagged, not decided here.

Format 1 — Essentials, 90 minutes

Talk-led with real practice in the room. The bar: one moment, one full pass, one tool, one cue.

Room size, reconciled (C4 §2.3, §7 item 9): Essentials is sold to teams of 1–20 and the plan is written for 8–20 seated so everyone can turn to a neighbour. Below 8, and at n=1, the solo variants in §B5 are the default rather than the alternative. Foundations is 12–20.

Delivery mode, declared (C4 §7 item 8): both formats as specified here are in-person only. The drill keeps the live build's online variant because that variant is already built; a full online Essentials is a separate design task, and it would have to carry the live 1-hour's own online provisions — captions on by default, no registration gate before the privacy notice, 12–25 participants — none of which is designed for the pair beats, the board narrowing, the moment slip or the full-pass sheet.

(Adult workplace and community audiences only. Schools, youth, public talks and keynotes are out of scope — K-08's control-state warnings and C-16 block them pending review, and no safeguarding lead is named.)

E1 — Names one recurring moment from their own week, specific enough to recognise when it arrives

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes one moment stated as a situation with a place and a trigger — "when my daughter asks for the iPad at dinner," not "stress" — and confirms with a neighbour, or against the two printed questions, that it has both.
Its job It is the participant's cue, so it carries the transfer path (D-0008); and it is the unit F-01 asks about. It is not required to recur at any frequency (D-0010: the Radar is "a personal map, not a three-part compliance task").
Content required The word Radar named as a thing a person has (closing C4 §1.5's residual — it is one of D-0003's six essential-content items and B2 introduced it in function but never in name). K-07's Radar prompt verbatim. One worked narrowing of a vague moment, modelled live. The two named stuck points, each scripted. Both Radar strands offered; one moment written.
Activity, with minutes 10 min. 3 min facilitator narrows one vague moment live on the board. 5 min private silent write — the moment, and which of the five skills it asks for (E8's 60 seconds is funded here, closing C4 §2.3; B2 left it unfunded inside a 4-minute write). 2 min shape check in pairs, on format only: "Does it name a place? Does it name a trigger?" Solo alternative stated before pairs form.
Items P-08 (post, existing) — "Write the one recurring moment you have chosen to work on." Scored for form only. B-07 (NEW, Form 1, pre-session), rewritten — see below.
Claim boundary (K-08) Licenses: "participants leave having chosen and written one specific moment from their own life." Does not license that they have a practice or a habit.

B-07, rewritten so it can be answered cold (closing C4 §1.7). B2's version — "how often do you face situations like these" — had no antecedent on a form sent seven days before the session. Revised:

B-07. "In a typical week, how often do you run into a situation you'd like to have handled better — a conversation that goes sideways, something you keep putting off, a moment where stress or frustration gets ahead of you? Not at all / once or twice / most days / not sure."

And it is stated as an abandonment, not a relocation. B2's crosswalk claimed countability "moves to a facilitator-side shape check plus B-07." It does not. The shape check is restricted to place-and-trigger and forbidden from asking frequency; B-07 asks about a generic class, not the participant's own chosen moment. Nothing in this design checks how often the chosen moment recurs. That is the right answer under D-0010, which prohibits a frequency target — but it is a thing given up, and B-07 is baseline context for F-01, not a replacement for it.

Our moments in Essentials — the in-room reveal is dropped. B2 added a 2-minute anonymous theme reveal and attributed it to D-0091. D-0091 §"The 1-hour format" gives the short format collection and host handover only, and the live build's own change list, item 08, reads: "What changes: Nothing in the one-hour room." B2 attributed a new beat to an approval that says the opposite. Closed by dropping the beat. The Form 1 nomination item is still collected in both formats, the facilitator still aggregates it, and the anonymised theme list still goes to the host — exactly as D-0091 provides. Adding it back to the room would cost 2 minutes from a clock with no slack, make pre-session aggregation a hard dependency of the short format, and require its own decision record; the draft is at §D2, note 3, unadopted.

K-E2 — Accounts for the knowing–doing gap in their own words, without MFC's vocabulary

Field Content
Observable behaviour Says to one other person, in one or two sentences, why someone who knows what would help still does the other thing — using none of MFC's words.
Its job It makes the definition land as an answer to a problem the room is holding. It earns Stop.
Content required A plain account of ordinary experience. Delivered as description a participant recognises, never as science — no brain diagrams, no amygdala, no fight-or-flight, and no route/pathway language (see the claim correction below).
Activity, with minutes 7 min. 4 min facilitator account, built on one of the four moments named just before. 3 min explain-back to one other person, or written alone.
Items B-06 (existing, all timepoints) — the scenario item. P-01b (NEW, post, free text, one line) — "In one sentence: why does someone who knows what would help still do the other thing?" ~30 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can account for the gap between knowing and doing in their own words." Does not license any claim about mechanism or brain change, and does not license that understanding the gap closes it.

Claim correction (C4 §5.1), applied to the script. B2's [SAY] line was "the old route is faster because it's been used more" — a neural-pathway claim in plain clothes, in a beat whose own boundary forbids mechanism claims, and K-08 bars "rewiring the brain" outright with mechanism sitting at Level 3, pending. Replaced throughout with the experience-level version: "whatever you've done most is what turns up first." B2's "That's it. That's the whole problem" is also cut — a flat sufficiency claim about the cause of the knowing–doing gap, and the sentence a committee member would quote back.

Authority flag, carried forward unresolved. This is K6 in 10-product-finalisation-v1/02-design-rationale-and-outcomes-checklist.md, marked "Proposed — requires Hunter's approval under D-0018", never approved, while B-06 already measures it. §D4 question 5.

E3 — Says what each of the three steps means, unprompted, without the colours

Field Content
Observable behaviour Given "Stop, Shift, Do" and nothing else, states what each one is: catch the moment; create enough space where useful and available; make the next move with intention.
Its job Retrieval under load. A step recognised on a slide but not producible in a car park is not available in a real moment.
Content required K-07's locked wording, verbatim. The traffic light named exactly once, as contrast (D-0054), then the three corrections taught as their own items. Stop taught as the pivot. Explanatory feedback, never correctness-only (D-0004).
Activity, with minutes 7 min teach + 10 min drill (Essentials) / 12 min drill (Foundations). See §0 for the live-build reconciliation of both figures. Choral call-and-response, whole room as one voice, nobody cold-called. Two sets alternating, finishing on Set B.
Items P-02 (post, existing). P-02b (NEW, post, free text) — "What does Shift mean? Don't use the colours." ~30 s. F-04 (3 weeks, existing).
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants could state the three steps and what each means, and X% reported recalling them during a real moment at three weeks." Does not license that they used them well, or that recall predicts use.

Scoring guidance, not room language (closing C4 §5.5). "Answering 'red, amber, green' is a fail" is a marking rule for P-02b only. It must never be said in the room, where the standing line is "there is no correct move here, and I'm not going to grade one." Marked as such wherever it appears.

E4 — Reads their own state as too much / too little / workable, for a specific moment

Field Content
Observable behaviour Verifiable: says why "workable" is not "calm" — it is about what choice is available, not how pleasant it feels. Delivered but unverifiable by design: one silent State Check in the room, never shared, never collected, never scored (K-08 rule 7).
Its job The only sanctioned self-assessment language MFC has, and the precondition for Shift meaning anything.
Content required The three words with the anchor phrase "for this moment" every time; the lock-in that State Check is not a fourth step; and the access idea — state changes what is available to you, not only how you feel.
Activity, with minutes 5 min. 3.5 min teach, ~1.5 min live silent check.
Items P-03 (post, existing).
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can state what workable means and distinguish it from calm, and were given one silent opportunity to apply it to themselves." Does not license that they can use the state language on a real moment of their own — nothing verifies the silent half. No claim about emotion regulation or physiological change.

E5 — Names one shift move, in their own words, for the moment they chose

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes a concrete move in their own words — "stand up and walk to the kitchen before I answer" — not a menu name and not "breathing".
Content required The Shift menu as a menu to pick from, not a taxonomy to learn — Move it / Zoom in or out / Ask a different question / Bring someone in. K-07: "Facilitators should use the menu names aloud, not the bare category words" — the bare category words are body, attention, perspective, connection, which is what must not be said. The claims boundary said aloud: breath is one option, not the required strategy (D-0083).
Activity, with minutes 5 min. 2 min menu named with one example each. 2 min private write. 1 min optional to a neighbour.
Items P-05 (post, existing). F-07 (3 weeks, existing) — naming something MFC never taught is a success at F-07, not a failure.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants left with a self-worded, retrievable move, and X% reported using something at three weeks." Does not license that any tool works or that MFC's tools were the ones used.

C4 §2.6's third finding is rejected on the record. C4 reported that the script "contradicts its own instruction" by leading each item with the bare category word. It does not: "Move it", "Zoom in or out", "Ask a different question" and "Bring someone in" are the menu names, and K-07 line 661 is explicit that they are what should be said aloud — "since 'attention' is also deep-tier vocabulary." B2's script was correct and is kept as written.

E6 — States what counts as a rep, including one that went badly

Field Content
Observable behaviour Says that a rep counts when the moment was caught with intention, whatever the outcome.
Its job Outcome-independence is what makes F-02 answerable honestly: "even partly, even badly" only works if the room has been told partly and badly count.
Content required K-07's locked definition, verbatim. What does not count: a moment by itself; a habit on autopilot; reading about it. The normalising beat.
Activity, with minutes 4 min. 2 min definition and normalising beat. 2 min: "think of a time this week you caught something and it still went badly." At most one volunteered aloud, never solicited by name, and capped — see §B7.
Items P-04 (post, existing). P-04b (NEW, post) — "Think of a rep you ran that didn't go the way you wanted. Did it still count? Yes / no." ~30 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can distinguish a rep from information or an accident, and can identify a rep that did not go well as still counting." Does not license any claim about practice volume.

E7 — Attempts all three steps on their own chosen moment, in the room

Renamed from B2's "Runs all three steps," and this is not cosmetic — see the P-09 correction below. The live build already ends on an actual rep: the 1-hour format's "Do one, right now" beat at 0:38–0:41, added 2026-08-05, carrying Baldwin & Ford and Bandura, mapped in the build's own traceability table to Form 2 Q7. This is not a discovered hole. E7 improves that existing beat in two respects: all three steps, and on the participant's own chosen moment, written eight minutes earlier. The 3-hour build's Application phase genuinely has no equivalent beat.

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes on their own moment: the moment / what the Stop looks like here / my state read / my next move — then says the next move out loud to themselves or a neighbour. Two of the four lines is a complete attempt, stated aloud before they start.
Its job The in-room analogue of F-02, which makes "even partly, even badly" refer to something they have already done once.
Activity, with minutes 8 min. 2 min modelled. 5 min private, silent, written. 1 min: say the next move out loud. No public hands-up — it sorts the room into completers and partial-completers on a construct K-07 defines as outcome-independent, and it contaminates P-09.
Items P-09 (NEW, post), reworded — see below.
Claim boundary Licenses: "X% of participants reported attempting all three steps on a moment of their own before leaving the room." Does not license competence, habit or transfer. One rehearsed pass in a supported room is not one pass in a real moment, and the two must never be reported in the same number.

P-09 no longer grades completion (closing C4 §6's second defect, which is defect 3 of this correction pass). B2's script authorised a two-line pass at 1:10 and then asked, at 1:21, "did you run all three steps? Yes / no" — so a participant who did exactly what the facilitator sanctioned had to tick no. Worse, B2 recommended cutting F-03 precisely because "a completion standard applied to a unit defined as outcome-independent" contradicts K-07's locked definition — and then rebuilt F-03 in the room, on the same construct. Revised:

P-09. "Today, did you have a go at running the three steps on a moment of your own — even partly? Yes / no."

The [SAY] line at 1:06 is matched to it word for word (§B). F-03 remains flagged as a founder decision (§D4 question 1) and is not decided here.

E8 — Says which of the five public skills their own moment mainly asks for

D-0003 fixes all six essential-content items as first introduced within the session, and the five public skills are one of them. K-07's amended staged-arc section and D-0091 resolve the Stage 1 / Stage 2 question: for a standalone session — the only contact this audience gets — Stage 1 and Stage 2 collapse and the session legitimately teaches the full five skills, full State Check and the full Shift menu. K-08's audience-translation table still reads "the five public skills are named from Stage 2" and is now stale; named in §D5, not silently chosen.

Field Content
Observable behaviour Given the five labels in locked wording, says which one their own written moment mainly asks of them, and why, in one line.
Content required K-07's locked wording, one short line each: Notice · Shift · Choose · Focus · Connect. The seven deep skills stay out (Stage 3 holds).
Activity, with minutes 4 min teach, plus 60 seconds funded inside E1's 5-minute write.
Items P-11 (NEW, post) — "Which of the five does your moment mainly ask for, and why?" ~30 s.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants can map a real moment of their own to one of the five public skills." Does not license that they can distinguish all five, define them, or use them.

Every change from B3's clock, and where the minutes came from.

Change Effect Why
Form/linkage block 5 → 4 +1 The Form 1 catch-up moves out of the block to the arrival window, as the live 3-hour build already does ("the pre-session form is on the table when they walk in"). B3's 5-minute block had to hold shuffled cards, the code explanation, the code items and a catch-up for a form B3 itself costed at 6.5 minutes — it was over-subscribed by its own arithmetic. Also: three code items now, not four
Shift menu 5 → 4 +1 The optional 1-minute neighbour exchange is cut. It measured nothing, and it was already the cut-order rule's own first ordinary cut
What counts as a rep 4 → 5 −1 The live 3-hour gives this beat 9 minutes (1:59–2:08, "You have been doing reps your whole life"). B3 gave it 4 and never declared the reduction. 5 is still −4, and it is now declared
The Radar beat 10 → 11 −1 Three moments, not one (founder decision, D-0010 restored). 3 min modelled narrowing + 6 min private write + 2 min shape check
State Check 5 → 6, drill 10 → 9 0 The three-component Human Operating System comes back. B3 removed it from Essentials entirely and drafted a decision record to authorise the removal — without noticing that the live 1-hour build carries it, at 0:32–0:38, "Driver, Passenger, Engine — three of the six, not all — then too much / workable / too little." Essentials now does exactly what the live short format does, in the same combined beat. The minute comes from the drill, which at 9 is still +3 over the live 1-hour's 6
Net 0 Clock still sums to 90

The cost of that last row, stated. The recorded-deviation drill cut becomes 9→8 rather than 10→8, so the cut-order rule's ceiling falls from 6 minutes to 5. That is a real loss of slack, and it buys back a governed element that B3 deleted without declaring and then wrote a record to excuse.

What the three-moment restoration costs, stated. Six minutes of private writing for three moments is tight, and the honest instruction in the room is that the first moment must be fully formed and the other two may be shorter — K-07's own Stage 1 range is "a Radar set with 1–3 moments", so a participant who finishes one and sketches two has not failed and is never told they have.

Every clock addition against B2, shown:

Change Effect Why
Form block 4 → 5 +1 The four linkage-code items were never collected (C4 §2.2); every three-week figure rested on them
Five skills 5 → 4 −1 The [SAY] block is ~100 words plus framing; 4 is honest
Moment beat 12 → 10 −2 The 2-minute Team Pulse reveal is dropped (D-0091 gives the short format nothing in the room)
Within the moment beat, write 4 → 5, shape check 3 → 2 0 Funds E8's 60 seconds, which B2 left unfunded (C4 §2.3)
Cue beat 3 → 4 +1 Live 1-hour gives cue + lapse 5 minutes; 3 was below both live builds
