Phase mapping (D-0003). Orientation 0:00–0:21 (welcome, forms, the four moments and the definition, the gap and the explain-back) · Skills 0:21–0:37 (five skills, Stop–Shift–Do, State Check) · Mechanism — absent, and a D-0018 record is drafted for it at §D2 · Revisiting/ Connecting 0:37–0:56 (the drill, the Shift menu, what counts as a rep) · Application 0:56–1:30.

D-0004's recall-based retrieval element sits at the head of Revisiting/Connecting, where the decision puts it. B2 mapped Skills as 0:20–0:52, which swallowed the drill and put the retrieval element inside the wrong phase — that was a mapping error, not a beat that moved. Under the corrected mapping nothing in Essentials has to move. This is stated openly so a reviewer can disagree with it: if Hunter reads the phase order as requiring the retrieval element to follow a Mechanism block that Essentials does not have, then the record at §D2 note 3 is owed and is drafted.

Format 2 — Foundations, half day (180 content min + 15 min break)

Foundations carries every Essentials outcome unchanged. What follows is only what the extra time buys. The rule: an outcome belongs here only if it cannot be produced in 90 minutes — because it needs a partner, a second person's material, a felt contrast, or a conversation the room has to prepare. "More content" is not a reason.

F1 — Runs the three steps on another person's moment, out loud, in both roles

Field Content
Observable behaviour In a pair, takes both roles; then names one thing that was harder about doing it with someone than alone.
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it Two turns plus a debrief. A one-turn version rehearses half the skill. 21 minutes minimum.
Content required K-07's "supporting others" table. The binding limits as content, not caveat: offer, never force (K-08 r6); peer support, not treatment (r2); knowing when to stop and bring in more support is part of the skill (r10). Opting out stated as normal before pairs form, with a solo written alternative offered by default.
Activity, with minutes 21 min. 3 model and limits · 7 turn one · 7 turn two · 4 debrief.
Items P-12 (NEW, post) — "Today, did you take someone else through the three steps? Both roles / one role / no — I worked alone." F-11 (NEW, 3 weeks), optional one line.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants practised the sequence as peer support, and X% reported using it with another person at three weeks." Does not license anything about team culture, relationships, psychological safety, or that MFC delivers support to third parties.

F2 — Picks a shift move that fits the specific moment, having run the contrast

Field Content
Observable behaviour States which move fits this moment and why another does not; and names one thing they noticed between the version run without the skill and the version run with it.
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it Two tools actually tried (10 min) plus the contrast and debrief (15 min). 25 minutes.
Content required The four categories with the downshift/upshift rule. Two tools tried live. The contrast both times ending identically — still tired, phone in hand, the thing still not done. Facilitator asks what participants noticed, never what was correct.
Items P-05 plus P-05b (NEW, post) — "Why that one, for that moment?" ~45 s. F-07 unchanged.
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants selected a tool for a specific moment and can say why." P-05b measures reasoning about fit; it does not evidence the felt contrast, and the contrast run is a delivered activity with no item of its own. Disclosed: the most expensive fifteen minutes in Foundations cannot be distinguished in the data from a room that skipped it.

F3 — Names the enabling condition their moment depends on, and who they have to ask

Field Content
Observable behaviour Writes: the enabling condition; whether it is inside their control or someone else's; if someone else's, the named person, the sentence they will say, and when. Separately, states where a problem goes if it is a workload, safety or leadership problem rather than a practice problem.
Its job The beat that opens the collective layer is the beat that closes the door on reframing a psychosocial hazard as a skill deficit. K-07: "a shared or team Radar must never be used to reframe harmful workload, unsafe leadership or psychosocial hazards as individual skill deficits. A route must exist for structural issues."
Why 90 minutes cannot produce it Diagnostic lens (8) then write and route (15). Compressed, it becomes a slogan about environment with no named person and no route — worse than not raising it.
Content required The Human Operating System's diagnostic question and the Environment component only. The enabling-conditions layer. That an Our moment requires genuine agreement. The hazard route, named concretely for that organisation, agreed with the host before the session.
Items F-12 (NEW, 3 weeks) — "You wrote down one thing you would ask someone for. Did you ask? Yes / no / not yet / it stopped being relevant."
Claim boundary Licenses: "participants identified an enabling condition and X% reported making the request at three weeks." Does not license anything about culture, norms, absenteeism or productivity. MFC has no organisational measurement instrument.

F5 — The room agrees one shared "when X, we will Y" commitment, or declines it out loud

D-0091's decided-and-built beat. This is the only place the theme reveal happens in either format (closing C4 §2.4 item 1 — B2's Part C left it running twice).

Field Content
Observable behaviour Either the room states one shared commitment as "when [this happens], we will [this]", written on each worksheet next to the participant's own moment — or the room declines, out loud, and moves on. Both are successful outcomes.
Activity, with minutes 6 min. 2 min anonymous theme reveal · 1 min genuine read of the room · then either 3 min drafting the sentence and naming who owns it, or "that's completely fine, plenty of rooms don't" and straight on.
Items No participant item, deliberately. The commitment, its wording and its named owner go on the facilitator delivery record. For case-study cohorts, reviewed at D-0056's extended wave. D-0091's day-10–14 templated reminder is drafted and not wired into the send infrastructure — do not describe it as running.
Claim boundary Licenses: "the room agreed one shared commitment" or "the room declined one" — a facilitator record of what happened in a room. Does not license anything about norms, culture, or that the commitment was kept.

F4 is deleted as a separate outcome. The five skills are E8 in both formats.

2:48–2:50 3:03–3:05 2 Close — threshold framing —
2:50–3:00 3:05–3:15 10 Protected form time — Form 2 in the room Measurement

First block: 8+5+10+4+7+5+7+5+4+8 = 63 (content 0:00–1:03). Second block: 12+10+15+4+6+10+8+21+15+4+2+10 = 117 (content 1:03–3:00). 63 + 117 = 180 content minutes ✓ Elapsed with the break: 3h15 before arrival — book the room for 3h30. Protected measurement time: 5 + 10 = 15 minutes (8.3%).

The wall-clock column closes C4 §2.5. B2 published content-clock times only and then issued operational instructions against them, so a facilitator with a wall clock was fifteen minutes wrong from the break onward. Every operational instruction in this document — including every cut-order checkpoint — is stated on both clocks.

Phase mapping (D-0003). Orientation 0:00–0:39 · Skills 0:39–0:55 · Mechanism 0:55–1:03 · Revisiting/Connecting 1:03–1:50 (drill, toolkit, contrast, what counts as a rep, Our moments) · Application 1:50–3:00. Skills precedes Mechanism, which is the fixed order; and D-0004's retrieval element now opens Revisiting/Connecting, where the decision puts it. This is a genuine restoration, not a re-labelling: the drill has moved to after the break (it was at 0:50–1:00, inside Skills, in B2). Retrieval after a spacing gap is also the stronger version of the mechanism, so the move costs nothing pedagogically.

3+10+5+8+2+5+15+6+21+15−1+1 = 90. 90 + 90 = 180 ✓ Every minute of the difference is attached to a named outcome or to a beat that exists in both, and no minute is unattached — which was C4 §2.4 item 2's finding against B2, where the moment beat's freed 2 minutes were silently absorbed into the "+6 Our moments" line. Here those 2 minutes are visibly the drill's.

A3 — The Leaders' Session is a separate offer, not part of either format

D-0090 Proposal 2: leader modelling "is an Offer 2 requirement and must not be retrofitted into Offer 1." Removed from both Offer 1 formats. Held as its own product, not built here. Four things must be true first: its evidential basis has to be rebuilt (the struck Mas & Moretti reasoning is not used); it needs a fifth instrument that does not exist; it cannot be anonymous at n=1–3, and the reporting floors — no report under 20, no subgroup under 10 — make single-organisation leader data unreportable; and the one prohibition worth carrying regardless belongs in the host agreement, signed before the session: a manager must never ask to see anyone's moment, and non-practice is never treated as a performance issue. §B6.

Consequence for Foundations, stated. F3 produces a named person and a sentence. Without a leader who knows what is coming, that request lands cold. F3 stands anyway — its hazard-routing half is what makes it safe and that does not depend on a leader — but the embedding promise on the offerings page does. §D4 question 3.

A5 — Burden arithmetic, shown, now including the linkage code

Baseline from the forms draft: Form 2 today = 12 items ≈ 8 min (B-03…B-06, P-01…P-08), ≈40 s per item. Form 3 = 10 items ≈ 6 min.

Form 2, Essentials. Cut B-03 and B-05 −80 s. Cut P-06 −40 s. Add P-01b 30 s, P-02b 30 s, P-04b 30 s, P-09 20 s, P-11 30 s = +140 s. 480 − 120 + 140 = 500 s ≈ 8.3 min → 9 minutes budgeted. 14 items.

Form 2, Foundations. Plus P-05b (45 s) and P-12 (20 s) = 565 s ≈ 9.4 min → 10 minutes. 16 items.

Form 3. Cut F-03 (§D4 q1) −1 item. Essentials 9 items ≈ 5.5 min. Foundations adds F-11 and F-12 with optional one-line free text: 11 items ≈ 7 min. A ~15% increase on the instrument whose response rate carries every durability claim MFC will make — disclosed, and the reason both free texts are optional.

Form 1. Adds B-07 (~20 s) and the nomination item (~30 s), plus the four linkage-code items (~40 s), which B2 omitted entirely (C4 §2.2). ≈5 min → ≈6.5 min.

In-room linkage block. The four code items are also read aloud and collected in the 0:05–0:10 block for anyone completing Form 1 in the room, and the token-card code is written on Form 2. This is why that block is 5 minutes, not 4.

All of this is arithmetic on the forms draft's own estimates. Nothing has been timed with real participants, and none of the new items has been through Eimear Quigley or Debra Fidler or been cognitively tested.

Part B — the Essentials session plan, beat by beat

Written so a facilitator who has never seen this can run it. [SAY] lines are the intent and the wording, not a script to read verbatim — except where marked verbatim, which are the locked or safeguarding lines.

Before the room: §B6's booking checklist must be complete. This session is not deliverable to participants until D-0016's six safeguarding matters resolve. The disclosure placeholder must not go out unresolved.

Room: 8–20 seated so everyone can turn to a neighbour; §B5 carries the n=1–7 variants. Visible clock or silent timer, facilitator-only. Standing rules, said once at 0:00 and honoured all session: you can step out of anything without explaining why; nobody is required to say anything personal; every pair activity has a written solo alternative, stated before pairs form, not offered on request.

0:00–0:05 · Welcome, scope, consent, disclosure — 5 minutes, non-compressible

Serves: the enabling conditions for everything else. This block is the same length it would be in a three-day programme. Brevity is never a legitimate reason to shorten safeguarding text.

Print it on a card. C4 §2.6 is right that ~110 words of dense compliance language delivered cold will be read off something; that is acceptable for safeguarding text and it should be designed as a facilitator card, not left as prose. The participant-facing summary of the collection paragraph is printed on the disclosure card as well, so it can be re-read.

Facilitator does: stands, does not sit; delivers D-0015's six universal minimum controls in full, the non-clinical scope statement, and the D-0016 disclosure statement with its visible placeholder. Points to the disclosure card in front of each person.

D-0015's controls, listed so the facilitator can verify "in full." B3 said "the six universal minimum controls" five times without ever listing them, and D-0015 does not state a count of six. The record's actual clauses are: (1) attendance does not equal consent to disclose; (2) participants have an alternative to public personal disclosure; (3) opting out of an activity requires no explanation; (4) the non-clinical scope is stated explicitly; (5) privacy and data-use are explained before any collection; (6) accessible alternative participation modes are provided where feasible; (7) plain language and flexible pacing. Clause 6 appeared nowhere in B3 and is added below; the live build's own print spec — 12pt minimum body, ≥1.4 line spacing, large-print 18pt copies on hand unasked — is carried into §B6.

[SAY] — VERBATIM. Every clause checked item by item against Form 1, Form 2, Form 3, the three linkage-code items, the follow-up opt-in slip and the facilitator delivery record.

"Before anything else — what today is, and then exactly what happens to anything you write.

This is education and skill practice. It is not therapy, not treatment, not counselling, and not a crisis service. If something comes up for you today that needs more than a workshop, that isn't a failure of anything — it's what the card in front of you is for.

And this isn't built on the assumption that you've got a supportive manager, a quiet office, or anyone checking in on you afterwards. People's situations and the support around them are different, and none of what we do today needs any of that to work.

You can step out of any part of today without telling me why. Coming today doesn't mean you've agreed to share anything with anyone. If you need a bigger print copy, a different chair, or more time on anything — say so now or any time, and it's not a favour.

You will never be required to say anything personal out loud. A few parts today invite you to share something if you want to. Every one of them has a written or silent alternative, I'll tell you what it is before we start, and if you pass, nobody will ask you why.

Now — what gets collected. I'm going to be exact, because 'nothing' wouldn't be true, and neither would 'everything'.

The moments you choose today are yours and they never leave this room with me. Your Radar, your state check, your reminder card, the four lines you'll write near the end — I never see them, and there is no question anywhere asking you to write out what your moments actually are. Not on any form, not today, not in three weeks.

Three forms are collected — the one from last week, one at the end of today, and one that reaches you in about three weeks. They ask what you learned, what got in the way, and whether you could get to it when something came up. One of them does ask you to write one line — name one thing you could do to give yourself a bit more space. That one we do read.

They carry a code, not your name. There is no name and no email address anywhere on them.

Whoever booked this session never sees an individual answer — not yours, not anyone's, ever. And because there are fewer than twenty of us, they get no participant data from today at all.*

If you'd rather not fill in a form, don't. It changes nothing about your place here."

Then, separately, the follow-up slip — handed out at the end, never with a form: "If you want the three-week one emailed to you, put an address on this slip. It's kept apart from your answers and never matched to them. You don't have to — [host] is sending the link to everyone anyway."

Facilitator note — when the group is 20 or larger, drop "and because there are fewer than twenty of us…" and say instead: "they get numbers for the whole group, with nothing broken down small enough to point at a person." Reporting floors: no report on a group under 20, no subgroup under 10.

Facilitator note — when the group is smaller than eight, the non-identifiability claim is not made. Three date-and-family facts in a room of four are close to unique, and saying "we can't work backwards from the code to you" would be a promise the arithmetic does not support. Say instead: "There are only a few of us, so I'm not going to pretend a code makes this untraceable. What I can tell you is that nobody who booked this ever sees a single answer, and there's no report at all on a group this size." B3 spotted this problem for the Leaders' Session and missed it for an Essentials product the offer ladder sells at 1–5 people. §D4 question 8.

Participants do: nothing but listen. No task in this block.

Materials: disclosure / participant card, one per person, on the seat before they arrive, with the collection paragraph printed on the reverse.

0:05–0:09 · Protected form time and linkage — 4 minutes

Serves: measurement. Protected: this block is never shortened to buy content time.

The Form 1 catch-up is not in this block. It happens in the arrival window, on the table as people sit down, exactly as the live 3-hour build does it — "the pre-session form is on the table when they walk in… it costs the session nothing." B3 kept the catch-up inside a five-minute block that also had to issue cards, explain the code and collect the code items, while B3's own arithmetic costed Form 1 at 6.5 minutes. That block could not be run.

Facilitator does: hands out shuffled token cards — pre-printed, never tied to a name. Explains the card code once. Then reads the three linkage-code items aloud and gives the room time to answer them.

[SAY]: "The card in your hand has a code on it. Write that code on anything you fill in today and on the form that reaches you in three weeks. It isn't your name. Keep the card.

Cards get lost, so there are four small questions that let us join your forms together if yours does. Your mother's first name — or another parent, or whoever raised you, just use the same person every time. The day of the month you were born. The month you were born. And how many older brothers and sisters you have. That's it. They exist for one job: so your answer in three weeks lands next to your answer today instead of being thrown away."

Note for the facilitator, not said aloud: the name is written in full and only the first two letters are kept — the raw name is never entered into the dataset. R3 §1.3's finding is that people do not forget the fact, they miscount to the second letter, so MFC does the extraction. All four elements appear on every form; dropping any one from a later form breaks the code and with it the match.

Participants do: write the token code on Form 2; answer the four linkage items.

Materials: shuffled token cards (one per person, +5 spare); Form 2 printed, face-down; identical pens. Form 1 and its spares live on the arrival table, not here.

0:10–0:14 · Four ordinary moments, the definition, the distinction — 4 minutes

Serves: B-04, and it loads the material K-E2 uses next.

[SAY]: "Four moments. The email you read three times before you answer it. The conversation at home that goes sideways in about nine seconds. The thing you meant to do at 4pm and it's now 7. The walk to the car after a meeting, replaying it. Anyone recognise any of those? Don't answer, just notice." "Mental health is how you're doing. Mental fitness is what you're able to do — think, feel, act and connect in life's everyday moments. They're related and they're not the same thing, and almost nothing you've ever been offered was aimed at the second one."

Hold this beat at four minutes. It is the tightest beat in the format. Questions policy, changed from B2 (C4 §2.3): short factual questions are answered where they land, in one sentence; anything longer goes to the close, which is now three minutes, not two. Do not tell the room twice to hold everything.

0:14–0:21 · Why the gap exists, and say it back — 7 minutes

Serves: K-E2.

Facilitator does (4 min): a plain account of ordinary experience, built on one of the four moments just named. No brain diagrams, no amygdala, no fight-or-flight, and no route or pathway language — this is a K-08 boundary, not a style preference.

[SAY] — shortened from B2, and it is not to be read aloud from the page: "Take the conversation at home. You know, at the time, that the useful move is to stop talking and listen. You've known that for years. And you interrupt anyway, and you notice about a second later. Nothing's wrong with you. Under load, your attention narrows — and whatever you've done most is what turns up first. Knowing the answer was never the missing piece." "And nobody sat you down and taught you what to do with that. Not at school. Not really at home. You assembled your own strategies out of whatever happened to you and whatever you picked up. That's why your life makes the sense it does. It isn't a you problem. It's a gap in what everyone was given."

Then (3 min): "Turn to one person. Say that back in your own words — and you're not allowed to use any of the words I just used. If you'd rather not turn to anyone, write it instead; that's a completely normal choice and it's the same exercise."

Facilitator listens to two or three pairs and corrects nothing except a science claim. If someone says "it's your amygdala": "that's the version we're all told — it's not what we're doing here, and we don't need it."

0:21–0:25 · The five public skills — 4 minutes

Serves: E8, one of D-0003's six essential-content items.

[SAY], the five verbatim: "Notice — notice what is happening inside you, around you, and between you and others. Shift — create enough space to become workable, through your body or through your thinking. Choose — identify what matters and follow through. Focus — put your attention where it matters and return it when it drifts. Connect — connect better with yourself and others." "That's the map. You're not learning five things today. You're going to pick one moment, and one of these is what that moment is mainly asking of you. We'll come back to it."

Materials: skills reference card, one per person.

0:25–0:32 · Stop, Shift, Do — 7 minutes

Serves: E3. Traffic light named exactly once, as contrast, then dropped (D-0054).

[SAY], the three steps verbatim: "Stop — catch the moment. Shift — create enough space where useful and available. Do — make the next move with intention." "People sometimes map these to red, amber, green. I'll say it once and then let it go, because the colours mislead in three specific ways. Red is not freezing — Stop is catching the moment, and it's the pivot: everything after it only exists because you noticed. Amber is not calming down — Shift is making space, and sometimes making space means getting your energy up, not down. Green is not the right answer — Do is your next move, made on purpose. There is no correct move here, and I'm not going to grade one."

Materials: SSD card (colour + word + glyph — colour is never the only carrier).

0:32–0:37 · State Check — 5 minutes

Serves: E4.

[SAY] (3.5 min): "One question: is my state too much, too little, or workable — for this moment. That last bit, 'for this moment', is not decoration; it's the whole thing. Too much is more intensity, urgency or load than the moment can use. Too little is less energy, clarity or alertness than the moment needs. Workable means you've got enough access to choice. It does not mean calm. You can be furious and workable. You can be perfectly calm and completely unable to act. This isn't a fourth step and it's never scored."

Then (~1.5 min), the live check: "Don't answer out loud, don't write anything, nobody will ever ask you. Right now, in this room — too much, too little, or workable, for this moment? Ten seconds. Eyes open or closed, your choice." Count ten seconds of silence. Then: "That was a Stop."

Nothing shared, nothing collected, nothing scored (K-08 rule 7).

0:37–0:47 · The retrieval drill — 10 minutes

Serves: E3. This is D-0004's mandatory retrieval element, and under the corrected phase mapping it opens Revisiting/Connecting, where D-0004 puts it.

10 minutes is MFC's product floor for this format, not a number from a decision record — see §0. The live 1-hour build gives it 6; this is a proposed +4. It is the last thing cut and the cut is a recorded deviation, not an ordinary one (§B4).

Facilitator does: call-and-response at pace, whole room in unison. Nobody cold-called. Two sets alternating, finishing on Set B. Feedback is explanatory, never correctness-only (D-0004): when the room gets one wrong, say why, not just "no."

  • Set A — the mapping. "Stop is?" → "Catch the moment." "Shift is?" → "Create enough space." "Do is?" → "The next move, with intention." Vary the order; speed up.
  • Set B — the three corrections, as standing items. "Is Stop freezing?" → "No — catching the moment." "Is amber calming down?" → "No — making space." "Is Do the right answer?" → "No — the next move, with intention."

Online variant (the only one specified in this plan): Set A becomes "say it where you are" (mics off, facilitator answers after a counted three). Set B becomes a chat waterfall released on a countdown. Nobody is ever unmuted by name.

0:47–0:52 · The Shift menu — 5 minutes

Serves: E5. Menu names aloud; never the bare category words — the bare category words are body, attention, perspective, connection (K-07).

[SAY] (2 min): "Four kinds of shift. Move it — feet on the floor, one slower breath, stand up, step outside. Zoom in or out — name three things you can see, or ask what this will matter in a week, or narrow to the one next thing. Ask a different question — what would I tell a friend here? Is this a fact, or a feeling talking? Bring someone in — text one person, ask for two minutes, say out loud what's actually going on." "One thing, plainly: breathing is one option on that list. It is not the required strategy and it is not what this is. Same tools go both ways — the same move can bring you down or bring you up."

Then (2 min), private write: "One move. In your words, not mine. Not 'Move it' — what you'd actually do." Then (1 min), optional to a neighbour: "Which of these do you already reach for?" — existing behaviour, not a commitment. Opt-out stated.

0:52–0:56 · What counts as a rep — 4 minutes

Serves: E6.

[SAY], the definition verbatim: "A mental rep is catching a moment and choosing your next move with intention. You may catch the moment before it happens, while it is happening, or afterwards. The outcome does not determine whether it counts." "Hands up if you've ever caught yourself scrolling and put the phone down. That was a rep. You've done thousands. Nobody ever named it — and nobody ever taught you the shift."

Then (2 min): "Think of a time this week you caught something and it still went badly. Went badly. That was a rep too. It counts. If a rep only counted when it worked, everybody would stop by Thursday."

Capped, and this is a change from B2 (C4 §2.3): take at most one volunteered example, never solicited by name, and close it with a stated move — "that's exactly it, thank you — let's keep going." This is the beat where a dominator can take four minutes out of a format that has five to give (§B4), and it is a raised-exposure beat under §B8.

What does not count, said once: a moment by itself; a habit done entirely on autopilot; reading about it without applying anything.

0:55–1:06 · The Radar — 11 minutes

Serves: E1, E8. No theme reveal in Essentials — see §A, E1. Three moments, not one — D-0010's approved structure, restored by founder decision 2026-08-11.

0:55–0:58 — narrowing, modelled live (3 min). The word Radar is named here, as a thing a person has: "What you're about to make is a Radar — the short list of moments you're actually watching for. Three of them." [SAY]: "'Stress at work' — I can't do anything with that. Where does it actually happen? 'When I open my laptop on Monday morning.' Now it has a place and a trigger, and you'll know it when it arrives. That's the whole test."

0:58–1:04 — private write (6 min). [SAY], the prompt verbatim: "Think about the person you are trying to become in this season of life." "Three moments. Some you want to handle better, some you want to experience more fully — both are real, and you don't need a set number of each. Write each one with a place and a trigger. Then, underneath, which of the five skills it's mainly asking for. Get the first one properly finished before you go to the second. If you end up with one good one and two rough ones, that's a Radar and you've done the exercise. Nobody reads any of this — it goes home with you."

Why that instruction is in the script and not a facilitator note. Three blank slots that a participant fills once reads as failure; one filled slot and two sketches, named in advance as a complete result, does not. K-07's own Stage 1 range is "a Radar set with 1–3 moments", so the floor is inside the Framework and the room is told so rather than left to guess.

The two stuck points, scripted — the facilitator walks the room and uses these by name: - "My moment is too big." → "Then don't take the whole thing. Take the first ten seconds of it. What's the smallest version that's still real?" - "I can't think of one." → "Don't hunt for the most important one. What happened yesterday that you'd rather have handled differently? That'll do — you're not marrying it."

1:04–1:06 — the shape check, in pairs (2 min). On format only, never content. [SAY]: "Turn to one person. You are not going to read your moment out. You're going to ask them two questions and hear yes or no. Does it name a place? Does it name a trigger? If you'd rather do this on your own, they're printed on your slip — check your own against them. That's a normal choice and it works." Do not ask how often it comes up. Frequency is not a criterion (D-0010).

Materials: moment slip, one per person, with the two shape questions printed on it; board or flipchart; marker.

1:06–1:14 · The full pass, on their own moment — 8 minutes

Serves: E7. This is the beat the whole session builds to.

1:06–1:08 — modelled (2 min). [SAY]: "My moment: opening the laptop Monday morning. What the Stop looks like here: my hand's on the lid and I notice my jaw. My state read: too much, for this moment. My next move: I stand up and fill the kettle before I open anything. That's the whole thing. Four lines. Eleven seconds in real life."

1:08–1:13 — private, silent, written (5 min). Four lines: the moment / what the Stop looks like here / my state read / my next move. [SAY], said before they start — and matched word for word to P-09: "If you only get two lines down — the moment, and the next move — you've had a go, and that's exactly what I'm asking for. Don't sit there stuck on line three."

1:13–1:14 — say it (1 min). [SAY]: "Say your next move out loud. To the person next to you, or under your breath to yourself — those are the same thing here, and I'm not checking which. If there's nobody next to you, under your breath is the default, not the fallback." No hands-up. Nobody is asked who finished.

Materials: full-pass sheet, A5, one per person. Not collected.

1:14–1:18 · The cue, and what happens when you stop — 4 minutes

Serves: transfer (D-0008).

[SAY]: "One cue. Something already in your week that will remind you — the kettle going on, unlocking your phone, sitting down at your desk. Write it on the card. You're not adding anything to your day; you're attaching this to something already in it." "And then the honest part. Most people's first go at this fades. Not some — most. That's expected, it isn't failure, and here's exactly how it'll go: you'll forget. You'll be unsure what to do in the moment. The moment will feel too big to pause in. You'll go a whole day without an obvious chance. All of that is normal, and all of it is the reason to pick one small moment rather than wait for a perfect one. One rep, whenever you next notice you stopped. That's the whole re-entry."

Also named once, in a line: sleep, movement and food shape what's available to you — that's the Engine, it's real, and it's on the card. Named, not expanded (K-07).

Materials: cue card, wallet-sized; take-home card carrying the locked rep definition and the Engine line.

1:18–1:21 · Close — 3 minutes

Facilitator does: threshold framing, then takes the held questions here — this is what the extra minute is for.

[SAY]: "You're leaving with the start of a skill, not a finished one. This isn't a course you complete, it's a practice you keep. Today was your first rep, not your last. You have one moment, one move, one reminder — that's the whole plan, and it's already written down in front of you."

1:21–1:30 · Protected form time, Form 2 — 9 minutes

Protected. In the room, before anyone leaves.

[SAY]: "Nine minutes, and then you're free. Code from your card at the top. Nothing here is scored, and nothing goes to whoever booked this with your name on it — same as I said at the start." Then stays quiet and does not answer content questions that would change an answer.

Participants do: complete Form 2 (14 items: B-04, B-06, P-01, P-01b, P-02, P-02b, P-03, P-04, P-04b, P-05, P-07, P-08, P-09, P-11).

B4 · The cut-order rule — checkpoints placed before the cuts they control

Why B2's version could not work. It checked once, at 0:52, and three of its five cuts had already run by then — the rule recovered two minutes at its own checkpoint, and its fallback pointed at the "95-minute variant," which is the Form-1-was-not-sent variant and adds nine minutes at the front. That fallback is deleted. It was not a slack reservoir; it relabelled an over-run the room never agreed to.

How this version works. Every cut has a checkpoint immediately before the beat it cuts, and each checkpoint states the minutes still recoverable from that point forward. The recovery decays as the session runs, which is the true shape of the problem.

Essentials — five checkpoints (content clock = wall clock; there is no break).

Check at Are you behind? Then, from here, you can still recover Ordinary + recorded Total
0:09 four moments (1) · five skills (1) · rep beat (1) · close (1) 4 drill 9→8 (1) 5
0:20 five skills (1) · rep beat (1) · close (1) 3 drill 9→8 (1) 4
0:37 rep beat (1) · close (1) 2 drill 9→8 (1) 3
0:50 rep beat (1) · close (1) 2 — 2
1:18 close (1) 1 — 1

What each cut costs: four moments 4→3 (name two, not four; K-E2 has less material) · five skills 4→3 (read the five, drop the illustration; E8 weakens to naming, P-11 still answerable) · what counts as a rep 5→4 (definition and normalising beat only, no volunteered example; P-04b gets harder to answer honestly) · close 3→2 (held questions go unanswered — say so).

The Shift-menu neighbour exchange is no longer on this list because it has been cut from the design (§Essentials clock). B3's rule could recover 7 minutes; this one recovers 6, and only if you catch it at 0:09. That is the honest cost of restoring the third Radar moment, and it is stated rather than absorbed.

The drill cut is not an ordinary cut. 10→8 is a material deviation under D-0014 §6 and must be written on the facilitator delivery record with the reason. It is placed last on purpose. It is also the one legitimate use of D-0014 in this document: a departure that arose in delivery, not a design-time change to an approved requirement. Even at 8 minutes the drill still exceeds the live 1-hour build's 6.

Never cut, in any circumstance: the 5-minute welcome/consent block · the drill's 8-minute residue · the 11-minute Radar beat · the 8-minute full pass · the 9-minute Form 2 block · the 4-minute form and linkage block.

The honest ceiling, stated. The maximum this rule can recover is 5 minutes, and only if you catch it at 0:09. If you are further behind than the table allows at any checkpoint, the rule cannot save you and you must not improvise: tell the room the session will finish at [time], hold every protected block, and record it. Silently shortening E1, E7 or the forms invalidates the outcome claim and the primary measure at the same time, which is precisely the failure this rule exists to prevent.

Foundations has no cut-order table in this document, and that is deliberate. Foundations is the live 3-hour build repackaged (see the opening section), and the live build carries its own pacing, its own two breaks and its own delivery guidance. Writing a second, competing cut-order rule for a session this document no longer designs would be exactly the kind of unowned duplicate that produced B3's Foundations problem in the first place. The only Foundations-specific pacing instruction here is that the two protected measurement blocks are never cut — the arrival form window and the 10-minute Form 2 block at the close.

B5 · The n=1, small-room and silent-room variants

Essentials is sold to teams of 1–20, and three beats use pairs. Every one has a stated alternative, given by default and not on request.

Beat Pair version Solo / silent-room version
K-E2 explain-back Say it to one person Write the sentence; read it to the facilitator if you want to
E1 shape check Two questions, yes/no Check your own against the two questions printed on the slip
E7 say-it Next move to a neighbour Next move under your breath — the default when there is nobody next to you, not a fallback

Below 8 participants, the solo column is the plan and the pair column is the option.

B6 · The booking checklist — five things the facilitator must know before arriving

  1. Was Form 1 sent seven days ahead? If no → the 95-minute variant, which adds a 9-minute Form 1 block at the front. This is not a slack reservoir and must never be invoked to absorb an over-run (see §B4).
  2. Have the Form 1 nominations been aggregated into two or three themes, and by when? Deadline: the working day before the session (closing C4 §7 item 11 — B2 gave a minimum-n rule and no deadline). If the response count is under five, do not reveal themes — say so plainly and move on. In Essentials nothing is revealed in the room at all; the themes go to the host in writing.
  3. The host agreement is signed, including the two standing prohibitions: no manager ever asks to see anyone's moment, and non-practice is never treated as a performance issue in a review, a one-to-one, or a joke.
  4. Foundations only: the hazard route is named concretely for that organisation, agreed with the host, before the session. F3 cannot be run without it.
  5. D-0016's six matters and the disclosure placeholder. Until they resolve, this is not deliverable to participants, and the placeholder must not go out unresolved.

B7 · The room that does not behave

Closing C4 §2.3 and §7 item 6. None of this was in B2.

  • The dominator. Named beats where it costs most: 0:52 (what counts as a rep) and, in Foundations, the 1:25 contrast debrief. Standing move: take one contribution, name what was useful in it in one clause, and close with "that's exactly it, thank you — let's keep going." Second attempt in the same beat: "I want to hear that one properly and we've got three minutes — grab me at the end?" Never invite the room to respond to a dominator's contribution.
  • The refuser. "You can step out" is not enough on its own. Standing move: "You don't have to do this one. Sit with it, or write instead — both are fine, and I won't come back to you." Then do not come back to them. Do not ask why, do not check in publicly later.
  • The question that will not wait. Short and factual → answer in one sentence where it lands. Long, personal, or off the arc → "That's a good one and it needs more than thirty seconds. Hold it for the close and I'll take it properly." Then actually take it at 1:18. The close is three minutes for exactly this reason.
  • The room that will not speak. Run §B5's solo column throughout; do not fill the silence by extending the teach beats, which is how the drill and the moment beat get eaten.

B8 · If somebody discloses something distressing — drafted, not approved

Closing C4 §7 item 5. This wording is drafted here so it exists to be reviewed; it is not approved, and it does not satisfy or advance D-0016. It goes to D-0016 Items 1–2, with the clinical-governance input those items require.

Raised-exposure beats, named: 0:52 (E6 — recalling a time something went badly), and in Foundations 2:08 / 2:23 (F1 — a peer takes someone through their own moment) and 2:29 / 2:44 (F3 — workload, safety and leadership raised explicitly). B2 disclosed that these two raise exposure above the current builds and correctly referred them to D-0016; what it did not do was write a line for what the facilitator says when it happens.

Standing sequence: stop the beat you are in · thank them plainly, do not explore, do not interpret, do not ask a follow-up question · name the boundary once, out loud — "that's more than a workshop can hold, and that isn't a failure of anything" · point to the disclosure card · offer to speak at the break or after · do not return to them in front of the room · record it on the delivery record the same day.

Do not continue teaching over it, and do not use it as material.

B3's new 180-minute design is withdrawn in full — its clock, its cut-order table, its added-beat list and its wall-clock columns. The reasoning is in the opening section; the short version is that B3 deleted two entire live teaching blocks without mentioning either, cut a third from 9 minutes to 4, replaced two breaks with one, and left 75 of its 180 minutes with no script — while D-0094 had already decided Foundations is "the intervention unchanged… what changes is the container around it."

Record 1 — D-[reserve] — Essentials delivers Mechanism inside the State Check beat, not as its own phase block

Decision. The 90-minute Essentials format delivers D-0003's Mechanism function and content — the Human Operating System's Driver, Passenger and Engine, and the access idea that state changes what is available to you — inside the State Check beat at 0:31–0:37, rather than as a separate phase block in the five-phase sequence. The content is not removed.

What it changes. D-0003 fixes "the five functional phases" and D-0014 §1 protects "the intended function of each phase." This changes the structure, not the function or the content.

Why the earlier version of this record was wrong. B3 proposed removing the HOS from Essentials altogether and argued that "90 minutes cannot carry the HOS." The live 1-hour build carries it in six minutes, combined with the State Check, at 0:32–0:38: "Driver, Passenger, Engine — three of the six, not all — then too much / workable / too little." B3 asked Hunter to approve deleting an element the shorter live format already delivers, without telling him it did.

What is given up, stated. Mechanism is not a separately paced block, so it gets six minutes shared with State Check rather than the live 3-hour's nine. Nothing in the Essentials instrument measures Mechanism, so this cannot be detected in the data. It is a design judgement.

Scope. Essentials only. Foundations is the live 3-hour build and is unaffected. Requires: Hunter's approval. Recommendation: approve. Confidence: moderate-to-high.

Record 2 — D-[reserve] — D-0005's context-neutral disclaimer is delivered in the opening block

Not a change — a gap being closed, recorded because it was missing from three consecutive drafts. D-0005 approves "an active, stated disclaimer — not silence": that the workshop "does not assume participants have workplace structures, an ongoing host relationship, organisational support, accountability systems, or continuing contact." No [SAY] line in B1, B2 or B3 carried it, in either format, while D-0005 sat in all three authority_ref lists.

It is now in the 0:00 script. And it is the reason B3's F3 is withdrawn (§Part C): a beat requiring a named person to ask, an ongoing host relationship and a pre-agreed organisational hazard route is the direct inverse of the disclaimer D-0005 requires the session to make.

Requires: no approval — this restores an approved requirement. Recorded so the omission is traceable. Confidence: high.

Record 3 — D-[reserve] — where D-0004's explanatory feedback operates in Essentials

Decision. D-0004's explanatory feedback operates in the Application phase as the record requires, delivered one-to-one by the facilitator circulating during the full-pass write at 1:08–1:13 — never publicly, never as scoring, never sorting the room.

What it changes. D-0004 places explanatory feedback "operating in the Application phase, explaining why a participant's articulation does or does not reflect the mechanism as intended — never scoring or grading whether a Mental Rep attempt 'succeeded.'" B3 attached explanatory feedback only to the drill, which sits in Revisiting/Connecting, and then built an Application phase deliberately containing no articulation a facilitator could respond to — "private, silent, written," "no hands-up," and a shape check restricted to format. The protected element had nowhere to operate.

How it is delivered without breaking E7's design. The facilitator walks the room during the silent write and responds only where a participant asks or is visibly stuck, on whether what they have written is a next move made with intention rather than an outcome they are hoping for. No public sorting, no hands-up, nothing collected. P-09 is unaffected.

Requires: Hunter's approval only if he reads this as a change rather than a placement. Recommendation: adopt as a placement. Confidence: moderate.

Record 4 — D-[reserve] — Foundations is the live 3-hour build repackaged, not a new design

Decision. Foundations is workshop-package.html's 3-hour build, content unchanged, with its own two 15-minute breaks, Form 1 at arrival and 10 minutes added at the close for Form 2. Elapsed 3h40; book four hours.

What it changes. Nothing in D-0094, which already says exactly this. It reverses B3, which designed a new 180-minute session that deleted two live teaching blocks, cut a third from 9 minutes to 4, replaced two breaks with one and left 75 minutes unscripted.

Requires: Hunter's yes or no. If he wants B3's new design instead, that needs its own record against D-0094 and roughly 75 minutes of script that does not exist. Recommendation: approve the repackage. Confidence: high.

D4 · The questions only Hunter can answer

Each arrives with a recommendation and a confidence. None of them blocks the session plan — Part B runs as written under every answer. Three of B3's six are now closed by his own decisions of 2026-08-11 and are not repeated.

1. Foundations — the live build repackaged, or B3's new 180-minute design? Recommendation: the repackage. Confidence: high. D-0094 already decided it. The repackage costs nothing, restores two deleted teaching blocks and two breaks, and has a script. The new design needs its own record and ~75 minutes of writing. §D2 Record 4.

2. The reporting floor forbids the thing D-0098 sells. Recommendation: change what is promised, not the floor. Confidence: high. The floor is "no report on a group under 20"; the offer ladder sells Essentials in bands of 1–5 and 6–15, and D-0098 promises "a findings note to the organisation." Every Essentials cohort is below the floor, so no Essentials buyer can ever receive participant data. Options: (a) the small organisation receives a session note plus MFC's pooled cross-cohort findings, never its own group's data — recommended, honest, still valuable; (b) drop the findings note from the offer and reprice; (c) lower the floor, which is not recommended — it is R3's benchmark, matched to People at Work, and it is the thing that makes the consent promise true. This needs to reach D-0098 and the offer ladder, not just this document.

3. Virtual delivery is priced and not designed. Recommendation: withdraw the virtual prices until an online variant exists. Confidence: moderate-to-high. The offer ladder sells Essentials virtual at $300/$650 and Foundations virtual at $1,000/$3,200. Both formats here are in-person only, and a full online variant would have to carry the live build's own online provisions — captions on by default, no registration gate before the privacy notice, 12–25 participants — none of which is designed for the pair beats, the board narrowing or the full-pass sheet. The access argument for virtual is real and it is yours; what is not defensible is selling a format that does not exist.

Confirmed consistent, 2026-08-10 — status: established. D3-delivery-models.md §7/§8 reaches the same conclusion independently, for a different reason (measurement-splitting cost and founder hours, not the online-provisions gap named here) and gives it a decision: live-virtual Essentials and Foundations (D3's V3/V4 — the same formats this question calls "the offer ladder's virtual Essentials/Foundations") are deferred on a demand-pull trigger ("a distributed or no-venue enquiry MFC would otherwise have to refuse"), not built in the near term. This document's recommendation to withdraw the virtual prices until designed and D3's deferral are the same conclusion reached twice. Not covered by either document: D3 §0/§7 separately adds a new build, V5 — the one-hour live digital format — as the one new format supported in the near term. V5 is this document's "60-minute Introduction" (Q7 below), not a virtual variant of Essentials or Foundations, so it does not answer or reopen this question.

4. Room size — the ladder's bands or B3's numbers? Recommendation: adopt the ladder's. Confidence: high. B3 wrote "sold to teams of 1–20, written for 8–20"; the ladder sells 1–5, 6–15, and 16–30 as two sessions of up to 15, and asks the committee to reduce the cap from 20 to 15. The cap of 20 is the committee's own judgement of 20 July, so changing it is changing theirs and the paper should say so.

5. K6 — is the knowing–doing-gap outcome approved? Marked "Proposed — requires Hunter's approval under D-0018" and never approved, while B-06 already measures it and K-E2 is a seven-minute beat. Recommendation: approve. Confidence: high.

6. Is Essentials ever delivered to schools, youth, or public audiences? Recommendation: no, until C-16 and the youth process are reviewed and a safeguarding lead is named. Confidence: high. Note the interaction with D-0098, which places the separate 60-minute Introduction in "schools, keynotes, community rooms" — different product, same unresolved gate.

7. The 60-minute Introduction has no session plan and no light form set. D-0098 says it is "built and tested, sellable now" and carries "light measurement only — not the full instrument." That light set does not exist anywhere. Recommendation: specify it as A-01 plus H-01 plus the referral line, and nothing else — one matched item, one harm item, no linkage, no follow-up. Confidence: moderate. It is the only thing MFC can sell today and it is the least documented.

Superseded in part, 2026-08-10 — status: established, not this document's own finding. D3-delivery-models.md §0 renamed this format V5 (one-hour live digital, sold to both organisations and individuals) and, working from a defect found in review, specified the measurement constant that runs on every MFC format, V5 included as larger than the light set recommended above: A-01 plus the then-test (one repeat of the primary stem at post) plus A-04 matched at baseline, plus H-01, the referral line, and the three-week follow-up — not A-01 + H-01 + referral alone. The reason, per D3 §0 and B5a §6.3/§4.4: a bare A-01 pre/post is not interpretable as evidence (response shift and the taught-denominator bias both run against MFC), and D3 repurposes this exact light set as an evidence engine (D3 §5a), which the original light set was never scoped to carry. B5-forms-build-ready.md already builds the constant in this expanded form (its Form 1/Form 3 A-01, the A-01-THEN then-test on Form 2, and A-04 matched at baseline) — so the build has already moved past this document's Q7 recommendation; only this record had not been updated to say so. D3 §0 itself flags that this amendment to D-0098 and to D2 §2 answer 7 has not yet been formally made — that formal amendment is still outstanding and is a genuine requires Hunter decision item, not resolved by this note.

8. Anonymity at n=1–5. The consent script's "we can't work backwards from the code to you" is not true in a five-person business — the four code facts are jointly near-unique. B4 now carries a small-group variant of the script that does not make the claim (§B 0:00). Recommendation: adopt the variant, and take the underlying question — whether MFC should sell a measured session to a five-person business at all — to Eimear and Debra. Confidence: moderate. F5 also cannot run below six people, so the Foundations 1–5 band delivers less than the ladder implies.

9. The Leaders' Session. D-0090 makes it Offer 2. The consequence is commercial and yours: the offer ladder sells it at $350 as an add-on while the committee paper says a manager-facing session is "deliberately not offered yet" because Black Dog gives one away free. Those two documents contradict each other and both are live. Recommendation: keep it as a paid add-on and correct the committee paper. Confidence: moderate.

Original source: 60-projects/committee-pack-v1/B4-session-plan-approved-draft.md

B5 Forms Build Ready

B5 — The instrument, ready to build

The bar this document is written to: someone could open a form tool tomorrow and build this without asking a question. Every item has its exact wording, its response options, its coding, its routing, and the outcome it serves. Where something cannot be built yet, it is named as a blocker with an owner rather than left as a gap.

Two things govern everything below. The construct is B5a — access under load, when it mattered, could you get to it? And B4 is the session that produces it. Where this document and the 2026-08-10 forms draft differ, this document is the later and the reasoned one, and every difference is listed at §9.

1 · The decision record this instrument owes — drafted, not adopted

This exists because the instrument changes an approved decision record in three places and B5a pointed at a record that had not been written. It is written here.

Reserve the ID at adoption: ruby 90-meta/controlled-automation-v1/portfolio-autonomy-v1/id_reservation_ctl.rb next "D-"

D-[reserve at adoption] — The measurement architecture moves to access under load

Decision. D-0017's approved measurement architecture is amended in three respects, and in no others.

1. The primary outcome changes. D-0017 §2 approved "'at least one reported attempted application,' with an added opportunity-sensitivity item." The primary outcome becomes one matched ordinal item measuring access under load (A-01), with the opportunity item retained as a separate yes/no (A-02). Why: an attempt threshold measures frequency of practice; MFC exists for the knowing–doing gap, and the question that matches it is whether the person could reach what they knew while the moment was happening. Full reasoning: B5a.

2. WHO-5 is out of the first cohort. D-0017 §5 approved "retain WHO-5 as an instrument." Why: it measures how a person is doing — mental health — which K-05 says mental fitness is not; it would reach a participant alone, weeks later, with no approved distress pathway while D-0016 items 1–2 are open; and it carried three contradictory statuses across MFC's own records. Recorded as available to re-add on Eimear Quigley's and Debra Fidler's advice, with the governance D-0017 requires.

3. The follow-up's Radar items change shape. D-0017 §3 required the follow-up to ask "whether any of the three Radar moments arose; whether a Mental Rep was attempted in any of them; general Radar helpfulness." The first two are replaced by A-02 and A-01, which ask about any moment where something could have helped rather than about the nominated ones — because checking whether a participant practised the specific thing they wrote down is compliance-checking and contradicts the same non-shaming principle that makes "naming a tool MFC never taught is a success" correct. D-0017 §3's third limb — general Radar helpfulness, not per-moment — is retained in full as RAD-01.

What is NOT changed. D-0017 §1's three timepoints; §4's separation of facilitator records from participant data; §6's exclusion of a substudy; §7's refusal to adopt an external instrument without a full seven-point assessment. D-0056 Matter 1's extended case-study wave stands.

One further divergence, declared rather than buried. K-07's locked definition says a rep may be caught "before it happens, while it is happening, or afterwards." A-01 scores only "while the moment was happening." This is deliberate — it is the harder question and the whole basis of the ceiling argument — and it means the headline number under-counts practice that K-07 counts as real. It must never be described as measuring reps.

Requires: Hunter's approval. Recommendation: approve. Confidence: moderate-to-high on 1 and 3; high on 2.

2 · Linkage, and how a form actually reaches anyone

2.1 Two keys, on every form

Key 1 — token card. Shuffled, pre-printed, handed out at registration, never tied to a name. Four characters. Participant writes it on every form and keeps the card. Projected (not yet measured) 98 to 100% pre-to-post match rate [estimate, not yet verified].

Key 2 — the code, R3 §1.7, used to recover linkage when the card is gone.

ID Item, exactly as printed Response Stored
L-01 "The code from your card" 4 chars as given
L-02 "What is your mother's first name? If you'd rather use another parent or the person who raised you, use theirs — just use the same person every time." free text first two letters only
L-03 "What day of the month were you born?" (01–31) 2 digits as given
L-04 "What month were you born?" (01–12) 2 digits as given
L-05 "How many older brothers and sisters do you have?" (0 if you're the eldest or an only child; 9 if nine or more) 1 digit as given

L-02 is the fix to the defect the forms draft shipped. That draft printed "the first two letters of your mother's first name" directly under its own rule that "you never ask someone to count letters." R3 §1.3 found letter-extraction items match at 31.5% (Source: R3 §1.3) and whole-fact items at 100% (Source: R3 §1.3): the instability is in the operation, not the fact. So the participant gives the fact and the software does the extraction.

Storage rule, which the forms draft does not have and needs. The name is entered, the first two letters are derived, and the raw name is never written to the dataset. This keeps R3's entropy (~900,000 codes; expected collisions at n=25 ≈ 0.0003) while ensuring MFC never holds a security-question answer.

All five elements appear on every form. Dropping one from a later form breaks the code.

2.2 The matcher — write it before the first cohort, not after

Three deterministic passes (R3 §1.6): 1. Exact match on the full 7-character code. Accept if unique. 2. Match on L-03 + L-04 + L-05 (the 100%-stability numeric core, Source: R3 §1.3, see above). Accept if unique in cohort. 3. Allow exactly one element to differ. Accept if unique.

Anything still ambiguous is left unmatched and counted. Never guessed. The unmatched count is reported beside every longitudinal figure, and matched-versus-unmatched baseline scores are compared and reported every time — R3 §1.5 documents that unmatched respondents are not missing at random, and omitting this comparison is the standard way small evaluations overstate effect.

2.3 How Form 3 actually gets sent — the hole the draft left open

The forms draft removed email entirely and then specified "sent day 21, reminders day 24 and 27." With no email and no identifier, there was no channel. Every durability figure rested on a form that could not be delivered.

Resolved per R3 §8 item 7 — two independent routes, neither joined to any response:

  1. Host-circulated generic link. The host organisation emails the same link to everyone who attended. MFC never learns who opened it.
  2. Optional opt-in slip, handed out at the close, physically separate from every form, on different-coloured paper: "This is only so we can send you the three-week link. It is kept apart from your answers and is never matched to them. You don't have to — [host] is sending the link to everyone anyway." Held in a separate file. Deleted at day 28 when Form 3 closes.

Disclosed: route 1 means the host knows a follow-up went to the group. It does not tell them who responded or what anyone said. Goes to D-0016 item 4 with the protocol.

3 · Form 1 — before the session · ≈5.5 min

Sent by the organisation ~7 days ahead. Anyone who has not done it completes it at the arrival table, as the live 3-hour build already does — not inside the protected in-room block, which is the change B4 makes to the session.

Standing header on every form: "Nothing here is scored and nothing is right or wrong. If anything in this brings something difficult up for you, Lifeline is 13 11 14, any time."

Never · Rarely · Sometimes · Often · Almost always — then, held outside the scale: I didn't know what might help · There wasn't a relevant moment · Not sure Ordinal 1–5. Out-of-scale = not scored, reported in own named cells PRIMARY

It came together each time · It didn't come into my head at the time · It came into my head but I couldn't get to it · It came into my head and I decided not to · Something else · Not sure Nominal Retrieval / enactment split — matched

A-01 carries a two-week window, and this is a correction, not a preference. The forms draft's B-01 had no reference period at all — a respondent supplies their own, and there is no reason two people, or one person twice, supply the same one. R3 §5.3(a): "a 'past 3 months, how often' item is a self-concept question wearing a number." An unanchored item is worse. Fix it now, before fielding, or never — after the first cohort the matched wording is locked and cannot be touched.

A-04 is matched at baseline, which the construct document originally had at follow-up only. Without a baseline there is nothing to compare the retrieval/enactment mix against — and that mix is the second reportable result and arguably the better committee story, because it says which part of the model is working.

Cut from the instrument entirely, at every timepoint: B-03 ("which statement best describes mental fitness") and B-05 ("when is building mental fitness relevant"). Concept-recognition items attached to no outcome in either format. The 2026-08-10 draft cut them from Form 2 only while keeping them on Form 1, which leaves a baseline with nothing to compare to — an incoherence, since the draft's own rule is that these items must be "identical across all timepoints or the comparison is void." Cut everywhere or kept everywhere; cut. Reversible on Eimear's or Debra's say-so.

4 · Form 2 — immediately after, in the room · 9 min Essentials / 10 min Foundations

Protected block. Never shortened to buy content time.

A-01 is NOT asked live on Form 2. There is no elapsed period for a participant to report on minutes after the session. Form 2 carries the then-test only — which is also what the 2026-08-10 draft did, correctly, and what the construct document initially got wrong by specifying A-01 at all three timepoints.

Now that you've done today, think back to how you actually were before today — not how you'd have rated it this morning, but how you'd rate it now, knowing what you know." Then: "Before today, when there was something you knew could help, how often did you remember to use it while the moment was happening?" Same scale as A-01 Ordinal 1–5 Then-test

Corrected 2026-08-17 (Hunter, direct): the colours ARE taught in the room as part of explaining Stop-Shift-Do, not internal-only shorthand as an earlier version of this record claimed. P-08 "How many moments did you write on your Radar?" (0 · 1 · 2 · 3) and "Does at least one of them name both a place and a trigger?" (Yes · No · Not sure) as shown Count + binary E1 — form only
P-09 "Today, did you have a go at running the three steps on a moment of your own — even partly?" Yes · No Binary E7
P-11 "Which of the five does your moment mainly ask for, and why?" Select 1 of 5 + one line Nominal + rubric E8
P-05b Foundations only. "Why that one, for that moment?" Free text Rubric F2
P-12 Foundations only. "Today, did you take someone else through the three steps?" Both roles · One role · No — I worked alone Nominal F1

P-08 is the largest single change to the instrument, and it comes from the construct. The 2026-08-10 draft's P-08 was "Write the one recurring moment you have chosen to work on" — free text, collected, described as "the participant's cue" because the follow-up asked how often that moment arose. The follow-up no longer asks that, so the content has no job. What is left is whether the Radar was built and whether it is well-formed, which is what E1 actually claims.

The consequence is a genuine gain, not a trade. Nothing a participant writes about their own life is collected anywhere in the instrument except the one optional narrative at A-06. That makes the 0:00 consent line "the moments you choose today are yours and they never leave this room with me" literally true, and it removes the highest-identifiability free text from the two forms that every participant completes.

H-01 exists because one Likert option is not harm detection. The construct document claimed A-03's "it made things harder" covered it; it does not — that option is routed away from anyone who reported no opportunity, and it asks only whether the tool made one decision harder. H-01 is unconditional, on every form, and cannot be routed past.

5 · Form 3 — 3–4 weeks · ≈6 min

Sent day 21, reminders day 24 and 27, closes day 28. Completed alone. Order below is the build order and it is load-bearing.

RET-01 is last, and that placement is a governed requirement, not a layout choice. D-0008 approves "one brief retrieval prompt at or near the existing 3–4 week evaluation contact" and requires that "the reinforcement or retrieval prompt may only follow after the relevant evaluation response is complete… The support prompt must not be allowed to influence the outcomes being measured." The 2026-08-10 draft had no unaided-recall item at all — its F-04 asked whether the participant remembered the steps, which is self-report of remembering, not recall. D-0008's protected element had quietly disappeared and nothing in three passes noticed.

F-03 does not appear, and no item may replace it. Founder decision, 2026-08-11. K-07, locked: "the outcome does not determine whether it counts." A completion standard reimports the performance threshold the framework refuses. P-09 is worded to attempt ("had a go… even partly") and is not a completion item. Any future item asking whether all three steps were completed is out.

Also removed from the draft's Form 3: F-01, F-02, F-03 (the counted trio), F-05 (absorbed into A-01), F-06 (absorbed into A-03), F-08 (absorbed into A-05), F-10 (absorbed into A-06), WHO-5.

6 · Extended wave — case-study cohorts only

Authorised by D-0056 Matter 1, which explicitly overrides D-0017 §6. Not a fourth form for everyone. Interval is a per-case-study choice decided and written down before the cohort runs — D-0056's 2026-08-05 correction is that three months was a working example, never a fixed rule. Choosing the interval after the data is in view is how a durability claim gets manufactured.

Items: L-01–L-05 · A-01 · A-02 · A-03 · A-04 · A-05 · RAD-01 · H-01 · A-06 · plus, where the room agreed one, "Is the thing your group agreed still being practised together?" (Yes · Sometimes · No · I don't know) — reported separately from individual practice.

Optional add-on, this cohort only: TYDQ-15. The single external validated instrument, carried once so the fair criticism — that MFC wrote its own exam and marked it — has an answer, without putting ~2 minutes per timepoint on every participant for constructs a 90-minute session cannot move. Licensing is unverified (R3 §5.3(b)) and one email to the corresponding author resolves it. Do not reconstruct the items; obtain the published wording or do not use it.

Binding on every claim from this wave (D-0056 Matter 1a): the case-study organisation receives the full package — fortnightly reminders plus organisation-led check-ins — so the claim is "this programme, one session plus the implementation the organisation ran itself, produced these changes," never "one session produced these changes."

Fixed before any data exists: the response rate is reported in the denominator beside every figure, and the survivorship direction is stated in words — the people who still reply are more likely to be the people it worked for.

7 · The analysis plan — pre-specified, before any data exists

This section exists because leaving it unspecified is the largest researcher-degrees-of-freedom hole a design like this can have. At n≈10 the difference between "proportion at Often or above" and "proportion improving by one category" can be the difference between a null and a headline.

Question Fixed answer
Primary comparison A-01, Form 1 → Form 3, matched respondents only
Primary statistic Proportion of matched respondents shifting up ≥1 category. Not a mean, not a cut-point proportion
Reported alongside, always The full Form 1 and Form 3 distributions, as counts, not percentages
Out-of-scale responses Excluded from the ordinal comparison; reported in their own named cells with counts
Non-responders and unmatched Reported in the denominator statement; matched-vs-unmatched baseline compared and reported
Then-test Reported alongside the real baseline, never instead. If Form 1 ≈ A-01-THEN, no detectable response shift — which removes one objection, not all of them
Secondary A-04's retrieval/enactment mix, Form 1 → Form 3, matched; SJT score change; A-03 distribution; RAD-01
A-04 coding note "It came into my head and I decided not to" is NOT scored as a failure. A deliberate choice not to act is values-based action. Scoring it as non-use inverts K-08's agency lens
Reporting floor No report on a group under 20; no subgroup under 10
Consequence of the floor, stated A single Essentials cohort will almost always be below 20. The primary outcome is therefore pooled across cohorts before any figure is reported. A single cohort receives a session note, not participant data. §8 and B4 §D4

The pre-registered disconfirmers

Written now, so a later null is honest rather than embarrassing.

  1. If the first cohort's baseline A-01 clusters at "Often" or "Almost always," the item has ceilinged, MFC's founding premise is not visible in its own participants, and the construct needs rebuilding, not the analysis rescuing.
  2. If A-01 rises with no corresponding shift in A-04's mix and no shift on the SJT items, that is more consistent with measurement reactivity than with access change, and must be reported as such.

What can move the number without anything having changed

Named because §7 of the construct document ruled out causal attribution without naming the specific alternatives. With no control group and a self-rating measured twice: priming (the baseline item is itself a noticing prompt); demand characteristics (at follow-up, unlike baseline, participants know what MFC wants); response shift (partly addressed by the then-test); regression from a baseline taken at the moment someone elected to attend a workshop; and testing effects from repeated administration.

Precision, stated plainly

A single ordinal item at n≈10 detects only very large shifts. Jackson et al. used 13 items, α = 0.84, n = 487 and still returned P = .68. This design is a case description, not a test, and that is a limitation of MFC's scale, not of the item. No p-value should ever be reported from a single cohort.

Reliability, and the honest gap. A single item has no internal consistency, and the design contains no intervention-free interval in which test–retest could be estimated. The cheapest partial fix is a one-week retest inside cognitive testing, reported as the item's only reliability evidence. Until then, MFC has none.

8 · What may and may not be said

Audience May be told Never
Participant What their cohort reported, in aggregate, once pooled Anything about their own performance. Nothing scored, nothing ranked
The employer Counts, denominators, distributions, barriers, what would help, curated de-identified examples with separate written permission for any verbatim Individual answers · any causal attribution · anything about culture, productivity, absenteeism or attrition · any participant data at all where the group is under 20
Internal Everything, including nulls and non-use, with equal prominence That a positive result proves the mechanism
Funders and committee The above plus explicit limits, the disconfirmers, and the precision statement Anything above the approved claim level — and no level is board-approved

The standard for how a result is written. The numbers below are a hypothetical worked example [illustrative only, not a reported result], showing the required shape, not a real cohort.

Right [estimate, illustrative example not a reported result]: "Of the 18 participants who responded at three weeks, 15 said a moment came up where they knew something might help [estimate]. Before the session, 4 of 18 said they could usually get to it while it was happening; at three weeks, 9 of 18 said so [estimate]. Six people moved up at least one step, one moved down, and 11 did not move. Three people told us it didn't come into their head at the time."

Wrong [estimate, illustrative example]: "The session improved participants' mental fitness by 65%" [estimate].

Note what the right version does. It is a denominatored, concrete, persuasive sentence — the thing the counted ratio was wanted for — built without asking a single participant to tally anything. That is the answer to the reasonable objection that dropping the ratio costs MFC its most persuasive form of statement. It does not.

9 · Every difference from the 2026-08-10 forms draft

Change Why

B5A Measurement Construct

B5a — What MFC is actually measuring

Written after a founder instruction to stop building counting machinery and rebuild the construct from the gap. This document states the construct, the primary item, what it can and cannot detect, and — because it was invited — the three places where I think the instruction is incomplete or where I depart from the standing research recommendation.

1 · The finding that should have been found three passes ago

The correct primary outcome was already in the instrument, mislabelled.

The 2026-08-10 forms draft carries B-01, which it calls "the single most important matched item" and files under "Starting point":

"When there was something you knew could help, how often did you remember to use it while the moment was happening?" Never · Rarely · Sometimes · Often · Almost always [held outside the ordinal scale] I didn't know what might help · There wasn't a relevant moment · Not sure

This is the Drive Measurement Blueprint's PRE-02, already specified as matched baseline-to-follow-up. It is the right item. It was treated as background context while F-01 ÷ F-02 — a counted ratio — was declared the primary outcome and an apparatus was built around it across B1, B2 and B3.

So the correction is not that a new measure has to be invented. It is that the existing one has to be promoted, and the apparatus around it removed.

2 · The construct

K-05: mental health is how you are doing; mental fitness is what you are able to do. K-04: mental fitness is "what you're able to do — think, feel, act and connect in life's everyday moments."

MFC exists for the knowing–doing gap: people know what would help and cannot reach it while the moment is happening. The construct is therefore access under load — when it mattered, could you get to it?

Three things follow, and each of them kills something previously built.

Because the construct is access under load… …this dies
The unit of interest is a moment that mattered, not a practice session Frequency-of-practice measurement. MFC does not exist to increase how often people rehearse
The question is could you reach it, not did you complete the procedure Any completion standard. F-03 is cut and stays cut, under any name
The question is about any difficult moment, not a nominated one Compliance-checking. Asking whether the participant did the specific thing they wrote down is a homework check, and it contradicts the same non-shaming principle that makes "naming a tool MFC never taught is a success" correct

3 · Why the ceiling problem dissolves — and the part of this that is an assumption, not a finding

The received account was wrong. The standing research (R3 §5.3) concluded that the ceiling that produced the ANU null was caused by the absence of a denominator, and prescribed an opportunity-conditional count as the fix. That diagnosis does not survive looking at what the ANU items actually asked.

Jackson et al.'s bespoke 13-item scale asked how often participants enacted UVC-Lite's techniques — behavioural activation, cognitive reframing, sleep hygiene, procrastination, social media use. Baseline endorsement of "at least sometimes" ran 49.1%–83.6%, median 70.8%, and the intervention returned P = .68.

Those are general daily actions that most people already do at some rate. Asked "how often," a reasonable adult says "sometimes." The ceiling is produced by the content and difficulty of the stem, not by the absence of a division sum. A ratio built on top of an easy question inherits the easy question.

A conditioned access item is a much harder question. "When there was something you knew could help, how often did you remember to use it while the moment was happening?" asks about the specific failure MFC's whole existence is premised on. If MFC's premise is true, people answer it honestly low, and the headroom is real.

Stated as the assumption it is. There are no published psychometrics for B-01. That it will not ceiling is a theoretical argument resting on MFC's own premise, not a finding. This is the single most important thing cognitive testing and the first cohort's baseline distribution have to settle, and the disconfirming result should be written down now, before any data exists:

If the first cohort's baseline on the primary item clusters at "Often" or "Almost always," the item has ceilinged, MFC's premise is not visible in its own participants, and the construct needs rebuilding — not the analysis rescuing.

4 · Four further reasons the ratio had to go, which the ceiling argument does not cover

The ceiling argument alone would only demote the ratio. These retire it.

  1. It hands the participant their own failure rate to compute. "Five came up, I did one" is a score of 20%, calculated by the person, at the exact moment D-0008's follow-up is supposed to work as a lapse-and-return door rather than a report card. No feedback protection removes this, because the participant does the arithmetic in their head while answering.
