5.1 A stale number in the pack's own headline

Committee paper §1 stat card and §3 "watch" box: "$8,244... our fee is 53% of it."

The arithmetic does not work with the fee the paper recommends:

  • $4,200 (recommended fee) + $3,844 (wages/super) = $8,044, and 4,200 ÷ 8,044 = 52.2%.
  • $8,244 and 53.4% only reconcile with $4,400 — the superseded at-capacity fee under the old base-plus-per-head structure.

The headline stat card was computed under the old pricing and never updated when the paper changed the recommendation. It is a small number and a large tell: it shows the pack was not read end-to-end after the pricing change. Correct to $8,044 and 52%, and re-read both documents for other survivals of the $4,400 figure.

Other pricing arithmetic checks clean: 11 × $66.10 + $150 = $877.10 ✓; $877 × 1.4 = $1,228 ✓; $4,200 − $1,228 = $2,972 contribution ✓; 21 × $2,972 = $62,412 and 27 × $2,972 = $80,244 ✓. One mislabel: the segment table says $4,200 is "3.4× direct cost". $4,200 ÷ $1,228 = 3.4, but the paper defines direct cost as $877 ($4,200 ÷ $877 = 4.8×). It is 3.4× fully-loaded cost. Relabel.

Part 6 — The hedges

6.1 The central hedge is inadequate — and inadequate in an unusual way

"on the best available reading of the evidence, no delivered Australian programme in this category can say whether anyone actually used what they were taught."

"That last clause is an inference from a documented search, not an audited census of every provider. We state it in that form deliberately, and we would rather be asked about the hedge than caught without it."

The footnote is honourable and the instinct behind it is right. It still fails, for three reasons:

  1. It hedges the wrong axis. "On the best available reading of the evidence" hedges evidential quality. The claim's weakness is scope — MFC searched; it did not audit. The footnote does say this, but the headline hedge does not, and the headline is what gets quoted.
  2. A hedge cannot survive a live counter-example. Black Dog publishes "84% of employees or sole traders report they've used at least one wellbeing strategy from the training" on the page the paper cites for its Black Dog facts. No amount of hedging repairs a universal negative that is false on its face.
  3. "In this category" is doing all the work and is undefined. An undefined category term inside a hedged superlative is a construction that can be defended against any counter-example by redefinition. That is not a hedge; it is unfalsifiability. Even unintentionally, it is the kind of thing a regulator or a hostile reader treats as bad faith.

Replace the negative universal with a positive statement of what was actually done:

We searched for Australian programmes in this space that publish whether participants used what they were taught, and found only single post-course self-report items — nothing that counts opportunities, distinguishes attempt from completion, or follows up over time. We have not audited every provider, and we would welcome a counter-example.

That is stronger, not weaker: it is unfalsifiable-proof, it survives the Black Dog page, and it states the real differentiator, which is rigour of measurement, not existence of measurement.

6.2 Hedged when solid — remove the hedging

  • DGR Item 1, ACNC registration, ABN, GST non-registration. Verified at the Australian Business Register. The paper handles these correctly. Do not let a later draft soften them.
  • s26A commencement, the comply-or-exceed duty, enforcement without proof of harm, $344m, 20 psychosocial inspectors. All verified. These need no hedging and currently carry none. Correct.
  • $14.5bn / $537 / $466; 161% / 12%; $588.5m; FRRR 18 August. All verified. State them flatly.
  • "Measurement motivates a purchase" disclaimer (market §7, committee §7). Correctly and unusually well hedged. It is a genuine unknown, named as one, with a test attached. Keep exactly as is.
  • Market §7 in its entirety. The best-governed writing in the pack. Do not touch it.

6.3 Under-hedged elsewhere

Breaches #4, #5, #9 and #10 (Part 3.2) are all present-tense capability or delivery claims carrying no hedge at all, in a document that hedges carefully elsewhere. The pack's hedging is inconsistent — heavy where MFC is honest about the market, absent where MFC describes itself. That asymmetry is itself a finding: a reviewer will read the careful hedging as evidence of discipline, then find the unhedged self-description, and the first will stop protecting the second.

Part 7 — What must change before circulation

Ranked. A items block circulation.

A · Blocking

  1. Rewrite the legal proposition. The code does not require documented control-effectiveness evidence; the real review duty lives in the WHS Regulation, predates 1 July 2026 by ~15 years, and is satisfiable without buying anything. Rewrite committee §1/§5 and market §2/§6 to the wording at Part 1.4. Remove "requires", "legal expectation" and "documented review" as descriptions of the code. Also: never let a sales conversation imply the product discharges a WHS duty (ACL s18).
  2. Correct Black Dog: three programmes, one staff-facing, free, 2 hr face-to-face, 20–25 in the room, up to three private workshops, and NFPs of any size eligible. Redraw the competitive distinction to "the only one at the staff layer measuring whether it got used."
  3. Withdraw the "no delivered Australian programme can say whether anyone used it" claim and replace with the positive search statement at Part 6.1. Black Dog publishes 84%.
  4. Fix the four unhedged self-claims: "We can" → "we are building"; "delivers" → "is designed to produce"; "our differentiator" → "our intended differentiator"; "what we are built to do" → "what we are building".
  5. Restore the "of those who respond" qualifier to the 90–95% three-week linkage figure, and add R3's sentence that response rate is a separate and larger problem.
  6. Resolve the §8.3 / §9.6 contradiction — the paper cannot both say grant language is formally blocked and ask for grant applications to proceed.
  7. Correct the $8,244 / 53% stat card to $8,044 / 52%, and sweep both documents for other survivals of the superseded $4,400 fee.

B · Should change

  1. Reinstate TYDQ-15 as a labelled secondary measure (R3's actual recommendation; ~2 minutes; removes most of the "built your own exam" attack). Add the licensing and item-wording riders.
  2. Soften or source the Smiling Mind and Gotcha4Life negative assertions; put the source on the face of the paper, not "available on request".
  3. Date the 69/111/35 measure counts as a 2015 scoping review, or drop them.
  4. Stop calling the Commonwealth service "non-clinical"; mark the Vistage figure as USD; relabel "3.4× direct cost" as fully-loaded cost; fix "thin margin" on the $2,400 tier; move the March 2026 inspector announcement out of the 1 July narrative.
  5. Add the denominator-inflation risk to the measurement section and to §9's falsifiers — a working intervention can drive the ratio down, and the paper currently treats a flat ratio as disconfirmation.

C · Note

  1. The youth prevalence indicator (26% → 38.8%) is not a like-for-like series; do not present it beside three that are.
  2. Say "$14.5bn on mental-health-related services", and note the per-capita figures are nominal.
  3. Name the "active Australian research group" or drop the sentence — it is uncheckable as written.

Part 8 — What would embarrass the organisation

In order of how quickly it would be found.

  1. Ninety seconds. Anyone opening the Black Dog page the pack cites finds a third, staff-facing, free, face-to-face programme — and a published 84% "used at least one strategy" figure. The pack's competitive claim and its central gap claim both fail on the same page. This is the one that would hurt most, because it is the page MFC itself pointed the reader to.
  2. A WHS adviser in the first buyer meeting. "The code says should, and we've had a review duty in the Regulation since 2011." The opening collapses, and MFC looks like it read commentary rather than the code. Worse if a compliance benefit was implied — that is misleading-conduct territory for a charity selling to small business.
  3. A funder's analyst on the measurement section. An organisation selling measurement rigour that rejected both validated instruments and built its own, with no psychometrics, no norms, no comparability — and whose own research recommended keeping a validated secondary it then dropped.
  4. A named competitor reading the market paper. "Exited the adult market entirely", "government funding fell to zero", "nothing has been published" — three hard negatives about two other charities, none independently sourced on the face of the document.
  5. A regulator or an ACNC-minded board member on §8.3 vs §9.6. The paper documents its own claims block and then schedules the blocked activity.
  6. Anyone with a calculator on the front page. $4,200 + $3,844 ≠ $8,244. It is trivial, and it is the kind of thing that makes a reader re-check everything else.

Part 9 — What is genuinely good, and should not be lost in the correction

Stated because a review that only subtracts produces a worse paper.

  • Market §7 "What we cannot claim" is the best claims-governance writing this vault has produced. It pre-empts three specific overclaims this organisation has previously made and corrects them in public-facing language. Keep verbatim.
  • Refusing to sell the workshop as a psychosocial control is the correct call, made unprompted, against commercial interest.
  • Committee §7's "Established / Not proven" table is the right instrument, and everything in the "Not proven" column is correctly placed. Only the "Established" column needs the legal correction.
  • "We will not be able to say that we caused anything — there is no control group", and the advance commitment to publish disappointing results with equal prominence.
  • The pricing structural argument — that base-plus-per-head pays less for a smaller room while costs stay flat — is correct, well-evidenced against eight published comparators, and the strongest purely commercial reasoning in the pack.
  • Naming the free competitor to the committee before being asked. That is the behaviour that makes the rest of the pack believable, and it is why the Black Dog error is worth fixing properly rather than quietly: the pack gets credit for raising it, and should get the facts right.

Method and limits of this review

Read in full: both HTML papers; K-08; R5; R6; the Managing Psychosocial Hazards at Work code of practice (May 2021, 39pp, extracted and read); the Black Dog NSW programme page and its FAQ (full page text); relevant sections of R1, R2, R3.

Verified at primary or named secondary source: s26A commencement and effect; the $344m package and inspector numbers; the code's review, record-keeping, control-hierarchy and key-terms sections; Black Dog's three programmes, eligibility, delivery modes, group sizes and published outcome figures; AIHW expenditure; Safe Work Australia claims data; the Commonwealth NEIS/Medicare Mental Health Check In funding, launch and service model; FRRR IAGP Round 12 closing date and criteria.

Not verified in this review, and flagged as such above: the four population indicators; the $288,542 NSW claim cost; Smiling Mind and Gotcha4Life financials and programme status; Black Dog's $48.9m revenue; the unnamed Australian research group; the ACNC sector-revenue percentages; Vistage's current fee and speaker-pathway terms.

Not addressed, deliberately: whether fee-for-service delivery raises any issue for MFC's charity tax concessions or stated purpose (R5 correctly defers this to a qualified adviser); anything under D-0016; the constitutional-purpose question at C-18. All three require qualified external input and none is resolved by anything in this review.

Original source: 60-projects/committee-pack-v1/C2-challenge-evidence.md

C3 Challenge Outcome Chain

C3 — Adversarial challenge to B1, the outcome chain

Verdict up front. B1 is the best-constructed product document in this project. Its arithmetic is correct, its claim boundaries are mostly tighter than the builds they replace, and it identifies at least three real defects nobody else caught. It is not yet sound enough to write a session plan on, for one structural reason that runs through most of the findings below: B1 was written against the design-of-record files (01-three-hour-design.md, 02-one-hour-design.md, 12-one-hour-delivery-kit.md) and not against the live build (workshop-package.html), which D-0091 states is what MFC actually runs today. Its own supersedes line names the design files and omits the live build. That single omission produces its headline false claim (§7), its deletion of a decided-and-built beat (§4), and several stale conflict statements.

Findings are numbered C3-nn and graded BLOCK (must resolve before a session plan), MAJOR (must resolve before delivery), MINOR.

1 · Are the outcomes actually observable?

Twelve of the sixteen outcomes are genuinely behavioural. The chain does not break at outcome → behaviour. It breaks at behaviour → item. Most of the named items measure recognition of a taught concept while the outcome above them claims unprompted production. That is the single most consequential defect class in the document, and B1 does not notice it because it checked whether an item exists, not whether the item measures the verb.

The outcomes that fail as written

C3-01 — MAJOR. E2 is an understanding, and B1 says so in its own claim boundary.

"Explains, without MFC vocabulary, why knowing what helps does not produce doing it" …"Understanding is not doing — that is the content of the outcome itself."

Producing a sentence is observable, so this is not fatal — but it is a knowledge outcome (the outcomes spine's K-series), not a skill outcome, and it is presented in a document whose opening sentence promises "what a participant can do." Label it K, not E. More seriously, see C3-04.

C3-02 — MAJOR. E4's primary behaviour is, by construction, unobservable and unfalsifiable.

"Asked in the room, silently, answers for themselves" … "Never shared, never collected, never scored."

Correct under K-08 rule 7 — and it means nothing verifies that half of the outcome ever happened. The claim boundary nevertheless licenses "participants can use MFC's state language on a real moment of their own." The only item, P-03, asks what "workable" means — a definition. Definition ≠ self-application. Either narrow the licensed claim to "participants can state what workable means, and were given one silent opportunity to apply it", or accept that E4 is a delivered beat, not an evidenced outcome. As written it is the one place in B1 where a claim exceeds its own item.

C3-03 — MAJOR. E5 smuggles an intention back in, forty lines after B1 cut ST-2 for being one.

E5: "a concrete move… that they would use in the moment they chose" / "would actually reach for" §2 cut: "ST-2 — intent to use. Intent is a weak predictor of behaviour and no outcome depends on it."

An outcome does depend on it — E5's own wording. The observable residue is "writes a concrete move in their own words," which is what P-05 measures. Delete "would actually reach for" or restore ST-2; do not do both. This is exactly the kind of contradiction §9b's producer/checker loop exists to catch.

C3-04 — BLOCK. Three outcomes claim unprompted production and are measured by forced-choice recognition.

Outcome (verb) Named item What the item actually does
E2 — "explains… using none of MFC's words" B-06 — "which explanation best fits" Selects from options MFC wrote, in MFC's framing. It cannot detect whether the participant needed MFC's vocabulary — the item supplies it.
E3 — "states what each step means, unprompted, without the colours" — "answering red, amber, green is a fail" P-02 — "which response best shows the three steps in order" Recognition of a correct sequence. No item in the instrument can register the failure mode E3 was written to catch. A participant who thinks Stop = red will still pass P-02.
E6 — "states what counts as a rep, including one that went badly" P-04 — "which example best represents a rep" Recognition. The outcome-independence half (a rep that went badly) is exercised by "one or two volunteered aloud" and measured by nothing.

E3 is the serious one. D-0054 exists to stop the traffic light teaching the wrong model fluently; B1 restates that correctly in teaching and then hands the verification job to an item that is blind to it. A one-line free-text at post — "What does amber mean?" — closes it and costs 15 seconds. That B1 proposes nine new items and not this one is a real miss.

C3-05 — MAJOR. F2's stated justification for the half-day is measured by nothing.

F2 exists because Essentials "cannot produce a felt contrast," and the felt contrast is what buys 19 of the extra 90 minutes. The outcome requires the participant to "point to something they noticed" — and the item, P-05b ("why that one, for that moment?"), measures reasoning about fit, which a participant could produce from the toolkit teaching alone without ever having run the contrast. The single most expensive activity in Foundations has no item that distinguishes a room that ran it from a room that didn't. B1's own §3 table lists "F2 — matched, not just named" as solved by P-05b. It isn't.

C3-06 — MINOR. L4 and L5 are prohibitions, not outcomes, and B1 says so. Correct. But listing them in an outcome table and then flagging "no item" as a defect (§3 row 3) mis-frames them: a prohibition's control is a facilitator sign-off, which B1 proposes. That row is resolved, not open.

What is genuinely well-built

E1, E7, F1 and F3 are properly observable, properly bounded, and each has an item that measures the verb. F3 is the strongest single construction in the document — enabling condition → control test → named person → sentence → F-12 asks whether the person actually asked. That is a real behavioural chain and it should survive whatever else changes.

2 · Does the time budget survive a real room?

The arithmetic is correct. I checked every row.

Essentials: 4+4+6+7+5+8+6+8+6+6+10+8+2+2+8 = 90. Clock times are internally consistent (0:00 → 1:30). Protected form time 12 min = 13.3% ✓.

Foundations: 4+4+14+6+7+5+8+8+6+8+6 = 76 (→1:16, break) then 10+15+6+12+10+21+15+4+3+8 = 104 → 180. Every clock boundary reconciles. Protected 12 min = 6.7% ✓.

The 90-minute difference reconciliation is also correct: self-elicitation 14 + peer 21 (=F1 35), contrast 15 + toolkit delta 4 (=F2 19), HOS 8 + enabling 15 (=F3 23), five skills 6 (=F4), plus moment +2, full pass +2, cue/close +3 = 90. No unassigned minutes. Credit where due — this is the first document in this project whose stated totals survive being added up on first pass.

So the clocks are honest as clocks. They are not honest as a room. Four specific problems:

C3-07 — BLOCK. The welcome/safeguarding block is 4 minutes. Both existing builds refuse to go below 5, in writing, as a stated floor.

The 1-hour build: "Scope, consent, disclosure — delivered in full, not compressed… all six of D-0015's universal minimum controls, the non-clinical scope statement, and the D-0016 disclosure statement with its visible placeholder. Brevity is never a legitimate reason to shorten safeguarding text. This block is the same length it would be in a 3-day programme." — 5 minutes. The 3-hour splits it: welcome/scope/consent 6 + disclosure 3 = 9 minutes.

B1 gives 4, and folds the D-0016 disclosure and placeholder into the same block. This is a 20% cut to the one block both prior designs declared non-compressible, made without argument, and it is the only safeguarding-load-bearing number in the document. Nothing else in this review is more straightforwardly wrong.

C3-08 — BLOCK. The retrieval drill is 8 minutes — below the 60-minute format's own protected floor.

D-0004 names the drill the one mandatory retrieval element. The 3-hour gives 15. The 1-hour gives 10 and states: "the single largest allocation in the format, deliberately: everything else compresses, this does not… at full 3-hour intensity in compressed time" — and its own guide says "there is no recoverable padding anywhere in this design."

B1's 90-minute session gives the mandatory element less time than the 60-minute session does, runs Sets A and B alternating in it, and does not mention that it has done so. Under D-0018, drill intensity is a Decision-2 essential function; reducing it is not a Stage-10 flexible-element change. Either restore 10 minutes or record it as a named D-0014 deviation with a reason. Right now it is neither.

C3-09 — BLOCK. The two beats the entire measurement architecture depends on are stacked in the last 20 minutes, and there is no cut-order rule.

E1 (10 min) and E7 (8 min) run 1:00–1:18. Everything the instrument's primary outcome needs — the cue (P-08), the frequency (P-10), the in-room pass (P-09), and the F-01/F-02/F-03 denominator itself — is produced in those 18 minutes, at the point of a 90-minute session where attention is lowest and accumulated over-run is highest.

The 3-hour design anticipated exactly this and wrote a control for it: "the Mechanism phase is the most narratively satisfying block to deliver and the most likely to over-run; when it does, Application is what gets cut live, which silently inverts the design's priorities. The guide carries a visible clock discipline and a named 'if you are behind at 2:15, cut this, not that' instruction."

B1 has no such instruction, and its design is more fragile than the 3-hour's, not less, because 90 minutes has no break to absorb slippage and because a single over-running question in E2 or the drill lands directly on E1. A facilitator six minutes behind at 1:00 will shorten the countability test and the full pass — the two beats that cannot be shortened without invalidating the outcome claim and the primary measure simultaneously.

C3-10 — MAJOR. Individually underbudgeted beats, in order of exposure.

  • 0:04–0:08, four minutes, "token cards issued, Form 1 catch-up." Two tasks. Issuing shuffled token cards to up to 15 people and explaining that the code must be written on every form is 2–3 minutes on its own. The forms draft puts Form 1 at ≈5 min. B1's own honest note concedes the ≈5 doesn't fit and resolves it by sending Form 1 ahead — but the 4 minutes still has to cover issuance plus catch-up for whoever didn't. The 3-hour build allocated 3 minutes for a 2-item pre-measure and said explicitly that this "allows for arrival, instruction and completion at a realistic pace." B1 allocates 4 for card issuance plus a 5-minute form.
  • E1, 10 minutes, and this is a regression against a fixed review finding. Finding SIT03 of the Audience Intelligence review found the silent Radar block was "the most likely point of quiet, undetectable non-completion" and was FIXED by splitting it into two supported halves with a modelled worked example between them and scripted responses to the two named stuck points. B1 lists the stuck points under "what must be taught" and then allocates no time to them: 3 min board + 4 min write + 3 min pair test leaves zero for the scripted way through "my moment is too big." The fix has been silently un-fixed, and §2's cut table removes "the worked example between the Radar halves" on the reasoning that "there are no longer two Radar halves" — which is true and is not a reason the stuck points stopped happening.
  • E7, 8 minutes. 2 min model + 4 min to write four lines + 2 min hands-up. Four lines in four minutes is achievable for a fluent writer at minute 74 of 90 and is not achievable for the "low-bandwidth adult" persona the review panel deliberately included. There is no stated minimum-viable version ("if you only get two lines, write the moment and the next move").
  • E2, 7 minutes, is the hardest four minutes of facilitation in the session — a causal account of the knowing–doing gap, delivered from a participant's own named moment, with no brain science permitted — and B1 supplies no script for it. Real rooms ask a question here. There is no buffer.
  • No arrival, settling or over-run allowance anywhere. The clock starts at 0:00 with everyone seated. In practice the 90 minutes is 82.

Judgement: 90 minutes is honest as an accounting document and optimistic as a delivery document. The margin was consumed by adding two new beats (E2, E7 = 15 min) without removing 15 minutes of risk. It survives contact with a compliant, punctual, verbal room of eight. It does not survive a room that arrives late, a group that will not speak, or one long question — and the beats it sacrifices in those cases are the ones the entire outcome chain rests on.

3 · The format difference

Is Essentials a real product?

Yes — and it is a better product than the 1-hour build it supersedes. It replaces a tour with a practice: one moment, one self-worded tool, one complete pass, one cue. The 1-hour's own honest bar was "understanding the distinction, able to recall Stop–Shift–Do, holding one moment and one next move. Not: sustained independent practice." B1 clears that bar and adds a rehearsed full pass. It also keeps the right boundary: no contrast activity, therefore no claim of what the long format claims. That is the correct line and B1 holds it.

But it buys its new outcomes from governed content, not from padding, and that is the honest criticism:

  • it removes the five public skills, which are one of the six approved essential-content items (see C3-12);
  • it cuts D-0004's mandatory drill below the 60-minute format's floor (C3-08);
  • it cuts the safeguarding block below both builds' stated floor (C3-07).

Restore those three and Essentials is 97 minutes, not 90. That, not 90, is the honest number, and it is worth putting to Hunter as a product question: sell 90 and cut governed content, or sell 100 and don't.

Is the half-day padded?

Mostly not — but the "three outcomes clear the bar" rule is applied more loosely than it reads.

C3-11 — MAJOR. F1's cost is inflated by charging it a beat that exists for a different reason, and the neat 83+7=90 reconciliation depends on that charge.

B1 assigns the 14-minute self-elicitation to F1 as "what makes the room safe enough for it." The 3-hour build states a different purpose entirely: it is the generation-effect opener, and it is non-cuttable "because it is why the definition needs no heavy definitional scaffolding later." Nothing in any record supports self-elicitation as a precondition for pair work, and B1 supplies no source. Strip that reattribution and F1 costs 21 minutes, not 35, the reconciliation lands at 76+7, and 14 minutes of Foundations are unattached to any outcome — which is exactly the state B1 says it has eliminated. The claim "every minute of the difference is attached to a named outcome" is true only because one beat was reassigned to an outcome it does not serve.

C3-12 — MINOR but revealing. F3 requires content B1 cut from Essentials for having no outcome.

The rule stated is "a beat survives if an outcome depends on it." The Human Operating System was cut because "no outcome depends on the six components." F3 was then written to depend on two of them. The reasoning is circular; the result is defensible product design. Say that, rather than presenting the cut as though the rule generated it. (Note also: the outcome traceability matrix names the HOS as one of the deliberately excluded items — so reintroducing any of it to Foundations is a Stage 7 scope addition, not a survival.)

Otherwise the half-day is not padded. F1 at 21 minutes is right; two turns and a debrief is the minimum honest version. F3 at 23 is right and its hazard-routing half is not optional. The one thing that could compress is F2, and only because its outcome is unmeasurable (C3-05).

One presentational honesty point (C3-13, MINOR): "half day" = 180 content + 15 break + arrival = 3h15 elapsed minimum. B1's own header says so; the offerings ladder should too, before a host books a room for three hours.

4 · The cuts

Does cutting the five public skills from Essentials breach K-07's staged arc?

No — and that is not the question that matters. Read carefully, K-07's staged teaching arc puts the five public skill labels in the deliberately held back column at Stage 1 and introduces them at Stage 2. Cutting them from a Stage-1-shaped session is the arc applied literally. B1's framing of this as a K-08-versus-D-0091 conflict is correct as far as it goes.

But B1 has already answered its own founder question 2 without noticing, and answered it the other way. K-07 Stage 1 holds back three things: the five public skills, State Check's full nuance, and the Shift menu's four options ("one is enough to start"). B1's Essentials teaches State Check in full (E4) and the whole four-item Shift menu (E5) — both Stage 2 content — and cuts only the skills. There is no principle in the document that selects those three differently. So:

  • if Essentials is Stage 1, E4 and E5 breach the arc too, and the cut list is one item long when it should be three;
  • if Essentials is a D-0091 collapsed standalone — which it plainly is, being the only contact this audience gets — then the five skills belong in it, on exactly the reasoning D-0091 gives.

C3-14 — BLOCK. Founder question 2 is real, but B1 must present it accurately: the document has already taken the collapsed-standalone position for two of the three held-back items and the Stage-1 position for the third, and asks Hunter to ratify the inconsistency rather than the choice.

Does anything cut breach a decision record or a claim?

Yes. Three things, and B1 catches none of them.

C3-15 — BLOCK. The five public skills are one of the six approved essential-content items, and D-0003 requires all six to be introduced in the session.

02-outcomes-spine/02-outcome-traceability-matrix.md, verbatim: "All six essential-content items (public definition; short distinction; five public skills; Stop–Shift–Do + mental rep; State Check; Radar concept) serve at least one listed outcome." D-0003, in "what is fixed provisionally": "All six essential-content items are first introduced within the session." Cutting them also drops approved Stage 7 outcome K3 — "can distinguish the five public skills as the workshop-facing architecture" — which no longer traces to any beat in Essentials.

Per D-0018: "a change to an 'essential function' requires a new decision record" and "essential-element changes require Hunter's approval." This is not a K-08-versus-D-0091 wording conflict. It is the removal of an approved essential-content item and an approved outcome, by assertion, in a candidate document. That is the exact class of silent essential-function change D-0018 exists to prevent, and which 03-measurement-and-behaviour-tracking.md explicitly refused to make when it faced the same temptation over the follow-up interval.

C3-16 — MAJOR. Reducing three Radar moments to one changes D-0010's approved structure for both formats, on the same authority basis.

D-0010's approved requirement is verbatim "three meaningful moments → one possible next move for each." The 1-hour build reduced it to one and recorded it as a named D-0014 deviation with a stated reason — the correct mechanism. B1 makes it the standard for both formats and describes the consequence accurately ("makes the 1-hour's named deviation the standard rather than the exception") without doing what the 1-hour did: recording it as a deviation. It needs the same treatment, or a decision record.

Related, and more interesting: D-0010 also states the Radar is "a personal map, not a three-part compliance task" and that participants are not required to "meet a frequency target." B1's E1 requires the chosen moment to recur at least twice a week and makes that a scripted pair test. That is a frequency criterion applied at selection — imposed not because it helps the participant but because F-01 needs a denominator. See C3-24.

C3-17 — BLOCK. Cutting "My moments / Our moments as taught structure" deletes a beat that D-0091 decided, built, and states is live today.

B1's §2 cuts Our moments on the reasoning that "nothing in the offer supports or follows up that step (D-0090 §2). The workshop produced an intention and stopped." That reasoning was superseded five days before B1 was written. D-0091 §2 redesigned Team Pulse onto MFC's actual three-form shape: private nomination on Form 1, facilitator aggregation before the session, anonymous aggregate reveal in the room at 3:04, the room asked (not assumed) whether there is appetite for one shared "when X, we will Y" commitment, reviewed through D-0056's existing case-study cadence. D-0091 §2a states plainly: "What's actually built and live, right now… It's in workshop-package.html today."

B1's escalation flag compounds this: it says the unbounded version "is exactly what D-0090 §1 recommended reopening and escalated to Hunter, undecided." Half of that is stale — the compressed version was decided and implemented by D-0091; only the full source mechanism remains deferred. B1 removes a live, decided beat, removes the Form 1 item that feeds it, removes the facilitator prep step it requires, and reports all of this as "not pre-empting" a decision that has already been made.

F3 is a better beat than the one it replaces — narrower, more checkable, with a follow-up item. That is an argument for a decision record superseding D-0091 §2. It is not a licence to delete it in a cut table.

C3-18 — MAJOR. The Leaders' Session is the leader-modelling component D-0090 decided must not be retrofitted into Offer 1.

D-0090 Proposal 2, verbatim: "this is an Offer 2 requirement and must not be retrofitted into Offer 1. A standalone workshop has no leader relationship to work with, and pretending otherwise would be the exact individual-responsibility framing K-07's own binding constraints prohibit." B1's L1–L5 is precisely a leader-modelling component attached to a standalone Foundations Session, and B1 does not cite D-0090 anywhere in it.

Worse, its evidential move repeats one D-0090 already had to correct. L2's rationale — "Norms shift when network-central people visibly adopt something" — is unsourced, and D-0090 records that the study previously cited for exactly this claim (Mas & Moretti) "was a misuse… the mechanism is behavioural spillover under observation, not observational learning from a model, and the line-of-sight direction runs opposite to what leader modelling requires." The Leaders' Session may well be the right product. It cannot be built on the sentence D-0090 struck.

C3-19 — MINOR. The remaining cuts are sound. The six-component HOS, the pair-share on wall themes, the worked example, the analogy bank, Engine Basics, the caveat pair, ST-1/ST-2/ST-3 and Form 3 Q8 all survive scrutiny. Engine Basics specifically: K-07 positions it as "named, respected, referenced when relevant — never expanded," so a take-home line is exactly compliant. Cutting the second Radar strand from the counted spine while keeping it offered is the right call and B1's reasoning for it (cutting it entirely "would reframe mental fitness as damage control") is the best single paragraph in §2.

One thing cut that no record requires but the room does

C3-20 — MAJOR. Essentials has no opt-out for pair work, and it now contains two pair activities.

E1's countability test is "done in pairs and out loud"; E2's explain-back is "Turn to one person." K-08 rule 6 prohibits forcing partner work; D-0015 control 2 requires that an alternative to any public disclosure exists. Foundations' F1 states this properly — "opting out of pairs is stated as normal before pairs are formed, and a solo written alternative is offered by default, not on request." Essentials states it nowhere, and Essentials is the format B1 also points at schools and public talks. The omission is almost certainly an oversight; it is still the kind that reaches a participant.

5 · The nine new items

Item by item

Item Measures its outcome? Answerable honestly? Uncounted burden
P-09 in-room full pass Yes — and the wording match to F-02/F-03 is genuinely good design Partly. It is asked ~90 seconds after the facilitator ran a public hands-up on the same question. Anyone who raised a hand answers consistently with the room, not with themselves ~30 s
P-10 weekly frequency No — it is a prediction, not a frequency, about a moment chosen eight minutes earlier. It cannot validate countability; it records a guess And the session taught the target answer. E1's pair test drills "would it come up twice in a week?" The item then asks for a number. This is a leading item manufactured by the design ~30 s
P-11 five skills Yes, trivially — asked minutes after teaching, near ceiling Yes ~45 s
P-12 peer roles Yes, cleanly Yes ~20 s
P-05b why that one Measures reasoning about fit, not the felt contrast it is credited with (C3-05) Yes ~45 s
F-11 used with another person Yes No denominator. Unlike F-01 it cannot distinguish "didn't" from "no occasion" beyond one crude option — reintroducing the exact conflation this instrument was rebuilt to defeat ~60 s (free text)
F-12 did you ask Yes — the best new item in the set Yes, and it is falsifiable ~60 s (free text)
L-01/L-02 moment, sentence Yes Yes 2 free-text writes
L-03/L-04 at 3 weeks Yes Yes — but see C3-23 a fifth instrument

C3-21 — BLOCK. P-10 is a leading item, and its lineage is the one this vault already wrote a lesson about. L-032 records a leading survey-question option found in August, root-caused to a bias check that ran once and was never re-applied after revision. P-10 is the same failure created fresh: the session establishes "twice a week" as the criterion for a good moment, and the instrument then asks the participant to state their frequency. Under-frequent choosers will round up. The countability problem P-10 exists to solve is real; the fix is a facilitator-side check at E1, or a frequency item on Form 1 about a moment the session has not yet shaped — not a post item.

C3-22 — MAJOR. The burden arithmetic is not in the document, and it does not net out.

B1's §5 claims "every burden figure is arithmetic on the forms draft's own estimates." There is no burden arithmetic anywhere in B1. Running it against the forms draft's own numbers:

  • Form 2 today: B-03…B-06 + P-01…P-08 = 12 items ≈ 8 min → ~40 s/item.
  • Essentials: +P-09, +P-10, −B-03, −B-05 = 12 items. Neutral. 8 minutes holds. ✓
  • Foundations: +P-09, +P-10, +P-11, +P-12, +P-05b, −B-03, −B-05 = 15 items ≈ 10 min. B1 budgets 8 in both clocks and reports "12 minutes protected" for both formats. Two minutes short, and the total is therefore 182, not 180.
  • Form 3: 10 items ≈ 6 min, +F-11 and +F-12, both carrying free-text "what happened?" → ≈ 7.5–8 min, a ~25% increase on the instrument whose response rate carries every durability claim MFC will make. B1 counts none of this and proposes no offsetting cut at follow-up.

The proposed cut of B-03 and B-05 is sound on its own merits, but it is spent twice — once to fund Essentials' two items and again, implicitly, to fund Foundations' five.

C3-23 — MAJOR. The leaders' instrument is a fifth form nobody has designed, and with one leader it cannot be anonymous.

The clock says "0:43–0:45 leaders' form, four items" — but only L-01 and L-02 are end-of-session items; L-03 and L-04 are at three weeks. So (a) the clock is wrong, two items not four, and (b) L-03/L-04 require a separate leaders' three-week instrument that does not exist in an architecture the forms draft states is "three forms, every participant, every pathway" plus a case-study wave.

B1 correctly identifies that reporting floors make single-organisation leader data unreportable. It misses the sharper problem: with one to three leaders, the self-generated linkage code provides no anonymity at all. MFC will know exactly who wrote L-01's moment and L-02's sentence. The privacy, consent and linkage protocol B1 itself names as the overdue blocker has no provision for a respondent group of one, and this is the first thing in the pack that would fail that protocol on sight.

6 · The counted-ratio conflict — is it real?

It is reconcilable. B1's reconciliation is right in substance and wrong in provenance, and it escalates the wrong item.

The case that there is no conflict, put properly

B1 presents the opportunity-conditional design as "the reconciliation this document assumes… this system's reading, not your ruling." That is too modest, and it is factually wrong about the authority. The structure is already approved. D-0017, decided under Hunter's delegated authority, approved:

"F2's Option A+C initial-use threshold: 'at least one reported attempted application,' with an added opportunity-sensitivity item, avoiding the failure/no-opportunity conflation F2 explicitly flags."

and extended the follow-up to ask

"whether any of the three Radar moments arose; whether a Mental Rep was attempted in any of them; general Radar helpfulness (not per-moment)."

That is F-01 and F-02 in binary form, standing and approved. 03-measurement-and-behaviour-tracking records the same thing in its own item table: "Radar item: did any chosen moment arise; did you attempt it." Opportunity-conditioning is therefore not a new proposal requiring founder ratification. It is the approved architecture, and the "don't count reps" instruction was given by Hunter with that architecture already in force — which is itself strong evidence he did not read one as excluding the other.

His objection has a precise, documented referent: Form 3 Q8, "approximately how many Mental Reps did you do in the past 14 days?" — an unbounded, uncued, self-tallied volume count over a fortnight, with no denominator, that rewards a busy life and penalises a quiet one. Everything in Hunter's stated preference points the same way: "did you use this in moments and you felt a benefit from" and "do you now feel more equipped to handle" rather than "how many reps did you do."

The case that the conflict is real, put properly

Three things survive that defence.

  1. D-0017 approved presence; the forms draft asks for cardinality. "Did any moment arise" is not "how many times, 0–20+." F-02 is, structurally, a count of reps in a window — bounded by a denominator, but still a tally the participant computes from memory. B1's claim that the ratio "does not tally practice volume" is half true: the ratio prevents volume being read as the outcome; it does not stop volume being asked for. Moving from binary to cardinal is a change to an approved measurement architecture and needs the same decision record D-0018 demands elsewhere.

  2. The ratio does not remove performance pressure. It relocates it, and arguably worsens it, in one specific respect B1 has not seen. A bare rep count has no denominator: "3 reps" is just 3. The ratio hands the participant a personal denominator and makes them compute their own failure rate in the act of answering — "five came up, I did one." No comparison to anyone else is needed for that to land as a score. It is self-administered, unavoidable, and it happens at the exact moment D-0008's follow-up is supposed to function as a lapse-and-return door rather than a check-up. B1's protection — "never fed back to the participant, and cannot rank anyone" — is real, and it is already guaranteed by the forms draft ("Anything about their own performance. Nothing scored, nothing ranked"). It does not touch this.

  3. F-03 is the item that actually breaches the framework, and B1 does not isolate it. K-07's locked Mental Rep definition: "The outcome does not determine whether it counts." F-02 is attempt-based and fully compatible. F-03 — "in how many did you get all the way through" — is a completion standard, i.e. an outcome grading, applied to a unit whose locked definition says outcome is irrelevant. And E7 rehearses it publicly: "Hands up if you got all the way through. Hands up if you got partway." Naming both as normal helps; it is still a room being sorted into completers and partial-completers on a construct that is defined as not having that property.

Verdict

Reconcilable, and the founder question as B1 poses it is too broad and wrongly targeted.

  • Opportunity-conditioning: not in conflict, and not a founder question. D-0017 approved it. Cite D-0017 and stop asking.
  • Cardinal counts (F-01/F-02): a real, narrow change to an approved architecture. Either revert to D-0017's binary + a bounded band ("did it come up: not at all / once or twice / most days"), which preserves the whole ratio logic without asking anyone to tally, or write the decision record. The band version defeats the ceiling problem identically and cannot be described as counting reps by anyone, including a sceptical committee member.
  • F-03: this is the item to put to Hunter, alone, with the K-07 outcome-independence quotation beside it. It is one line, and it is the only place the instrument genuinely contradicts a locked record.
  • C3-24 — MAJOR: the instrument is now shaping the intervention, and that is the deeper version of this conflict. E1 requires a moment recurring twice weekly so that F-01 has a denominator. D-0010 says participants select moments that are "personally meaningful to them" and are not required to meet a frequency target. B1's own framing concedes the direction of travel: "Every outcome below is written so that measure can detect it. Anything in the existing build that does not serve it has to justify itself on its own." That is measurement setting product policy. A participant whose most important moment is a monthly performance review is now told, in a scripted pair exercise, that it is the wrong shape. That is a worse outcome than an uninterpretable F-01.

Finally: B1 blocks too much on this. "No session plan should be written before it is answered, because E1, E6 and E7 are all shaped by it." E6 (what counts as a rep) and E7 (running one pass) are K-07 content and stand whatever the answer is. Only E1's countability test and F-03's in-room analogue change. Blocking the whole session plan on a question that moves two beats is the kind of over-escalation §6a exists to prevent.

7 · The biggest claim in the file — verified

"E7 (the in-room full pass) is new. The existing builds contain a live State Check, a Radar write and a cue selection, but no beat in either format has a participant run all three steps on their own moment… the same gap for the full sequence was never caught." "This is currently the largest measurement hole in the build: the session's central activity has no item."

C3-25 — BLOCK. The claim is half true, and the false half is the load-bearing half.

True of the 3-hour build. I read its full beat table. Its Application phase runs Radar (both layers) → worked example → Our moments → cue selection → non-requirement → second live State Check → close. No beat has a participant run Stop → State Check → Shift → Do on their own material. And the 3-hour's own outcomes spine claims exactly that: outcome 3, "Run one rep — catch one moment and choose one next move with intention — at least once." That is a genuine, serious, correctly identified defect and B1 deserves credit for it.

False of the 1-hour, as currently built. workshop-package.html — which D-0091 §2a states is what MFC runs "today" — contains, at 0:38–0:41, marked New, a beat titled "Do one, right now":

"The whole room runs one rep together, live: a ten-second State Check on how you actually are right now, then one Shift — the simplest one, a breath or a change of posture — chosen and done in the room, not described." … "New against the standing 1-hour design, which only drilled the words. A talking session that never has the room actually do a rep isn't finishing on experience — it's finishing on a recap."

It carries its own rationale (Baldwin & Ford transfer-of-training; Bandura mastery experience, both added 2026-08-05) and the build's own traceability table maps it to an outcome and an item:

"Run one rep — caught a moment, tried a next move … ✓✓ … Q7 (yes/no) — 0:38–0:41 is built specifically to make this true by the time the form is sent."

So: a live-rep beat exists in a current build, was added deliberately five days before B1 was written, and is mapped to an existing item. "Exists in NEITHER current build and is measured by NO item" is wrong on both halves.

What survives, and it is still worth having. The package's live rep is (a) a State Check plus one Shift, not all three steps, and (b) run on "how you actually are right now", not on the participant's own chosen Radar moment — which comes afterwards, at 0:41. So E7's precise claim, all three steps on their own chosen moment, is genuinely unmet in both builds, and running it on their own material is a real upgrade over running it generically. State it that way. The difference between "this beat does not exist" and "this beat exists in one format, generically, and should be run on the participant's own moment in both" is the difference between a discovery and an improvement — and only one of those framings survives Hunter checking the live build.

And the gap was partly caught. B1 says it "was never caught." The Audience Intelligence review's own unresolved-unknowns list, item 5: "Whether outcome 3 (run one rep) occurs at all post-session — currently measured only at follow-up, and a participant may use it once and not recall it." The review saw the measurement half and deferred it as an unvalidatable hypothesis rather than fixing it. That is a weaker defence than "never caught," and it is more accurate.

Root cause, and it is the most important line in this review. B1's supersedes field names 01-three-hour-design.md and 12-one-hour-delivery-kit.md. It does not name workshop-package.html. B1 reviewed the design-of-record documents and not the live build. That single omission produces C3-25 (E7), C3-17 (Our moments / Team Pulse deleted), the stale D-0090 escalation flag, and the missing Form 1 nomination item. Before anything else in this document is acted on, B1 should be re-run against the live build.

8 · What is still missing before a facilitator could write a session plan

In order of blocking severity.

  1. A cut-order rule. "If you are behind at 1:00, cut this, not that." The 3-hour has one; B1's more fragile design has none (C3-09).
  2. A script for the beats that carry the new outcomes. E2's causal account and E7's modelled pass are the two hardest pieces of facilitation in Essentials and both are described, not written. The existing kits carry [SAY] blocks; this recut carries none.
  3. Opt-out language for Essentials' pair work (C3-20), and a solo variant — B1 sells Essentials to "teams of 1–15," and E1, E2 and F1 all break at n=1. There is no one-participant version of a pair activity.
  4. Participant materials. The moment slip, the four-line full-pass sheet, the token card, the take-home card carrying the Engine Basics line. None exists for this recut; all are referenced.
  5. The leaders' three-week instrument as an actual form, with an anonymity answer for a respondent group of one to three (C3-23).
  6. The Form 1 nomination item and the facilitator aggregation step that D-0091 requires and B1 silently drops (C3-17) — either restored, or explicitly superseded in a decision record.
  7. The extended case-study wave. D-0056 approved it and 03-measurement calls it "the only point that can carry the case-study claim." B1's chain stops at three weeks. F-11, F-12 and L-04 all need a stated position on whether they repeat at the extended wave, and the forms draft's wave list currently does not include them.
  8. A mapping of every beat to D-0003's five phases. Both existing builds publish this; B1 publishes neither the mapping nor a note that it changed. On its face Foundations inverts the fixed order — the HOS (Mechanism) runs at 0:40–0:48, before Stop–Shift–Do (Skills) at 0:48–0:56, where both prior builds run Skills first. D-0003 fixes the sequence; D-0018 says changing it needs a decision record. It may be a defensible change. It is currently an undeclared one.
  9. A booking-time checklist. B1 creates four host-side preconditions — Form 1 sent seven days ahead, the hazard route agreed with the host beforehand, whether the Leaders' Session ran, and which Essentials variant (90 or 94 minutes) is being delivered — and no artefact captures them. The facilitator must know all four before arriving; B1 says so, and provides no vehicle.
  10. Distress-likelihood reassessment. E6 asks participants to recall "a time this week you caught something and it still went badly"; F3 raises workload and psychosocial hazards explicitly. Both raise disclosure probability above the current builds, and D-0016 items 1–2 are open. B1 notes D-0016 generally; it does not assess whether its own new beats increase exposure to it.
  11. The schools problem, unflagged. Format 1's second line: "Also used for schools, public talks and keynotes." K-08's control-state warnings, C-16: youth/schools "Blocked until youth process reviewed"; external use "No until reviewed"; mandatory-reporting detail needed; no named safeguarding lead (BD-05, pending). Naming a school audience in the first sentence of a format description, in a committee pack, with no reference to C-16, is the kind of line that reads as authorised once it is in a document.

Summary of gradings

BLOCK (7): C3-04 recognition items for production outcomes · C3-07 safeguarding block below the stated floor · C3-08 drill below D-0004's protected floor · C3-09 no cut-order rule with both measurement-critical beats stacked last · C3-14/C3-15 five public skills are an approved essential-content item and outcome K3 · C3-17 deletes a D-0091 decided-and-built beat · C3-21 P-10 is a leading item · C3-25 the E7 claim is false against the live build.

MAJOR (11): C3-01, C3-02, C3-03, C3-05, C3-10, C3-11, C3-16, C3-18, C3-20, C3-22, C3-23, C3-24.

What should not be changed: the outcome-chain format itself; E1, E7, F1 and F3 as constructions; F-12; the second-Radar-strand compromise; the "items with no outcome" analysis; the refusal to build an organisational measure; and the arithmetic discipline, which is the best in this project.

Original source: 60-projects/committee-pack-v1/C3-challenge-outcome-chain.md

C4 Challenge Rebuilt Plan

C4 — Adversarial challenge to B2

Verdict up front. B2 is materially better than B1. It opened the live build, it fixed most of what C3 found, and Part B is the first artefact in this project that reads like a thing a person could stand up and deliver. It is still not runnable tomorrow, and the reasons are not stylistic. Three of them are mechanical: the cut-order rule cannot function at its own checkpoint, the primary in-room item contradicts the pass the facilitator is scripted to authorise ninety seconds earlier, and the opening safeguarding promise is falsified by the form handed out at the end of the same session.

And the headline claim needs qualifying. B2's frontmatter says it was "built against workshop-package.html — the live build… This is the file B1 did not open." B2 did open it: the 0:38–0:41 details it quotes are all verifiably in the file. But on the two numbers where B2 leans hardest on the live build to justify a change, it repeats C3's figures rather than the build's (§1.3 below). B1 failed for not opening the file. B2 opened it and did not finish reading it.

1 · The seven BLOCKs, one at a time

C3's summary lists eight IDs across seven numbered BLOCK findings. B2's crosswalk table also mis-grades C3-04 as MAJOR; C3 grades it BLOCK and counts it in the BLOCK set. The substance is resolved anyway, but a document whose central claim is "every BLOCK resolved" should not restate one of them at a lower grade.

1.1 C3-04 — recognition items for production outcomes · RESOLVED

P-01b, P-02b, P-04b are added, each aimed at the exact failure mode C3 named. C3-04's specific prescription was "a one-line free-text at post — 'What does amber mean?'"; B2's P-02b is "What does Shift mean? Don't use the colours." — the same item, better worded, because it also refuses the colour vocabulary the outcome is written to exclude. P-04b measures the outcome-independence half that C3 found measured by nothing. This one is fully closed.

1.2 C3-07 — safeguarding block below the floor · RESOLVED for Essentials, one unargued minute lost in Foundations

Verified directly: workshop-package.html's 1-hour clock runs "0:00 – 0:05 · Welcome, scope, how today works — non-clinical scope, six consent controls delivered in full — not skipped for time." B2's 5 minutes matches the live floor exactly, states it as a floor in the clock table, repeats it in the beat heading, and puts it first on the never-cut list. Correct, and correctly evidenced.

Foundations gets 8. The live 3-hour gives the same material 9 (welcome/scope/consent 6 + disclosure 3, per C3-07's own quotation of it). B2 labels its 8 "Floor 5 + 3" — a construction it invented — and never mentions that the format this replaces gave 9. That is a one-minute unargued reduction to the one block both builds declare non-compressible: C3-07's defect at smaller scale, reintroduced in the long format while being fixed in the short one.

1.3 C3-08 — drill below D-0004's floor · REMEDY RESOLVED, JUSTIFICATION FALSE

B2 gives the drill 10 minutes in both formats, names it a floor, and never-cuts it. As a remedy that is right.

The justification is not. B2 states twice — in the E3 row and in the clock — that "the live 60-minute build gives it 10 and calls it the single largest allocation in the format." The live 60-minute build gives it 6:

0:26 – 0:32 · Drill it — full pace, both sets · 8 → 6 min "Tightened from the first cut, but still the largest single practice block of the hour."

The "10 minutes" and the "single largest allocation" quotation come from 12-one-hour-delivery-kit.md via C3-08 — a design-of-record file, which is precisely the class of source C3 said B1 failed by relying on. B2 has carried a design-of-record number into a document whose entire claim to authority is that it checked those numbers against the live build.

A second, undeclared reduction rides on this. The live 3-hour gives the drill 15 minutes. Foundations gives 10. D-0014 §1 names "Decision 2's explanatory feedback and recall-based retrieval" an essential function that "may not be removed, contradicted, or materially weakened." A third off the protected element, in a format of identical length, is not remarked on anywhere.

1.4 C3-09 — no cut-order rule · NOT RESOLVED. This is the most serious finding in this review.

§B4 exists, is well written, and does not work. It instructs:

"Check the clock at 0:52. If the 'what counts as a rep' beat has not started by 0:52, you are behind, and you cut in this order."

Now place the five cuts on the clock B2 itself published:

Order Cut Runs at Available at 0:52?
1 Five public skills illustration 0:20–0:25 No — 27 min in the past
2 Four ordinary moments 0:09–0:13 No — 39 min in the past
3 Shift-menu neighbour exchange 0:47–0:52 No — just finished
4 What counts as a rep 0:52–0:56 Yes — recovers 1 min
5 Close 1:19–1:21 Yes — recovers 1 min

At its own checkpoint, three of the five cuts have already happened and the rule recovers two minutes. A facilitator six minutes behind at 0:52 — C3-09's exact scenario — follows the rule precisely and is still four minutes over, standing in front of the never-cut list.

The fallback compounds it: "If you are more than five minutes behind at 0:52, you are running the 95-minute variant — tell the room, and finish at 1:35." But the 95-minute variant is defined in §B6 as the Form-1-was-not-sent variant, which adds a 9-minute Form 1 block at the front. It is a longer session for an unrelated reason, not a slack reservoir, and invoking it at 0:52 does not create the five minutes; it just relabels an over-run the room did not agree to.

Foundations is worse. §"What does not change" says the rule is "the same list, checked at 2:09 instead of 0:52, with the contrast beat (15 min) inserted at position 1." The contrast beat runs 1:23–1:38 — 31 minutes before the checkpoint.

The fix is not a rewrite of the rule; it is a rewrite of the checkpoints. A working version needs checks before each cuttable beat (0:20, 0:47, 0:52), each stating the decision at the moment it can still be taken.

1.5 C3-14/C3-15 — the five public skills · RESOLVED

E8 is a genuine restoration, not a relabelling. The five are taught in K-07's locked wording as a named 5-minute beat in both formats (0:20–0:25 Essentials, 1:00–1:05 Foundations), with a [SAY] block carrying all five verbatim, a reference card, an outcome, and an item (P-11). Approved Stage 7 outcome K3 traces to a beat again. D-0003's "all six essential-content items are first introduced within the session" is satisfied for this item, and C3-14's inconsistency charge dissolves — B2 now takes the collapsed-standalone position for all three of K-07 Stage 1's held-back items (skills, State Check, full Shift menu) rather than two of three.

The K-08-versus-K-07/D-0091 conflict is named in §D5 and resolved toward the governing record with its reason, not silently chosen. Correct handling.

One residual, unnoticed. D-0003's six essential-content items include the Radar concept. Essentials uses K-07's Radar prompt verbatim and has participants write one moment — but the word "Radar," and the concept of a Radar as a thing a person has, appear nowhere in Part B's script. The sixth item may be introduced in function and not in name. That needs one line, or an explicit note that naming is not required.

1.6 C3-17 — Our moments / Team Pulse · PARTLY RESOLVED, and the Essentials half misattributes its authority

Foundations is fully fixed. F5 restores D-0091's beat as built: 6 minutes, anonymous aggregate reveal, the room asked not assumed, "when X, we will Y," an owner named, declining protected as a successful outcome, no participant item by design, and the day-10–14 reminder correctly labelled "drafted but not wired into the send infrastructure — do not describe it as running." The Form 1 nomination item and the facilitator aggregation step are both restored. This is the best-executed resolution in B2.

Essentials is not what B2 says it is. B2 claims its 2-minute in-room anonymous theme reveal is "exactly the treatment D-0091 §'The 1-hour format' already approves, carried as a named D-0014 deviation." Read the source. D-0091 gives the short format collection and host handover only:

"It keeps its existing, already-correct decision to decline working Our moments live… the same Form 1 nomination question is still collected… and the facilitator can hand the host organisation what people privately said they'd want to work on together."

And the live build's own change list, item 08, is unambiguous — "Form 1 nomination question — collected, not worked live here… What changes: Nothing in the one-hour room."

So B2 has added a new in-room beat to the short format and attributed it to an existing approval that says the opposite. It costs 2 minutes of a 90-minute clock that has no slack, it makes pre-session aggregation a hard dependency of the short format (it was optional there), and it is exactly the species of error C3 was written to catch: a claim of record support the record does not give. Either drop the reveal and hand the themes to the host as D-0091 provides, or write the decision record that extends it.

1.7 C3-21 — P-10 is a leading item · DEFECT RESOLVED, REPLACEMENT UNFIELDABLE

P-10 is cut, the "twice a week" criterion is removed from the teaching and from the pair check, and "Do not ask how often it comes up" is written into the beat. D-0010's no-frequency-target position is restored. The leading-item defect is genuinely gone.

B-07 cannot be fielded as written. "In a typical week, how often do you face situations like these? Not at all / once or twice / most days." On Form 1, seven days before the session, there is no antecedent for "these." The participant has not chosen a moment, has not seen the four ordinary moments, has not met MFC's vocabulary. As drafted the item has no referent.

And it does not do P-10's job. P-10 asked about the moment this participant chose; B-07 asks about an unspecified generic class, which cannot contextualise F-01, an item about the participant's own moment. B2's crosswalk says countability "moves to a facilitator-side shape check in the room plus B-07." But the shape check is explicitly restricted to place-and-trigger and explicitly forbidden from asking frequency. Countability is checked by nothing. That is probably the right answer under D-0010 — but it should be stated as an abandonment, not presented as a relocation.

1.8 C3-25 — the E7 claim · RESOLVED, and verified line by line

Every detail B2 asserts about the live build is in the file: the beat title "Do one, right now", its 0:38–0:41 slot, its New marker, Baldwin & Ford and Bandura added 2026-08-05, and the traceability row "Q7 (yes/no) — 0:38–0:41 is built specifically to make this true by the time the form is sent." B2 states the correction in the crosswalk, in the E7 heading, and in the body, in the terms C3 asked for — improvement, not discovery; all three steps and the participant's own moment as the two specific deltas; the 3-hour's genuine absence preserved. This is honest work.

Tally

Finding Status
C3-04 recognition items Resolved (mis-graded MAJOR in B2's own table)
C3-07 safeguarding floor Resolved for Essentials; 1 unargued minute lost in Foundations
C3-08 drill floor Remedy resolved; justification false against the live build; 5 min lost in Foundations undeclared
C3-09 cut-order rule NOT RESOLVED — the rule cannot function at its own checkpoint
C3-14/C3-15 five skills Resolved
C3-17 Our moments Foundations resolved; Essentials misattributes its authority
C3-21 P-10 leading Defect resolved; replacement item unfieldable as worded
