D1 Premise Resolutions

D1 — The three premise resolutions

What this is. C5-premise-audit.md §11 ranked three premises as most likely to be wrong. This document closes all three in one place. P1 was decided by Hunter directly and is written up here as decided, not re-argued. P2 and P3 were open, and are decided here.

What this is not. It does not restate the Ledger and Obverse findings — those live in D1-review-findings.md and stand. It does not reopen pricing, which D2-pricing-and-nine-answers.md governs.

A note on the file history, because the record should be honest about itself. The three source resolutions (D1-who-actually-pays.md, D1-environment-layer.md, D1-what-measurement-is-for.md) and D2 were believed lost when two earlier sessions were interrupted. They were not lost — they are intact in commit 79b2f9b and were recovered verbatim rather than reconstructed from memory. Everything below is sourced from those recovered files, not from a paraphrase of them.

1 · P1 — Who pays. Decided by the founder, 10 August. Closed.

The premise C5 challenged

That the employer is the buyer. C5 §1 ranked this first: "the person who needs this is not the person who buys it" — and it argued a funder-primary model resolved acquisition cost, the Black Dog free-competitor problem, and P2's environment gap simultaneously. The pre-decision draft (D1-who-actually-pays.md §1) recommended exactly that: the funder pays and the organisation pays nothing for year one.

What was decided instead

Hunter decided this directly on 10 August, after the reviews ran and before the funder-primary recommendation was acted on. In his own framing: "the half day workshop is our main source of revenue... employers/corporates fund access for others — which is hard."

Decided. 1. Corporates and businesses are the main revenue source. Not funders. 2. The half-day Foundations workshop is the main revenue product. Essentials is reach and evidence, not a revenue line. 3. Community organisations pay, at a reduced tier that still clears its loaded cost. 4. Pro bono is by application, on named offerings only (the Introduction and Essentials), never blanket, and never Foundations. 5. Corporate margin cross-subsidises access, shown as an explicit named levy rather than left implicit — D2 §1b-i.

The recommendation in D1-who-actually-pays.md §1 is withdrawn and superseded by this. That file is retained because its research, its confidentiality architecture and its funder-route analysis remain live; only its §1 recommendation lapsed.

Why this is a founder decision and not a system one, stated plainly

It meets D-0049 protected condition 6 on its face — it is a judgement about what MFC is, not only about which revenue arrives faster. A funder-primary charity and a trading charity that funds access from margin are different organisations. The system's recommendation was the other one. Hunter's call supersedes it, and the honest record is that the analysis and the decision disagreed, not that the analysis anticipated him.

What survives from the challenge, because it was never really about which option won

Four of C5 §1's findings bind regardless of who pays, and they are carried into the live documents:

  1. Acquisition cost is real and unfunded either way. One person cannot run 105–168 qualified conversations a year on top of delivering. The answer is series engagements, not more prospecting — three to four clients rather than twenty-one sales. Committee paper §3.
  2. The Black Dog free competitor is not answered by price. It is answered by what MFC measures and by the segment Black Dog does not reach (R6, R7).
  3. The reporting floor is a hard constraint on what any buyer receives — no participant data below 20, and every Essentials band is below it. D2 §2 answer 2.
  4. SEDI ineligibility until $50,000 of trading revenue exists now argues for the founder's decision rather than against it. Obverse's finding 11 said a free-only year forecloses SEDI; a corporate-primary year opens it. This is the one place the founder's decision is better supported by the evidence than the system's recommendation was, and it should be said.

The falsifier, kept live

If ten conversations with local businesses produce no close at the corrected Essentials prices, and no corporate Foundations sale lands by the March review, the buyer premise has failed empirically and the funder route in committee paper §6 becomes primary. R7's honest warning stands: an absence of competitors can mean the market does not work, not that it is unserved. Cost of the test: a fortnight.

2 · P2 — The client commitment. Decided: the claim is withdrawn, and the smaller true thing is made real.

The instruction

C5 §2: the client commitment is "written, not priced" — unpriced, unenforced, unmeasured, unstaffed. "An unpriced, unenforced, unmeasured, unstaffed commitment is a document, not a layer." It is the sentence that lets the pack acknowledge the graveyard evidence and proceed unchanged. Either make it real, or withdraw the claim that MFC has an environment layer.

The decision: both, in that order.

The sentence "this is the environment layer we can actually deliver" is withdrawn. MFC does not have an environment layer. It has delivery preconditions, and from this decision, a measure of whether they held.

C5's four tests, answered honestly:

Requirement Met? How
Priced Met differently Not in money. It is a signed condition of delivery — a schedule to the services agreement. MFC does not deliver without it. The price is paid in refusal, the only currency a one-facilitator charity holds
Enforced Met minimally, and stated as small No penalty, no clause with teeth. The consequence is: reported at contracting level, and no second cohort into that organisation until the commitment is renegotiated in writing
Measured Met properly — this is the substantive change Two Form 3 items, ~30 seconds of instrument time. Enactment reported split by the answers
Staffed Not met, and this is why the claim is withdrawn rather than restated The facilitator leaves. The only party who remains is the manager layer, and D-0090 Proposal 2 prohibits retrofitting a leader requirement onto a standalone session

The fourth row decides it. In the transfer literature MFC cites, an environment layer is a standing feature of the setting — not a promise made before a visitor arrives. MFC cannot staff that at one facilitator.

The three named obligations that replace the three-clause sentence

Each written so a person can tell whether it happened. Full text: D1-environment-layer.md §3.

  • A — attendance is genuinely voluntary, and demonstrably so. No one directed to attend, a named alternative use of the time exists, non-attendance recorded against nobody. Detected by: Form 1 asks whether the participant chose or was told. First, because obligation C is coercive if stacked on conscription (K-08 safety rule 4).
  • B — one named real opportunity, named before delivery. One specific foreseeable occasion in the next three weeks — a handover, a difficult client call, a particular meeting. Not a category, an occasion. Written into the schedule, read aloud in the room. Detected by: Form 3. Obverse said keep this one if only one survives.
  • C — one named manager asks once, and records nothing. "Was there anything from the session you wanted to use?" — not "did you use it." Nothing recorded, nothing passed to MFC. Detected by: Form 3 asks whether they were asked, never what was said.

Obligation C is deliberately weaker than what it replaces, and the reason is a founder catch on the record. C5 §10.3: a manager arranged to ask about skill use is "close to the compliance-checking he has already rejected once, relocated from the form into the workplace." B5a retired exactly that check from the instrument; it must not reappear in the workplace under another name.

Scope, per D-0090 Proposal 2: obligations B and C bind series engagements only. A standalone session carries voluntary attendance and the named occasion; the leaders' briefing is offered, not required; and the paper must say the environment condition is weaker there.

What actually binds in the modal engagement, stated plainly because the modal year-one engagement is standalone, not a series. At zero delivered sessions and with an acquisition problem D1-review-findings already names, "MFC refuses to deliver without the signed commitment" is a threat MFC cannot yet credibly make — refusing the first buyer who declines a clause is refusing the only revenue MFC has. The rhetoric of refusal is replaced here with what is actually checkable: for the modal (standalone) engagement, only obligation A (voluntary attendance, demonstrably so) and obligation B (one named occasion) bind — both cost the buyer nothing and neither requires a series relationship to enforce. Obligation C requires a manager who persists past one session and does not bind a standalone booking. The pre-committed answer to the first real case where a buyer declines the signed schedule: MFC delivers anyway, records in the file that the schedule was declined, and reports that engagement, honestly, as one without a measured precondition — it is not withheld from the split reporting, it is reported as the arm without obligation coverage. This is the checkable commitment; "refusal" is not, until MFC has enough volume that refusing one buyer is not existential.

The measurement

F3-E1. Before the session, your organisation named one specific situation where you might use this. In the last three weeks, did that situation actually happen? Yes / No / I was not told what it was / Not sure

F3-E2. In the last three weeks, did anyone above you ask whether there was anything from the session you wanted to use? Yes / No / Not sure

Reporting, on an honest clock. Split reporting is subject to R3's floors — N ≥ 20 overall, N ≥ 10 per arm. With cohorts capped at 15–20, no first cohort can report the split, and MFC must say so rather than publish an under-floor breakdown. It becomes reportable across pooled cohorts, realistically in 2027. The items are laid down now because data not collected in cohort one cannot be recovered in cohort four.

And the limit MFC applies to everyone else's evidence applies here. Organisations that name an occasion and follow through are systematically different organisations. Any difference is a signal worth investigating, confounded by organisational self-selection — not evidence the precondition caused anything. K-08 does not license the causal reading, and this is the same shape as the cross-sectional error the vault has already been burned by.

It cuts both ways, which is why it is worth doing. Higher enactment where B and C happened is MFC's first signal that preconditions matter, and it is directly fundable. No difference weakens MFC's own environment argument by MFC's own instrument — and must be published with the same prominence.

What the committee paper now says

Client commitment · A condition of delivery, signed before the session · Three named obligations, two measured at follow-up. This is not an environment layer. MFC cannot supply one — the facilitator leaves. What MFC can do is make the preconditions explicit, refuse to deliver without them, and measure whether they held. MFC is shipping an individual-content product with the environment as a measured variable rather than a delivered layer, and is betting that measuring it honestly is worth more than claiming it.

Obverse called the withdrawal "the most honest page in the pack" and said not to soften it under committee pressure. That instruction is carried here.

One thing C5 asked that is not closed here, disclosed

C5 §2 listed four delivery vehicles never assessed — delivery into a group that already meets, cue placement in the environment, manager-delivered micro-practice, and asynchronous delivery. Withdrawing the environment-layer claim does not answer them. They are generated and tested in D3-delivery-models.md, which is where that question now lives.

3 · P3 — Measurement. Decided: a research programme that a product carries.

The conflation

C5 §3: MFC's measurement is "priced as a feature, argued as a research asset, and described in §5 as 'our differentiator' — a business claim." Three readings, mutually constraining, never separated.

The separation, with who pays for each

Product feature Research programme Business
What it is A written findings report inside the fee An instrument, a protocol, cohorts, publication Recurring revenue from measurement itself
Who pays The corporate buyer, inside the Foundations fee A funder or a research partner — Perpetual IPAP's outcomes pillar, PRF's evaluation stream, a university group Someone who buys evidence rather than sessions
Success is Buyers choose MFC because of it A validated instrument, a published result including nulls, sector credibility A different company
Costs ~4 of 11 facilitator hours per session A partner, a protocol, ethics, years Capital, staff, a comparator base
MFC today Unproven and contested Already true, and unnamed until now Not available

Decided

MFC's measurement is a research programme that a product carries. It is not a product feature, and it is not a business.

  • Business — rejected. It needs an instrument someone else accepts, a comparator base, and an organisation that runs measurement independently of delivery. MFC has none of the three, cannot build them from ~$12,000 with one person, and the door that would buy it is verified shut: icare's $5.4m is an establishment partnership, and SafeWork NSW's $5.6m is already committed to Black Dog and Transitioning Well. Re-entry condition: one published cohort result. Not before.
  • Product feature — demoted, not deleted. "Our differentiator" becomes "our intended differentiator, and the first thing we are testing." Present tense for something unbuilt, undelivered and unvalidated was C2 breach #9, never applied until now. No dollar value is claimed for the report — the old "$1,700 of the fee" was arithmetic from a withdrawn flat price, not evidence of what a buyer pays (D2 §1d).
  • Research programme — adopted, named, and made the thing that is fundable.

Why the research reading is not a consolation prize. Every attribute that makes the measurement commercially weak makes it fundable:

Attribute As a product feature As a research programme
Instrument unvalidated Fatal (C2 §4.2(6)) Normal — it is what the programme is for
Zero delivered cohorts Fatal to credibility The reason to fund a first site
Committed in advance to publishing nulls Commercially punished The strongest integrity signal available to a funder
Claims discipline refusing causal language Weakens the pitch C5 §9.2 — "a genuine asset with funders and researchers"
B5a's circularity — the instrument's validity depends on the thesis it tests An unmanaged risk A pre-registered question with a named falsifier

B5a's circularity finding is the sharpest edge and should be escalated, not buried. If MFC's own participants do not report a knowing–doing gap at baseline, the market thesis failed, not the instrument. A funder can be told that in those words. A buyer cannot.

The reading absent from the whole pack, assessed directly

C5 §3 stated it and nothing in the pack engaged with it: the party who values the evidence is the party who pays for it. Assessed here, because the brief asks for an assessment and not an endorsement.

Where it is right, and it is right about something important. It correctly identifies that MFC has been charging the party with the least interest in the evidence for the most expensive part of producing it. A corporate buyer of a half day wants a competent session and a defensible reason to have run it; it does not want a validated instrument, and no Australian employer survey ranks evaluation as a purchase criterion. Meanwhile funders, research partners and eventually insurers want precisely that and are structurally set up to pay for it. On that half, the reading is correct and it is adopted:

The corporate buyer pays for the workshop and receives the session note or, at Foundations 16–20, the findings report. It is not asked to fund instrument validation, publication, ethics or a research protocol. Those are funded from research and philanthropic money, or not done. This is exactly consistent with the founder's cross-subsidy decision: corporates fund delivery; research money funds the evidence programme.

Where it is wrong, and this is why it does not become the strategy. C5 pushed it further — "and delivery to the employer becomes cheap or free," inverting the business model. That inversion is rejected, on three grounds:

  1. It is the funder-primary model under another name, and the founder decided against it. Free delivery to employers with a funder paying is precisely what D1-who-actually-pays.md §1 recommended and Hunter overturned on 10 August.
  2. It forecloses SEDI — up to $120,000 for evaluation capability specifically, the largest realistic grant in R4, unlocked only by $50,000 of trading revenue. A model that makes delivery free by design can never reach that threshold. The reading that claims to fund the research is the one that shuts the largest research-capability grant.
  3. It puts the evidence programme on money MFC does not have and cannot date. Perpetual reopens "~October" and its reopening "hasn't been announced"; PRF's round dates are NOT FOUND in R4's own register; the research partnership "costs an email" that has still never been sent. Building the delivery model on that is building it on an undated maybe.

So the reading is adopted as a funding-attribution rule and rejected as a business model. That is a narrower conclusion than C5 implied, and it is the one the evidence supports.

The gate this identity creates — and it was missing entirely

R3 §3.8: publishing results as research triggers NHMRC National Statement / HREC review, which cannot be obtained retrospectively for data already collected, and it changes the consent wording. A research-programme identity is built on an advance commitment to publish, so it triggers exactly that, before the first form is completed.

This is a second D-0016-shaped gate — external approval on the critical path, un-retrofittable — with the difference that this one is being created by MFC's own choice rather than inherited.

  • Route: a research partner supplies the ethics pathway. One email, still unsent (R1 Route 6, R3's licensing rider).
  • Named alternative if no partner is found: state in writing that the first cohorts are internal evaluation only, and describe the identity to funders as evaluation capability rather than research. That forecloses the thing that makes it fundable, and the trade must be made knowingly.
  • Standing rule, from Obverse finding 4: no grant application is submitted until the safeguarding gate has an owner and a target date. Grants carry fixed delivery windows; D-0016 has no date, and accepting restricted funds against it risks returning money to MFC's first funders.

Two things the founder's later input, 10 August, adds to this premise

His instruction on delivery models — "we've got a pre-form and a post-form, and we still check in... but we have different offerings" — strengthens P3's resolution rather than complicating it.

  1. It makes the measurement the invariant and the format the variable. That is precisely what a research programme carried by a product looks like from the inside: the protocol is constant, the delivery vehicle is what varies. It is the clearest statement in the record that the evidence base, not the workshop, is the thing being protected.
  2. It creates a real risk P3 must name. More formats means the same instrument run across materially different delivery conditions. Pooled across formats, a null is uninterpretable; split by format, no arm clears the N ≥ 20 floor for years. D3 §7 carries this; it is not solved here, and it is the largest measurement cost of the wider ladder.

4 · What each resolution asks of the committee

Decided here, no committee action Needs the committee
P1 The revenue model and the cross-subsidy Ratification of the corrected price list (D2), and the Essentials cap at 15 rather than the committee's own July 20
P2 The withdrawal, the three obligations, the two Form 3 items, the scope limit to series engagements Nothing. It is a product decision — but the paper must not let the withdrawal be softened in the room
P3 The identity, the demotion of "differentiator", the rejection of measurement-as-a-business, the funding-attribution rule Whether MFC is willing to describe itself to funders as a research programme. D-0049 condition 3 — identity. Recommended: yes, conditional on a named research partner secured by 30 September 2026 (proposed — the committee should set the actual date; this gives roughly six weeks from the paper, enough to send the partner email C5/D1 §3 record as still unsent and get a response, not so long that the identity sits unresolved through the FRRR round closing 18 August). It is accurate and fundable — but it is not costless: §3 itself discloses that this identity creates a second D-0016-shaped gate (HREC/ethics review, an unsent partner email, consent wording that must be right upfront). The "costs nothing MFC has" framing is struck as inconsistent with that disclosure. Without a partner secured by that date, the identity defaults to internal-evaluation-only, and the paper must say so rather than claim the research identity is free

Committee item 1, added here because it was absent from every version of this pack until this revision: name a safeguarding lead and approve a budget for D-0016 items 1, 2 and 4 — the three requiring qualified clinical-governance and legal input. 17 August is the one date on which the committee can authorise this. Cost is a few hours of clinical-governance and legal time against ~$12,000 remaining; the highest-value spend available to the committee on that date is closing this gate, not any of the three resolutions above. D-0016 has until now been reasoned from — used to reject V9 and international delivery — without ever being budgeted to close. That asymmetry is fixed here.

And D-0016 gates all three. Nothing above is deliverable to a participant until the six safeguarding matters have a named owner, a cost and a date.

5 · Independent check

Two seats, separately briefed, neither exposed to the other's findings or brief.

  • Seat V — verification reviewer. Every quotation, figure, section reference and attribution checked against C5, D1-review-findings, the three recovered D1- files, D2, B5a, R3, R4 and R7.
  • Seat P — premise auditor. No verification remit. One question per resolution: what would have to be true for this to be right, and is it?

Findings and what changed: D3-delivery-models.md §9 records the same two seats' findings across this document and D3, because both were reviewed in one pass. Per D1-review-findings.md §0, no reviewer's findings are drafted ahead of the reviewer.
